the post caption ### step:review approve before anything goes public everything above is assembled and nothing has been published. check three things, because all three have to be right at once and this is the last point where they are cheap to change: 1. **the caption** — is it what you'd actually say, under 280 characters? 2. **the image** — did `image_url:` come back with a real url, or `none`? 3. **the account** — is `${{args.brand}}` the right brand, on the right platforms? approving here does not publish. publishing is a separate run: iris playbook run freelabel-ads topic="${{args.topic}}" brand=${{args.brand}} action=publish ### step:publish publish the ad

entries.name: freelabel-bounty-ads
entries.describe: Render a branded bounty/promo ad (Remotion SocialPost) and post it to Instagram + X. Turns a preset into a live social post in two commands. Built to drive creators into live UGC bounties, but works for any promo. Pass an action (e.g. "render", "post", "render-and-post", "dry-run", "list").
entries.haystack: freelabel-bounty-ads render a branded bounty/promo ad (remotion socialpost) and post it to instagram + x. turns a preset into a live social post in two commands. built to drive creators into live ugc bounties, but works for any promo. pass an action (e.g. "render", "post", "render-and-post", "dry-run", "list"). --- name: freelabel-bounty-ads description: render a branded bounty/promo ad (remotion socialpost) and post it to instagram + x. turns a preset into a live social post in two commands. built to drive creators into live ugc bounties, but works for any promo. pass an action (e.g. "render", "post", "render-and-post", "dry-run", "list"). allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run freelabel-bounty-ads` # bounty ad — render + post to instagram/x create a branded ad (video + story + still) with remotion and publish it to instagram + x through the existing upload-post integration. built for driving creators/tastemakers into live bounties (ugc rewards), but works for any promo. the whole loop is two steps: **render a preset → post the file.** both are one command. ## arguments `$arguments` — action and parameters. examples: - `/freelabel-bounty-ads render <preset>` — render square video + 9:16 story + still from a preset - `/freelabel-bounty-ads post <file|url> --caption="..."` — host on r2 + post to ig + x - `/freelabel-bounty-ads render-and-post <preset> --caption="..."` — do both - `/freelabel-bounty-ads dry-run <file>` — host on r2, print the cdn url, do not post - `/freelabel-bounty-ads list` — list presets + the live bounties worth advertising --- ## 1. render the ad (remotion) ad content is a preset json in `remotion/presets/*.json`: `{ brand, headline, roles[], eventinfo, ctatext, contacthandle }`. copy an existing `bounty-*.json`, change the values. **important — render via the minimal entry.** the main `remotion/src/root.tsx` has missing carousel imports that break the whole bundle. always render through `src/bounty-index.ts` (registers only the socialpost compositions): requires `remotion/public/social-post-audio.mp3` (drop a licensed music bed; a silent placeholder renders fine — generate with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc -t 15 public/social-post-audio.mp3`). run `npm install` in `remotion/` first if `node_modules` is missing. ## 2. post to instagram + x (`social:post-video`) the `social:post-video` artisan command hosts a local file on cloudflare r2 (`cdn.heyiris.io`) then posts via `uploadpostservice` (per-platform isolation + retries reused). r2 + upload-post keys are **prod-only**, so run with `railway run` to inject them into the local command (which has the rendered file): **always pass `--board=545 --user-id=193`** (the "freelabel creative" board). this auto-registers the creative in review studio as a tracked, reviewable item (pending on host, → approved on successful post) so nothing generated is ever untracked. add `--campaign=<id>` to group it. use `--dry-run --board=545 --user-id=193` to host + register for review without posting. - `--dry-run` hosts + prints the url without posting (always do this first). - route x through **`freelabelnet`** (has x connected). ig-only handles (`@thediscoverpage_`) skip x gracefully. - accepts a public url directly (skips hosting): `social:post-video --user=freelabelnet`. - confirm final status (async worker): `get with header `authorization: apikey $upload_post_api_key`. --- ## live bounties to advertise | bounty | rate | apply link | |--------|------|-----------| | #532 summer vibes clip campaign | $5 / 1k views ($1000 pool) | freelabel.net/marketplace/opportunity/532 | | #523 song wars content team | $0.50 / 1k | freelabel.net/marketplace/opportunity/523 | | #519 artists wanted | $0.10 / 1k | freelabel.net/marketplace/opportunity/519 | **always use the `freelabel.net` domain in ad copy** (brand-facing). it 301-redirects to the live marketplace page with the path preserved — confirmed working. do not use `web.freelabel.net` or `web.heyiris.io` directly in captions. ## key files - `remotion/presets/bounty-*.json` — ad content (copy + edit to make a new ad) - `remotion/src/bountyroot.tsx` + `src/bounty-index.ts` — clean render entry (bypasses broken root.tsx) - `fl-api/app/console/commands/postvideotosocial.php` — the post command - `fl-api/config/uploadpost.php` — brand → social handle routing ## proof it works first real post (2026-07-06): the summer vibes bounty ad went live on ig `instagram.com/reel/dadtuo3jhti` + x `x.com/freelabelnet/status/2074165976648634831`.

entries.name: freelabel-social
entries.describe: Turn a live bounty, opportunity, event or program into FREELABEL-branded social content for X and Instagram. The creator-audience counterpart to howto-social — same render and publish rails, different source and different voice. Money numbers are MAPPED from the record, never written by a model. Pass an opportunity/bounty id, or "list" to see what is live.
entries.haystack: freelabel-social turn a live bounty, opportunity, event or program into freelabel-branded social content for x and instagram. the creator-audience counterpart to howto-social — same render and publish rails, different source and different voice. money numbers are mapped from the record, never written by a model. pass an opportunity/bounty id, or "list" to see what is live. --- name: freelabel-social description: turn a live bounty, opportunity, event or program into freelabel-branded social content for x and instagram. the creator-audience counterpart to howto-social — same render and publish rails, different source and different voice. money numbers are mapped from the record, never written by a model. pass an opportunity/bounty id, or "list" to see what is live. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- # freelabel → social `howto-social` posts iris developer recipes to a developer audience. this is the other half: **freelabel content for creators** — bounties they can earn from, events they can play, programs they can join. same render and publish rails. different source, different voice, and one extra rule that does not apply on the iris side: **the numbers are real money, so they get mapped, never generated.** ## arguments `$arguments` — an opportunity/bounty id, or `list`. - `/freelabel-social 519` — artists wanted — song wars live 2 - `/freelabel-social list` — what is live right now - `/freelabel-social event 41` — event promo ## the rails already exist. audited 2026-08-21. nothing here needs building. know what is already there before adding anything: | rail | command | state | |---|---|---| | brand tokens | `remotion/src/brands.ts` | 9 brands: freelabel, discover, beatbox, emc_radio, capital_collective, noys, creative_gs, vanguard, heyiris | | bounties | `iris bounty list` | live — real budgets and spend | | opportunities | `iris opportunities list/get/pull` | live | | events | `iris events list/get/pull` | live | | programs | `iris programs list/get/pull` | live | | carousel from a record | `iris deliver:carousel --from opportunity:<id>` | exists, **ai-written** | | single promo image | `iris remotion still socialpost…` | exists | | ad with an approval gate | `iris playbook run freelabel-ads` | v2, multi-platform, ownership-enforced | | bounty promo, two commands | `iris playbook run freelabel-bounty-ads` | exists | | publish | `iris x post --brand freelabel --also instagram` | @freelabelnet **connected** | | asset hosting | `iris cloud:upload <file>` | returns a cdn url | `freelabel` and `discover` both post as **@freelabelnet** and both are connected. `heyiris` and `capital_collective` are **disabled**. ## 🔴 the money rule an opportunity record carries `budget_pool_cents`, `budget_remaining_cents`, `budget_spent_cents`, `days_until_deadline`, `application_deadline`, `bounty_type`, `compensation_model` and `applicant_count`. **read those fields. do not let a model phrase them.** `iris deliver:carousel --from opportunity:<id>` and `remotion auto-carousel` write copy with a model. that is fine for a headline and fatal for a rate. a hallucinated `$0.50/1k views` on a post promising creators money is a commitment you did not make, to an audience that will screenshot it. put them on the stats slide verbatim, converted from cents. if a number is missing, **leave the slide off** — an empty stat is better than a confident wrong one. this is the same principle `howto-social` uses for recipe copy, and it matters more here because the downside is financial. ## voice — freelabel is not iris | | iris | freelabel | |---|---|---| | audience | operators, developers | creators, artists, producers | | proof | "here is the command" | "here is what it pays" | | cta | read the recipe | apply / submit / pull up | | tone | precise, technical, no fluff | direct, warm, concrete | | handle | @heyiris.io *(disabled)* | @freelabelnet | lead with the offer, not the mechanism. a creator does not care that the payout is computed from a views ledger; they care that 1,000 views pays them something and the deadline is friday. never post an iris recipe from @freelabelnet just because that account is connected. wrong audience, and it trains the feed on the wrong thing. `howto-social` documents the same fork. ## the pipeline for anything with an offer in it, prefer `freelabel-ads` — it has a **human approval gate** built in and stops there by default. publishing is a separate, deliberate act. that is the right default when the post promises money. ## ⚠️ verify the render before uploading `iris remotion carousel` shipped a version that rendered the composition's **demo content** and reported success — props were passed as an inline string, remotion could not parse them, and every slide read *"5 ways to grow your brand on social media"* under `done. 9 slides saved`. it also resolved a relative `-o` against the remotion package, printing that same success line over an empty directory. both fixed in cli **v1.3.198**. regardless: 1. **open `slide-0.png` and read it.** a green run is not evidence. 2. **`ls slides/<name>/*.png | wc -l` must be 9.** 3. **check the money on the stats slide against the record**, not against the props you wrote. ## batch by what is live, not by what exists do not promote a bounty whose `budget_remaining_cents` is 0 — creators will submit work that cannot be paid. filter on remaining budget and `days_until_deadline > 0` before rendering anything. ## related - `howto-social` — the iris/developer counterpart. same rails, different audience. - `freelabel-ads` — idea → creative → caption → **approval gate** → publish. use for offers. - `freelabel-bounty-ads` — preset → socialpost → ig + x in two commands. - `carousel-announce` — diary-sourced carousels, ai-written. - `discover-publish` — multi-brand publishing across beatbox, discover, emc radio, capital collective and freelabel.

entries.name: general-relativity-demo
entries.describe: Watch a 56-year astronomical mystery get solved on your own machine, down to the arcsecond. Simulate a planet's orbit the way Newton's gravity predicts it and the way Einstein's does, and see general relativity's extra term land on the exact anomaly that convinced physicists Einstein was right in 1915 — real orbital data, one equation, no black box. Pass a planet name as argument.
entries.haystack: general-relativity-demo watch a 56-year astronomical mystery get solved on your own machine, down to the arcsecond. simulate a planet's orbit the way newton's gravity predicts it and the way einstein's does, and see general relativity's extra term land on the exact anomaly that convinced physicists einstein was right in 1915 — real orbital data, one equation, no black box. pass a planet name as argument. --- name: general-relativity-demo description: watch a 56-year astronomical mystery get solved on your own machine, down to the arcsecond. simulate a planet's orbit the way newton's gravity predicts it and the way einstein's does, and see general relativity's extra term land on the exact anomaly that convinced physicists einstein was right in 1915 — real orbital data, one equation, no black box. pass a planet name as argument. version: 2 args: planet: type: string required: false default: mercury enum: [mercury, venus, earth, mars] description: which inner planet's orbit to simulate. mercury is the historical case einstein solved. allowed-tools: - bash --- # general relativity, checked against reality in 1859, the astronomer le verrier noticed that mercury's orbit was precessing — its perihelion, the closest point to the sun, slowly rotates around the sun over time. that much was expected: the gravity of every other planet tugs on mercury and makes its ellipse rotate. le verrier calculated that effect precisely, using nothing but newton's law of gravity, and it came up short. mercury precesses about 43 arcseconds per century faster than newtonian gravity, accounting for every known planet, can explain. for 56 years nobody could close that gap. the leading guess was an undiscovered planet, closer to the sun than mercury, tugging on it — they even named it *vulcan* and searched for it. it was never found, because it does not exist. in november 1915, einstein worked out that his new theory of gravity predicted an *extra* term in a planet's precession that newton's theory simply does not have — and when he computed it for mercury, it came out to almost exactly 43 arcseconds per century, with no free parameter he could have tuned to force the match. it was the first real experimental confirmation of general relativity. this playbook computes that number itself, from the planet's own real orbital measurements, so you can watch it land on the historical value rather than take anyone's word for it. ## arguments `$arguments` — which inner planet's orbit to simulate: `mercury`, `venus`, `earth`, or `mars`. defaults to mercury, the historical case. ## steps ### step:simulate newton's orbit vs. einstein's correction ## why this is worth running rather than reading anyone can be told general relativity is well-tested. this playbook makes the test happen on your own machine, in a few hundred milliseconds, using nothing controversial — mercury's real orbital elements and einstein's 1915 equation, unmodified. if it printed the wrong number, that would be worth knowing too. it doesn't: run it and check.

entries.name: genesis-guide
entries.describe: Build pages and apps on IRIS Genesis without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you — wire your own components to live data, score the design against the house standard before you publish, and prove it renders in a browser instead of trusting a green check. Pass a topic such as design, component, bind, publish, or verify.
entries.haystack: genesis-guide build pages and apps on iris genesis without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you — wire your own components to live data, score the design against the house standard before you publish, and prove it renders in a browser instead of trusting a green check. pass a topic such as design, component, bind, publish, or verify. --- name: genesis-guide description: build pages and apps on iris genesis without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you — wire your own components to live data, score the design against the house standard before you publish, and prove it renders in a browser instead of trusting a green check. pass a topic such as design, component, bind, publish, or verify. version: 2 allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task - skill --- # genesis guide — building ui on iris a page binds an address. where the rows live sits behind it. that one separation dissolves the question that blocks most genesis work — *"should the data live at the item level or the bloq level?"* it is unanswerable because it conflates how a page **addresses** rows with where rows are **stored**. this guide covers the whole path: the design standard, authoring a component, binding it to live data, publishing, and the browser verification that keeps going wrong. ## arguments `$arguments` — a topic: - `/genesis-guide design` — the design standard. mandatory before any html or css. - `/genesis-guide model` — the addressing model; read this before designing anything. - `/genesis-guide component` — author a component. - `/genesis-guide bind` — attach data to it. - `/genesis-guide publish` — compile, store, push, cache-clear. - `/genesis-guide verify` — prove it works (the part that keeps going wrong). - `/genesis-guide gaps` — what is not built yet, so you do not plan around it. --- ## 1. the model — read this first **a page binds an address. where the rows live sits behind it.** | address | rows are | backed by | writable | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `item:181094` | the table a **card carries** | `bloq_items.content.dataset` | no | | `list:2115` | the **cards in a list** | `bloq_items` | yes | | `bloq:620` | the **cards in a workspace** | `bloq_items`, `list` is a field | yes, with a list | | `dataset:sessions` | **typed records** | `atlas_schemas` + `atlas_records` | yes, gated | `item:` treats a card as a **container of rows**. `list:` and `bloq:` treat cards **as** rows. `list:` is not its own provider — it is `bloq:` with a filter, which is why a board component binds the workspace **once** and groups by the `list` field instead of binding a column at a time. ### which to reach for the line is **who reads a row**, not where it is stored. 560 generated rows should not be 560 draggable cards. a curated todo list should not need a schema migration. both are servable; neither has to become the other. ### two backing modes - **`mode_query`** — rows have their own table. sql does search, sort, count, paging. - **`mode_materialised`** — rows live inside one record. php does the same work, and the provider **must** declare `maxrows()`. past the cap the read is **refused, not truncated** — a silently short answer is indistinguishable from a correct one. --- ## 2. design — mandatory, before any html or css ** not advisory. score every page against it **before publishing**: one point each, **9–10 ship · 6–8 revise · 0–5 redesign.** **a1 is the predictor.** *could this design be moved onto a different subject unchanged?* if yes, it is a template, it will score ≤4, and local fixes will not rescue it — restart from the subject. ### if the page renders data, it must pass the second instrument too eleven more checks, and they are the ones real pages fail: d1 and d8 are the ones a component author owns: **a genesis component is bound to live data**, so the empty state, the loading state and the malformed row are yours, not the page's. ### genesis-specific non-negotiables each was learned by shipping something broken: - **theme comes from the host, not the os.** inside a genesis page, switch on `html.dark` — never `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`. a block that follows the os renders dark inside a light page. (artifacts are the opposite: they own their document and *do* use `prefers-color-scheme`.) - **a `customhtml` block must not paint its own `background`.** it becomes a slab floating on the page ground. - **namespace every selector.** `customhtml` injects via `v-html` with no isolation — a bare `body`, `section` or `table` rule leaks into the host page. - **no webfont cdns.** the csp blocks them and it falls back to arial *silently*. build stacks from faces that ship on macos and windows, or inline a data uri. - **nothing owns its outer space.** components ship `margin: 0`; the container owns rhythm via `gap`. 4px unit, 8px base, air is opt-in. ### and the one that keeps being skipped **render-verify in a real browser.** grepping strings out of the served html is not verification — point a10 exists because that failed in production. `iris pages screenshot <slug>`, then *look at the image*. --- ## 3. authoring a component options api, always. that is a **security** decision, not a style one: `<script setup>` is a module body whose safety depends on anticipating every global, while an options object reaches state through `this`, so the legal name set is *closed* — derived from your own source. there is no `window`, `document`, `fetch` or `localstorage`, and no route to one. data arrives through `$dataset` / `$datasets`, bound **on the page** — a component can never name a feed it was not given, which is the property everything else rests on. refused, each for a reason someone found the hard way: `v-html`, `<component :is>`, imports, `this` as a value, computed access via a variable, non-literal `data()`, webfont cdns, remote `url()` in css, `constructor` / `__proto__` / `object.values(this)` chains. **check before publishing:** --- ## 4. binding data or an atlas dataset, singular or named: `emitto` routes an event into page state; `bindstate` feeds page state into another component's prop. both live in the page json, so the wiring between two components is readable without opening either one. ### search, sort, write — all server-side filtering `rows` in the browser searches only the page already loaded — a term matching row 300 of 500 returns nothing and **looks exactly like no match**. `sort` is validated against declared fields; a refused key is named in `meta.sort_ignored`, so a dropped sort cannot pass as an honoured one. **the gate rule, and it is not negotiable:** a **collection never serves an ungated visitor**. it has neither a public flag nor per-column visibility — the two things that make an atlas dataset safe to expose. an atlas dataset marked public can render publicly; a collection cannot. both the ssr path and the query/create lane enforce this identically, because two lanes with different rules is how the same data ends up both gated and not. --- ## 5. publish every component compiles **before** anything is stored, so one failure aborts the batch having written nothing. re-running is idempotent; replacing someone else's component under that name returns **409** unless you pass `"replace": true`. **push from the repo root.** `iris pages push` reads `./pages` from the working directory, and `fl-iris-api` has a stale shadow `pages/` that will silently win and ship an old page. --- ## 6. verify — the part that keeps going wrong **a screenshot you actually look at.** not `mounted: true`, not a grep of the served html. grepping a page lies in both directions, repeatedly: a gated page returns 200 carrying the otp gate's markup and reads as an empty page; a symbol grep confirms a deploy that never happened; an href escaped inside page json reads as missing. for anything with a viewport, the instrument is your eyes. then: **check the instrument before believing a null result.** run a known-good control. a filtered command that prints nothing may be measuring nothing. --- ## 7. open gaps — do not plan around these - **no container primitive** (#181954 / #181956). the component host renders `display: contents` and has no box, so edge-to-edge is the default outcome for a *correctly written* component. this is why every polished page in production is still nav + one customhtml blob. it is a limit of the **page layer**, not the format — and it is what a spatial canvas would have to be built on. - **no markdown primitive.** `list:` / `bloq:` bind prose cards, and `v-html` is banned — so a board renders titles with blank bodies today. the fix is a trusted `<markdown>` primitive rendered by runtime code, which is a **new trusted surface** and deserves the stress-test treatment the compiler got. - **`textblock.maxwidth` is declared and ignored** (#181955). asked 72rem, rendered 848px. - **no per-record update on collections.** the contract has no stable row identity — a card-carried table is positional rows in a json blob. the endpoint answers **501**, not a misleading 422. - **no cli verb to declare a bloq schema.** `bloqs.custom_fields_config` is the slot; setting it currently needs the api. - **`stale: true`** is set on components compiled under an older compiler. nothing acts on it. --- ## the two page lanes, and when each wins **composable** — `codecomponent` naming stored components. a page carries **no executable code** (the console page is 1.8 kb of json), which is what makes it safe to hand to a non-trusted owner, and what lets the same components render on two pages that know nothing about them. blocked today on layout — see the container gap. **bespoke** — `render_mode: html`, one hand-written block. full layout control, and currently the only way to get a polished marketing page. costs: the page owns its own ground (`html` and `body` are transparent), every selector must be namespaced because `v-html` injects without isolation, theme comes from `html.dark` and **never** `prefers-color-scheme`, and no webfont cdn will load. pick composable when the page is a **surface over data**. pick bespoke when it is a **document someone will read**. both score against **both** instruments before publishing. a composable page does not get an exemption because its parts are components. --- ## reference - contract, diagrams, use cases — - how-to — - studio (compiles as you type) — - worked example — - same components, second page — - design standard —

entries.name: genesis-regression
entries.describe: Run the Genesis SDK regression suite before publishing anything — compiler, runtime, markdown, harness, auditor, schemas and the PHP collection/composition/trace tests, all offline. Use it before any component publish, page push or deploy that touches Genesis. Pass an action such as run, why, or add to extend coverage.
entries.haystack: genesis-regression run the genesis sdk regression suite before publishing anything — compiler, runtime, markdown, harness, auditor, schemas and the php collection/composition/trace tests, all offline. use it before any component publish, page push or deploy that touches genesis. pass an action such as run, why, or add to extend coverage. --- name: genesis-regression description: run the genesis sdk regression suite before publishing anything — compiler, runtime, markdown, harness, auditor, schemas and the php collection/composition/trace tests, all offline. use it before any component publish, page push or deploy that touches genesis. pass an action such as run, why, or add to extend coverage. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- # genesis regression suite **run this before you publish a component, push a page, or deploy anything touching genesis.** no server, no deploy, no browser, no database. about fifteen seconds. ## arguments `$arguments` — `run` · `why` · `add` · `gaps` ## what it covers | suite | checks | answers | | --- | --- | --- | | `compiler:check` | 85 | what a component may not do — every escape it has ever caught | | `runtime:check` | — | the controlled scope, compiler deliberately bypassed | | `markdown:check` | 49 | injection cannot be expressed, not merely filtered | | `harness:check` | 36 | behaviour: binding, nesting, actions, chat ordering | | `audit:check` | 19 | is it any *good* — raw values, empty states, null props | | `schemas:check` | — | declared props match their generated json | | phpunit | 70 | collections, graph gating, composition paths, trace origin | ## why one command, and why it is not just `genesis:check` `genesis:check` ran only the javascript half. on 2026-08-24 a rewrite of `findcomponent()` read one of three possible page shapes — `fetchpage()` returns a page record, so components live under `json_content` — and broke `$dataset` reads, writes and actions on **every page**, including pages that had been working all day. it was committed and deployed. **nothing anyone runs would have caught it**, because the failing code was php and the command people run is javascript. a suite split across two runners is a suite half of which nobody runs. `genesis:test` is both halves. ## what it does not cover, stated so it is not assumed - **layout.** happy-dom has no layout engine. widths, overflow, gutters and clipping are still a screenshot question — `iris pages screenshot <slug>` and *look at the image*. - **gated paths end to end.** a collection write needs an atlas session, which no offline test can mint. prove those in-container: `php artisan collections:read|write`, `atlas:graph`. - **the live agent.** `$actions` is exercised against a recorded fake, not a real reactloop run. ## before publishing — the order that catches things step 2 matters more than it looks: republishing a component changes every page naming it, immediately. version history exists, so it is recoverable — but a rollback changes all of them a second time. ## adding coverage put a test where the bug was, not where it was convenient: - **a compiler rule** → `scripts/check-code-component-compiler.mjs`, with a fixture that must trip it and a clean one that must not. a check that never fires converts "unchecked" into "passed". - **component behaviour** → `scripts/check-harness.mjs`. mounts the real compiler output through the real runtime; records every platform call, so "did it write" is answerable with no database. - **a quality rule** → `scripts/genesis-audit.mjs` + a control in `check-audit.mjs`. - **server-side shape or gating** → `tests/unit/{collections,graph,genesis}`. this is where today's regression belonged and where nothing was looking. ## the pattern behind most of these tests nearly every bug this suite guards was the same shape: **a true-looking answer to a question nobody asked.** a count of the unfiltered set. a refused sort silently answered with id order. a search that filtered nothing and returned everything. a component that rendered as empty because its artifact never resolved. a run whose origin was hardcoded. none of them threw. all of them looked fine. that is what the assertions are actually for.

entries.name: genesis-sdk
entries.describe: Build real pages and apps on IRIS — dashboards, tools, client-facing UI — without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you. Wire your own components to live data (a bloq, a table, a dataset) and get told before you publish if the design breaks the house standard or the data won't render. Pass an action as argument.
entries.haystack: genesis-sdk build real pages and apps on iris — dashboards, tools, client-facing ui — without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you. wire your own components to live data (a bloq, a table, a dataset) and get told before you publish if the design breaks the house standard or the data won't render. pass an action as argument. --- name: genesis-sdk description: build real pages and apps on iris — dashboards, tools, client-facing ui — without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you. wire your own components to live data (a bloq, a table, a dataset) and get told before you publish if the design breaks the house standard or the data won't render. pass an action as argument. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task --- # genesis sdk — building ui on iris the current understanding, in one place. where this contradicts `pages`, `bespoke` or `seed-pages`, **this is newer** — those describe a page-json world that predates components and collections. ## arguments `$arguments` — an action: - `/genesis-sdk design` — **the design standard. mandatory. read before writing any html or css.** - `/genesis-sdk model` — the addressing model; read this before designing anything - `/genesis-sdk component` — author a component - `/genesis-sdk bind` — attach data to it - `/genesis-sdk publish` — compile, store, push, cache-clear - `/genesis-sdk verify` — prove it works (the part that keeps going wrong) - `/genesis-sdk gaps` — what is not built yet, so you do not plan around it --- ## 1. the model — read this first **a page binds an address. where the rows live sits behind it.** one separation, and it dissolves the question that blocked this design for a long time — *"should a dataset live at the item level or the bloq level?"* unanswerable, because it conflated how a page **addresses** rows with where rows are **stored**. | address | rows are | backed by | writable | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `item:181094` | the table a **card carries** | `bloq_items.content.dataset` | no | | `list:2115` | the **cards in a list** | `bloq_items` | yes | | `bloq:620` | the **cards in a workspace** | `bloq_items`, `list` is a field | yes, with a list | | `dataset:sessions` | **typed records** | `atlas_schemas` + `atlas_records` | yes, gated | `item:` treats a card as a **container of rows**. `list:` and `bloq:` treat cards **as** rows. `list:` is not its own provider — it is `bloq:` with a filter, which is why a board component binds the workspace **once** and groups by the `list` field instead of binding a column at a time. ### which to reach for the line is **who reads a row**, not where it is stored. 560 generated rows should not be 560 draggable cards. a curated todo list should not need a schema migration. both are servable; neither has to become the other. ### two backing modes - **`mode_query`** — rows have their own table. sql does search, sort, count, paging. - **`mode_materialised`** — rows live inside one record. php does the same work, and the provider **must** declare `maxrows()`. past the cap the read is **refused, not truncated** — a silently short answer is indistinguishable from a correct one. ### what this replaced all of it existed only to reconcile two stores, and none of it is needed: a promotion pipeline (card grid → atlas), `atlas_schemas.bloq_item_id`, a `source_hash` + drift detector, schema inference with per-field overrides, a demotion policy. **nothing migrates.** --- ## 1b. design — mandatory, before any html or css ** not advisory. score every page against it **before publishing**: one point each, **9–10 ship · 6–8 revise · 0–5 redesign.** **a1 is the predictor.** *could this design be moved onto a different subject unchanged?* if yes, it is a template, it will score ≤4, and local fixes will not rescue it — restart from the subject. ### if the page renders data, it must pass the second instrument too eleven more checks, and they are the ones real pages fail: d1 and d8 are the ones a component author owns: **a genesis component is bound to live data**, so the empty state, the loading state and the malformed row are yours, not the page's. ### genesis-specific non-negotiables each was learned by shipping something broken: - **theme comes from the host, not the os.** inside a genesis page, switch on `html.dark` — never `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`. a block that follows the os renders dark inside a light page. (artifacts are the opposite: they own their document and *do* use `prefers-color-scheme`.) - **a `customhtml` block must not paint its own `background`.** it becomes a slab floating on the page ground. - **namespace every selector.** `customhtml` injects via `v-html` with no isolation — a bare `body`, `section` or `table` rule leaks into the host page. - **no webfont cdns.** the csp blocks them and it falls back to arial *silently*. build stacks from faces that ship on macos and windows, or inline a data uri. - **nothing owns its outer space.** components ship `margin: 0`; the container owns rhythm via `gap`. 4px unit, 8px base, air is opt-in. ### and the one that keeps being skipped **render-verify in a real browser.** grepping strings out of the served html is not verification — point a10 exists because that failed in production. `iris pages screenshot <slug>`, then *look at the image*. --- ## 2. authoring a component options api, always. that is a **security** decision, not a style one: `<script setup>` is a module body whose safety depends on anticipating every global, while an options object reaches state through `this`, so the legal name set is *closed* — derived from your own source. there is no `window`, `document`, `fetch` or `localstorage`, and no route to one. data arrives through `$dataset` / `$datasets`, bound **on the page** — a component can never name a feed it was not given, which is the property everything else rests on. refused, each for a reason someone found the hard way: `v-html`, `<component :is>`, imports, `this` as a value, computed access via a variable, non-literal `data()`, webfont cdns, remote `url()` in css, `constructor` / `__proto__` / `object.values(this)` chains. **check before publishing:** --- ## 3. binding data or an atlas dataset, singular or named: `emitto` routes an event into page state; `bindstate` feeds page state into another component's prop. both live in the page json, so the wiring between two components is readable without opening either one. ### search, sort, write — all server-side filtering `rows` in the browser searches only the page already loaded — a term matching row 300 of 500 returns nothing and **looks exactly like no match**. `sort` is validated against declared fields; a refused key is named in `meta.sort_ignored`, so a dropped sort cannot pass as an honoured one. **the gate rule, and it is not negotiable:** a **collection never serves an ungated visitor**. it has neither a public flag nor per-column visibility — the two things that make an atlas dataset safe to expose. an atlas dataset marked public can render publicly; a collection cannot. both the ssr path and the query/create lane enforce this identically, because two lanes with different rules is how the same data ends up both gated and not. --- ## 4. publish every component compiles **before** anything is stored, so one failure aborts the batch having written nothing. re-running is idempotent; replacing someone else's component under that name returns **409** unless you pass `"replace": true`. **push from the repo root.** `iris pages push` reads `./pages` from the working directory, and `fl-iris-api` has a stale shadow `pages/` that will silently win and ship an old page. --- ## 5. verify — the part that keeps going wrong **a screenshot you actually look at.** not `mounted: true`, not a grep of the served html. grepping a page lies in both directions, repeatedly and in this codebase: a gated page returns 200 carrying the otp gate's markup and reads as an empty page; a symbol grep confirms a deploy that never happened; an href escaped inside page json reads as missing. for anything with a viewport, the instrument is your eyes. then: **check the instrument before believing a null result.** run a known-good control. a filtered command that prints nothing may be measuring nothing. --- ## 6. open gaps — do not plan around these - **no container primitive** (#181954 / #181956). the component host renders `display: contents` and has no box, so edge-to-edge is the default outcome for a *correctly written* component. this is why every polished page in production is still nav + one customhtml blob. it is a limit of the **page layer**, not the format — and it is what a spatial canvas would have to be built on. - **no markdown primitive.** `list:` / `bloq:` bind prose cards, and `v-html` is banned — so a board renders titles with blank bodies today. the fix is a trusted `<markdown>` primitive rendered by runtime code, which is a **new trusted surface** and deserves the stress-test treatment the compiler got. - **`textblock.maxwidth` is declared and ignored** (#181955). asked 72rem, rendered 848px. - **no per-record update on collections.** the contract has no stable row identity — a card-carried table is positional rows in a json blob. the endpoint answers **501**, not a misleading 422. - **no cli verb to declare a bloq schema.** `bloqs.custom_fields_config` is the slot; setting it currently needs the api. - **`stale: true`** is set on components compiled under an older compiler. nothing acts on it. --- ## the two page lanes, and when each wins **composable** — `codecomponent` naming stored components. a page carries **no executable code** (the console page is 1.8 kb of json), which is what makes it safe to hand to a non-trusted owner, and what lets the same components render on two pages that know nothing about them. blocked today on layout — see the container gap. **bespoke** — `render_mode: html`, one hand-written block. full layout control, and currently the only way to get a polished marketing page. costs: the page owns its own ground (`html` and `body` are transparent), every selector must be namespaced because `v-html` injects without isolation, theme comes from `html.dark` and **never** `prefers-color-scheme`, and no webfont cdn will load. pick composable when the page is a **surface over data**. pick bespoke when it is a **document someone will read**. both score against **both** instruments before publishing — see §1b. a composable page does not get an exemption because its parts are components. --- ## reference - contract, diagrams, use cases — - how-to — - studio (compiles as you type) — - worked example — - same components, second page — - design standard —

entries.name: geometric-reasoning-briefing
entries.describe: A tiny lab claims its small models out-reason giants 60-1000x by training the actual geometry of thought instead of scaling data. The claim is unverified and the company name is uncertain, but the evaluation trick they use to prove it is real, reusable, and worth stealing for our own eval harness today. Pass a question about the claim or the technique as argument.
entries.haystack: geometric-reasoning-briefing a tiny lab claims its small models out-reason giants 60-1000x by training the actual geometry of thought instead of scaling data. the claim is unverified and the company name is uncertain, but the evaluation trick they use to prove it is real, reusable, and worth stealing for our own eval harness today. pass a question about the claim or the technique as argument. --- name: geometric-reasoning-briefing description: a tiny lab claims its small models out-reason giants 60-1000x by training the actual geometry of thought instead of scaling data. the claim is unverified and the company name is uncertain, but the evaluation trick they use to prove it is real, reusable, and worth stealing for our own eval harness today. pass a question about the claim or the technique as argument. version: 1 args: focus: type: string required: false description: what to dig into — the core claim, the perturbation-testing technique, or the strategic implications for iris. defaults to a full briefing. allowed-tools: - read - webfetch - websearch - write --- # geometric reasoning — research briefing **source:** a ~54-minute interview (youtu.be/4s8i22ybg2c), transcribed via `iris transcribe`. full transcript archived at ` **confidence: low-to-medium, name now confirmed.** this is one interview with one founder about their own unpublished work. the company is **sophontic** (sophontic.ai) — confirmed by web search after the asr transcript garbled it five different ways ("sofontic" / "phontik" / "sofantek"); their own site independently confirms the geometric-reasoning framing, the rejection of the scale paradigm, and an unreleased "perturbation-paradigm eval kit," which lines up with the interview. that's real corroboration of the *positioning* — it is not a third-party benchmark or a reproduction of the *result*. no paper, no independent eval, no reproduction exists in what we have. **treat the company and the technique as real; treat the 60x-1000x number as their own unverified claim until an outside benchmark exists.** ## arguments `$arguments` — what to focus on: the core claim, the evaluation technique, or the strategic read for iris. leave blank for the full briefing below. --- ## 1. the claim, in plain terms mainstream ai training treats reasoning as an emergent side effect of scale: feed a model enough data and enough compute, and something that looks like thought shows up as a "mysterious emergent property." the guest's argument is that this is backwards. reasoning, in his framing, is a **geometric structure** — a specific mathematical shape — that already exists inside a model's internal (latent/vector) space. instead of hoping that shape emerges from brute-force scale, his lab studies it directly, empirically, inside the latent space itself, and trains it into the model from the foundation up. the claimed result: very small models (laptop-scale, discussed as possibly under 10b — even under 1b — parameters) **out-reasoning models 100-1000x larger** on rigorous reasoning tests. the founder is explicit that the exact multiplier is unresolved — "somewhere between 60 times and three orders of magnitude" — and says so on his own website as the conservative number. that candor is a point in the claim's favor; a huckster picks the biggest number and doesn't hedge it. ## 2. the technique that's real regardless of the bigger claim: perturbation testing this is the part worth adopting **whether or not the geometric-reasoning story holds up**, because it's a testing method, not a training claim, and we can verify it ourselves. **the problem it targets:** standard ai evals can be gamed by memorization. a model that has seen a problem (or something close to it) in training can answer correctly without having reasoned about it at all — and most benchmarks can't tell the difference, because they only score whether the final answer matches. **the fix — "the perturbation paradigm":** take a problem the model gets right, then make a small, targeted change to it that flips the correct answer (change a number, swap two words that alter the logic) without changing the problem's surface difficulty. a model that memorized the original still gives the original answer — now wrong. a model that actually reasoned through the structure gets the new one right, because it re-derives the answer instead of recalling it. **why this matters to us specifically:** the pricing-model audit (see `price-your-business` and the underlying iris labs cost review) already surfaced that our own eval harness (`eval:v6`) has no cost column and no `--model` flag — we can rank model quality but not quality-per-dollar, and we can't hold a test set constant while swapping models. perturbation testing is a cheap, orthogonal upgrade to add on top of that fix: it would tell us whether a model routed into production is actually reasoning about a client's case/lead/document, or pattern-matching a similar one it's seen before. worth prototyping against one of our own agent eval suites independent of whether we ever look at this lab again. ## 3. the strategic argument, and why it's worth taking seriously even if the number is wrong independent of whether "60x to 1000x" survives scrutiny, the founder makes three structural arguments that are worth engaging with on their own merits: - **"frozen giants."** a frontier model is trained once, at enormous cost, to a stable state, then frozen — what looks like "learning" in a chat session (memory, context) is closer to sticky notes for someone with amnesia than actual learning. if small models can genuinely reason, the barrier to *continual* learning drops with them — a model that keeps adapting on ordinary hardware, not one re-trained from scratch by a lab with a nation-state budget. - **concentration risk.** only a handful of organizations can afford frontier-scale training, which means only a narrow slice of human thought gets instilled into the systems everyone increasingly relies on — a "monoculture," in his phrase, at exactly the layer where diversity is usually what keeps a system resilient. - **precedent for small-and-real over big-and-scaled.** the protein-folding model that drove real biotech breakthroughs was under 100m parameters — "a toy" by frontier standards — and it worked because it was small enough to genuinely iterate and specialize, not despite being small. none of this requires believing the specific multiplier. it's a coherent argument for why "small, real reasoning beats large, statistical pattern-matching" is a plausible direction, and it's the same direction iris hive already bets on: run real work on hardware you own instead of paying for a data center, and treat model routing (not raw scale) as the lever that actually controls cost and capability — which is close to word-for-word what the pricing-model audit found about our own routing decisions in §04-05. ## 4. what to actually do with this 1. **done — the source is confirmed.** sophontic (sophontic.ai) is a real, findable research company matching the interview's claims. still watch for an independent benchmark or paper before treating the 60x-1000x figure as anything more than their own number. 2. **prototype perturbation testing on one existing eval suite** — this doesn't require the bigger claim to be true to be worth doing. 3. **do not cite the 60x-1000x figure externally** (a pitch deck, a client conversation) without independent confirmation. internally, it's a reason to watch the space; externally, an unverified single-source number stated as fact is exactly the kind of claim this team has burned time chasing down before (see the pricing-model audit's own §16 on rejecting an outside review's claims that didn't survive checking against our own numbers). ## the shape of the mistake this briefing is trying to avoid the easy failure here is treating "a founder said an impressive number in an interview" as equivalent to "a benchmarked, reproduced result." the founder himself doesn't make that mistake — he publishes the conservative number and says the truth is somewhere in a range he hasn't pinned down. this briefing tries to hold the same line: separate the part that's a genuinely reusable technique (perturbation testing — adopt it) from the part that's an unverified claim from one interview (the multiplier and the company itself — verify before repeating).

entries.name: getting-started-with-iris
entries.describe: Go from a laptop with nothing installed to a working setup with your own tools connected, your own files searchable, and your first reusable procedure published — in one sitting. Every step is a command you can actually run, and each one ends by proving it worked instead of assuming it did.
entries.haystack: getting-started-with-iris go from a laptop with nothing installed to a working setup with your own tools connected, your own files searchable, and your first reusable procedure published — in one sitting. every step is a command you can actually run, and each one ends by proving it worked instead of assuming it did. --- name: getting-started-with-iris description: go from a laptop with nothing installed to a working setup with your own tools connected, your own files searchable, and your first reusable procedure published — in one sitting. every step is a command you can actually run, and each one ends by proving it worked instead of assuming it did. version: 2 industries: - onboarding - training - operations - agency args: bloq: type: number required: false description: the knowledge base (atlas board) to ingest files into. find yours with `iris atlas list`. leave empty to be shown how to pick one. topic: type: string required: false default: onboarding description: a word or phrase to sweep for once your data is in — a client name, a project, a product. recording: type: string required: false description: path to a recorded walkthrough (audio or video) to turn into a playbook. leave empty to be walked through recording one. on-error: ask timeout: 1800 --- # getting started with iris a first-day path, in order, ending with something you built rather than something you read. by the end you will have: the cli installed and authenticated, your own accounts connected, your own documents ingested and searchable, and **one published playbook that you made from a recording of yourself doing the work.** ## who this is for someone who has never opened this tool before — and the person sitting with them. no prior setup is assumed. every command below is real; nothing is illustrative. ## the one habit worth teaching on day one **every step here ends by checking its own result.** not because the tool is untrustworthy, but because the failures that cost the most time are the quiet ones — an ingest that reports success and moves zero files, a connection that says "connected" and has no permission to read anything. a command that exits 0 has told you it *ran*. it has not told you it *worked*. so each step below does the thing, then asks a second, different question to confirm it. if you teach one habit on day one, teach that one. --- ## steps ### step:install install the cli and confirm who you are two separate questions, deliberately. `--version` proves the binary is on your path. `auth whoami` proves this machine is authenticated **and shows which account** — the single most common day-one confusion is being logged into a different account than the one your data lives in, and every later step will look mysteriously empty if you are. ### step:doctor take a baseline reading before changing anything run this **now, before connecting anything**, and read it as a starting photograph rather than a report card. warnings on a fresh install are expected — nothing is connected yet. its value is comparative: when something breaks in week three, the useful question is "what changed since day one," and this is the only moment you can cheaply capture the "before." ### step:explore see what the tool actually covers roughly a hundred command groups ship here, which is genuinely too many to learn linearly — and trying to is the most common way a first session stalls. `iris guide` lists them by category; `iris guide <topic>` opens one. two escape hatches worth memorising instead of memorising commands: `iris <command> --help` for any command, and `iris guide <topic>` for a whole area. ### step:connect connect the accounts you already use start with wherever your **documents** live — that's what the next step ingests. chat and calendar can wait; storage cannot, because everything downstream reads from it. ### step:connect-check prove the connection can actually read "connected" in a sign-in window and "readable by this tool" are two different claims. this step is the second one. it exists because the failure it catches is invisible: a partial oauth grant produces an ingest job that starts, finishes, and imports nothing. ### step:ingest pull your own files in **pick one folder, not your whole drive.** a first ingest should be small enough that you can personally verify the result in the next step — if you import ten thousand files you cannot tell a successful import from a broken one by looking. ingestion is asynchronous: `sync` hands back a job id and returns immediately. the command finishing is not the import finishing. `iris data-sources status <jobid>` is the one that actually answers "is it done." ### step:search confirm your data is really in there this is the step that makes the ingest real. search for something you *know* is in the files you just imported — a client name, a heading, a phrase you remember. if it comes back empty, believe the search, not the earlier success message. ### step:pulse sweep every trail one topic left `pulse check` takes **a topic, not everything** — it sweeps the trails one subject left across your commits, notes, files, sessions, messages and mail, then scores how warm the thread is. it answers *"where does this topic actually live, and is it still moving?"* use it as the "what do i already have on this?" question before starting work — not as a bulk-import step. importing is `data-sources sync` above; this is retrieval. ### step:record record yourself doing a real task recording beats writing here for one reason: written procedures drift from what people actually do, and they drift silently. a recording of the real thing cannot drift, because it *is* the real thing. the written version becomes an output of the recording rather than a separate chore someone has to remember. ### step:draft turn the recording into a playbook this transcribes the recording and structures it into steps for you. it produces a **draft** — expect to edit it. the machine can hear what you did; it cannot always tell which parts mattered, and it will occasionally promote an aside into a step. same input, three outputs, depending on who the reader is: `playbook draft` for something runnable, `playbook sop` for a person to follow, `transcribe` for the raw words. ### step:validate check it before anyone else runs it `doctor` catches the failures that are invisible from the outside — a step that will silently never execute, a duplicate copy of the playbook shadowing the one you edited, a step declaring a mode that isn't real. all of these *look* fine when you read the file. then `--dry-run` before a real run, always. it prints the plan without executing a single step, which is the cheapest possible way to find out you pointed something at the wrong folder. ### step:publish publish it, then verify it landed **a successful publish and a live, current playbook are two different claims.** publish returning a checkmark means the request succeeded. `verify` is the one that checks the local file, what's actually stored, whether they still match, and whether the page really loads — four separate questions, because they can and do disagree. start private. you can widen scope later; you cannot un-share something. ### step:next where to go after day one the reason to capture procedures at all is that the work you do repeatedly is the work worth handing off — to a colleague, or to an agent that can read it. both need the same thing: the procedure written down accurately, which is what you just made.

entries.name: heartbeat-debug
entries.describe: Debug, diagnose, and manage the heartbeat agent system in production. Use when heartbeats aren't running, agents are looping, circuit breakers trip, or you need to inspect/kill/restart heartbeat jobs. Pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "diagnose", "kill", "logs").
entries.haystack: heartbeat-debug debug, diagnose, and manage the heartbeat agent system in production. use when heartbeats aren't running, agents are looping, circuit breakers trip, or you need to inspect/kill/restart heartbeat jobs. pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "diagnose", "kill", "logs"). --- name: heartbeat-debug description: debug, diagnose, and manage the heartbeat agent system in production. use when heartbeats aren't running, agents are looping, circuit breakers trip, or you need to inspect/kill/restart heartbeat jobs. pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "diagnose", "kill", "logs"). allowed-tools: - read - bash - grep - glob - task --- # heartbeat debug — production debugging skill debug and manage the autonomous agent heartbeat system across fl-api and iris-api. ## arguments `$arguments` — action to perform. examples: - `/heartbeat-debug status` — quick health overview of all heartbeat agents - `/heartbeat-debug diagnose` — full diagnostic (loop detection, rapid-fire, token burn) - `/heartbeat-debug diagnose 11` — diagnose specific agent - `/heartbeat-debug logs` — tail production heartbeat logs - `/heartbeat-debug kill 248` — emergency kill a runaway agent - `/heartbeat-debug run 766` — manually trigger heartbeat for agent - `/heartbeat-debug history 766` — view recent execution history - `/heartbeat-debug circuit-breaker 11` — check/reset circuit breaker - `/heartbeat-debug scheduler` — check if scheduler is running - `/heartbeat-debug jobs` — list all heartbeat scheduled jobs - `/heartbeat-debug pause 764` — safely pause a heartbeat (won't resurrect) - `/heartbeat-debug resume 764` — resume a paused heartbeat - `/heartbeat-debug model 604 grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning xai` — change agent model --- ## architecture quick reference ### infrastructure (railway — april 2026) | service | role | db | production url | |---------|------|-----|----------------| | **fl-api** | orchestrator — schedules jobs, runs `agents:process-jobs` every minute | `freelabelnet` | `raichu.heyiris.io` (railway) | | **iris-api** | executor — builds prompts, calls llms, writes results back | `iris_db` + `fl_api` connection to `freelabelnet` | `freelabel.net` (railway) | | **iris-worker** | queue worker — processes `runworkspaceagenticjob` for heartbeat execution | same as iris-api | railway (separate service) | ### flow ### key principles 1. heartbeat runs through `agents:process-jobs`, not its own cron. if heartbeat stops, the scheduling infrastructure is broken. 2. the scheduler is the **universal cron harness** for all job types. 3. `executeagentjob` has a **staleness guard** — if the job status is no longer "running" when the queue worker picks it up, it skips execution. this prevents backlog floods. 4. `tries = 1` — no laravel retry. retries on scheduled jobs cause duplicates. --- ## iris cli commands (preferred) --- ## action implementations ### 1. `status` — quick health overview --- ### 2. `diagnose` — full diagnostic --- ### 3. `pause` — safely pause a heartbeat (won't resurrect) **critical: you must do both steps or the heartbeat will resurrect within minutes.** there are **three resurrection paths** in processagentjobs.php that recreate paused jobs: 1. `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` — creates new job if none found (checks completed/cancelled/paused) 2. `resetstuckjobs()` — auto-recovers paused heartbeats after 1 hour (checks for "auto-paused" in last_error) 3. `heartbeatservice::enableheartbeat()` — `updateorcreate` always sets status='scheduled' **the only reliable way to stop a heartbeat: set `heartbeat_mode = 'off'` on the agent and cancel the job.** just setting `status = 'paused'` is not enough — the job will be recreated within minutes by `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` or un-paused by `resetstuckjobs()`. ### 4. `resume` — resume a paused heartbeat --- ### 5. `model` — change agent model **critical bug (as of april 2026): agent model is stored in two columns — `settings` and `config`.** - `settings.model` — written by ui and `iris` cli - `config.model` — read by `heartbeatexecutorservice` (line 182) - if only `settings` is updated, heartbeats keep using the old model (defaults to `gpt-4.1-nano`) - v6 `reactloopservice` reads `config` first, `settings` as fallback (line 272) **bug filed as #67225. until fixed, always update both columns:** note: `config` column may be `[]` (empty array) not `{}` (empty object). if `json_set` fails, use: **recommended models:** - `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning` / `xai` — $0.20/m input, fast, good for heartbeats - `gpt-4.1-nano` / (default openai) — $0.10/m input, cheapest - `gpt-5-nano` / (default openai) — slightly better reasoning --- ### 6. `kill` — emergency kill agent --- ### 7. `run` — manually trigger heartbeat --- ### 8. `history` — view recent executions --- ### 9. `scheduler` — check scheduler health **known issue (fixed april 23, 2026):** `start-queue-worker.sh` had `set -e` + `curl` to `/workspace/yt-dlp`. if `/workspace` doesn't exist (railway), the queue worker enters fatal state on every deploy. jobs accumulate in redis indefinitely. fix: removed `set -e`, added `mkdir -p /workspace`, made installs non-fatal. --- ### 10. `jobs` — list all heartbeat jobs --- ## known bugs & fixes (april 2026) ### fixed: queue worker crash on railway deploy **commit:** `7e3704f5` | **severity:** critical `start-queue-worker.sh` had `set -e` + curl to `/workspace/yt-dlp`. `/workspace` doesn't exist on railway → exit code 23 → fatal state. jobs accumulate in redis forever. when worker restarts, all backlogged jobs fire at once. **fix:** removed `set -e`, added `mkdir -p /workspace`, non-fatal installs. ### fixed: backlog flood / duplicate dispatches **commit:** `8d703ce7` | **severity:** high dead queue worker → scheduler keeps queuing `executeagentjob` to redis → auto-recovery resets job → another dispatch → hundreds of jobs in redis → worker restarts → all fire simultaneously. **fix:** staleness guard in `executeagentjob.handle()` — checks `$job->status !== 'running'` before executing. `tries = 1` prevents laravel retry. ### fixed: dead iris-api url **commit:** `7e3704f5` | **severity:** high `irisapiservice.php` hardcoded `iris-api.freelabel.net` (dead after railway migration). changed to `heyiris.io`. ### fixed: scheduler logs invisible **commit:** `d7b5928d` | **severity:** medium `agents:process-jobs` output went to file only. now uses `tee >&2` to write to both file and stderr (railway captures). ### fixed: paused heartbeats resurrecting **commits:** `be6101cb`, `9d868493` | **severity:** high two code paths ignored paused status: 1. `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` — excluded completed/cancelled but not paused → created new jobs 2. `resetstuckjobs()` — treated all paused heartbeats as "dead" → un-paused after 1 hour **fix:** added `'paused'` to exclusion list. `resetstuckjobs` now distinguishes auto-paused (system, from failures) vs manually paused (user). **however:** these fixes are insufficient. there are additional resurrection paths (heartbeatservice `updateorcreate`, syncagentrecurringtasks). the **only reliable way** to stop a heartbeat is setting `heartbeat_mode = 'off'` on the agent and cancelling the job. see the `pause` action above. ### open: agent model split (settings vs config) **bug:** #67225 | **severity:** high `bloq_agents` has `settings.model` and `config.model`. heartbeatexecutorservice reads `config.model`, ui writes `settings.model`. workaround: update both columns. see the `model` action above. ### open: chain som_batch → inbox_scan 422 **fix deployed:** `ea1a463` on iris-api — added `inbox_scan` to nodetaskcontroller validation. --- ## common production scenarios ### heartbeat not running 1. check agent: `heartbeat_mode` must not be 'off' 2. check job exists: `iris schedules list` — look for the agent 3. check scheduler: `railway logs --service fl-api | grep agents:process-jobs` 4. check queue worker: `railway logs --service fl-api | grep "fatal\|queue-worker"` — if fatal, redeploy 5. check queue backlog: `echo "llen queues:agent-jobs" | railway connect redis` 6. check iris-worker: `railway logs --service fl-iris-worker | grep runworkspaceagenticjob` ### agent running too often (spam) 1. check if there are duplicate jobs for the same agent: 2. check queue backlog: `echo "llen queues:agent-jobs" | railway connect redis` 3. if backlog > 0, flush it: `echo "del queues:agent-jobs" | railway connect redis` 4. cancel duplicates, keep one per agent 5. check if `heartbeat_mode` is set — `ensureheartbeatjobsexist` creates new jobs for any agent with mode != 'off' ### agent using wrong model / getting 429 1. check both columns: `select json_extract(settings,'$.model'), json_extract(config,'$.model') from bloq_agents where id = x` 2. if `config.model` is null → heartbeat defaults to `gpt-4.1-nano` regardless of `settings.model` 3. update both: see `model` action above 4. 429 = credits exhausted on that provider. switch provider or top up credits. ### agent won't stop (keeps resurrecting) 1. **don't just pause the job** — it will come back within minutes 2. set `heartbeat_mode = 'off'`: `update bloq_agents set heartbeat_mode = 'off' where id = x` 3. cancel the job: `update bloq_scheduled_jobs set status = 'cancelled' where agent_id = x and task_name = 'heartbeat'` 4. both steps are required. see `pause` action above. ### post-deploy: queue worker dead 1. check: `railway logs --service fl-api | grep "fatal\|exit status"` 2. if you see `exit status 23` or `entered fatal state` → queue worker crashed during startup 3. usually caused by missing `/workspace` directory or failed curl downloads 4. fix: ensure `start-queue-worker.sh` doesn't have `set -e` and all installs are non-fatal 5. redeploy: `railway redeploy --service fl-api --yes` --- ## database schema reference ### bloq_agents (fl-api) ### bloq_scheduled_jobs (fl-api) --- ## key files ### fl-api - `app/console/commands/processagentjobs.php` — core scheduler + `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` + `resetstuckjobs()` - `app/jobs/executeagentjob.php` — queue job with staleness guard + type routing - `app/services/agentjobschedulerservice.php` — `getduejobs()`, `markjobcompleted()`, `calculatenextrun()` - `app/services/heartbeatservice.php` — `enableheartbeat()` with `updateorcreate` (resurrection path #3) - `app/services/irisapiservice.php` — bridge to iris-api (`dispatchdirecttask`, `dispatchhivetask`) - `app/console/kernel.php` — `agentjobscheduler()` scheduling config - `start-queue-worker.sh` — queue worker startup (installs yt-dlp/ffmpeg) - `start-scheduler.sh` — scheduler startup (schedule:run loop) ### iris-api - `app/services/heartbeatexecutorservice.php` — prompt builder + llm execution (reads `config.model`) - `app/services/v6/reactloopservice.php` — v6 agentic workflow engine - `app/services/v6/v6aiservice.php` — model→provider routing (openai/xai/openrouter) - `app/http/controllers/api/nodetaskcontroller.php` — hive task dispatch validation --- ## active agents reference (april 2026) | agent id | name | model | provider | frequency | schedule id | |----------|------|-------|----------|-----------|-------------| | 604 | delo alert trading simulator | grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | xai | every 4 hours | #764 | | 605 | delo backtester | grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | xai | daily | #766 | | 606 | delo oversight | grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | xai | every 4 hours | #768 | **disabled agents** (heartbeat_mode = 'off'): 315 (legal reviewer), 366 (ayala+goodbuy), 593 (platform updates bot), 594 (leads crm digest), 595 (delo alert assistant), 596 (dent society), 597 (cottonwood creek), 598 (ayala engineering) --- ## production access cheatsheet

entries.name: hive-rent-compute
entries.describe: Rent a long-lived machine, put it in your Hive, run your code on it, and release it when you are done. Covers Railway (hosting) and DigitalOcean (raw boxes, GPUs). Use this instead of standing up a server by hand.
entries.haystack: hive-rent-compute rent a long-lived machine, put it in your hive, run your code on it, and release it when you are done. covers railway (hosting) and digitalocean (raw boxes, gpus). use this instead of standing up a server by hand. --- name: hive-rent-compute description: rent a long-lived machine, put it in your hive, run your code on it, and release it when you are done. covers railway (hosting) and digitalocean (raw boxes, gpus). use this instead of standing up a server by hand. version: 2 args: name: type: string required: true provider: type: string required: false default: railway command: type: string required: false default: python3 -c "import platform,sys;print(sys.version.split()[0], platform.node())" on-error: stop timeout: 600 --- # rent a machine a rental is a machine you **keep** — not a job that finishes. iris provisions it, installs the iris agent so it joins your hive, and you run work on it like any machine you own. nothing releases it for you. that is the point of a rental, and it is why the last step matters more than the first. ## steps ### step:providers check what you can rent from ### step:rent rent the machine ### step:confirm confirm it is yours and running ### step:run run your code on it ### step:release release it, and stop the bill

entries.name: howto-social
entries.describe: Turn a published how-to recipe into an Instagram carousel and an X post, with no AI writing step. A recipe is already structured content, so the slides are a MAPPING of it rather than a model's summary — which means the post cannot say something the recipe does not. Pass a recipe slug (e.g. "hive-tailscale", "remote-support-a-family-pc"), or "all" to batch the library.
entries.haystack: howto-social turn a published how-to recipe into an instagram carousel and an x post, with no ai writing step. a recipe is already structured content, so the slides are a mapping of it rather than a model's summary — which means the post cannot say something the recipe does not. pass a recipe slug (e.g. "hive-tailscale", "remote-support-a-family-pc"), or "all" to batch the library. --- name: howto-social description: turn a published how-to recipe into an instagram carousel and an x post, with no ai writing step. a recipe is already structured content, so the slides are a mapping of it rather than a model's summary — which means the post cannot say something the recipe does not. pass a recipe slug (e.g. "hive-tailscale", "remote-support-a-family-pc"), or "all" to batch the library. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- # how-to → social every published recipe at `heyiris.io/how-to` is a finished piece of content with a real use case, correct copy, and a link that goes somewhere. this turns one into 9 carousel slides and an x post. **the content step uses no model.** a recipe already carries title, summary, category, level, duration, tags, section headings and a code block, and `carouselslide`'s schema wants exactly those fields. generating slides from it is a mapping, not an inference — so the post cannot drift from what the recipe actually says. use `iris remotion auto-carousel` when you have only a topic; use this when you have the article. ## arguments `$arguments` — a recipe slug, or `all`. - `/howto-social hive-tailscale` - `/howto-social remote-support-a-family-pc` - `/howto-social all` — batch every published recipe find slugs with `iris how-to list` (grouped by category) or browse `heyiris.io/how-to`. ## the pipeline `--also instagram,threads` on `iris x post` cross-posts in one call. ## check the account before you render not every brand account is connected at any given moment, and the state changes — a dated list here would be wrong within a week. read the command output, not this paragraph. **that matters for this playbook specifically.** these recipes are product content for a developer audience. posting them from a different brand's account is a brand decision, not a fallback — ask before doing it. if the intended account is disconnected, fix the connection rather than quietly posting as someone else. ## verify the slides before posting. do not skip this. **`iris remotion carousel` used to render the composition's demo content and report success.** the shell wrapper passed props as an inline string (`--props "$json"`); remotion could not parse it and silently fell back to placeholder copy, so every slide read *"5 ways to grow your brand on social media"* while the command printed `done. 9 slides saved`. fixed in cli **v1.3.198** by passing a props file per slide. two habits survive the fix, because the failure mode is a wrong post rather than an error: 1. **open slide-0.png and read it.** if it says anything about growing your brand on social media, the props did not bind. a green run is not evidence. 2. **count the files.** `ls slides/<slug>/*.png | wc -l` should be 9. the same wrapper also resolved a relative `-o` against the remotion package instead of your cwd, printing `9 slides saved` over an empty directory. also fixed in v1.3.198, but count anyway. ## what lands on which slide | slide | content | source field | |---|---|---| | 0 | category badge, headline, opening paragraph | `category`, title, first `##` section | | 1–2 | section highlights | first three `##` headings + text | | 3 | terminal card | first fenced code block, capped at 52 columns | | 4–7 | checklist, tags, stats | `tags`, `level`, `duration_min`, section headings | | 8 | cta | `heyiris.io/how-to/<slug>` + `iris how-to view <slug>` | code lines are cut at 52 columns on purpose — the card wraps mid-word past that and reads as broken rather than dense. ## the x caption assembled from the recipe's own words: headline, first sentence, canonical url, up to three tags. it refuses to exceed 280 including the link, dropping the sentence before the link. read it before posting. it is faithful to the recipe by construction, but "faithful" and "good opening line" are different bars, and a recipe whose first sentence is throat-clearing will produce a flat post. rewrite the caption freely — the slides are the part that must stay accurate. ## batch mode generate props for everything, then render selectively. rendering 46 recipes is ~9 stills each and is not something to kick off without a reason. **pick by category, not alphabetically.** `iris how-to list --category "getting started"` is the set worth posting first — they are the recipes a new reader can act on immediately. ## wrong audience is a failure mode, not a fallback these recipes are developer content. when the intended account is disconnected and another brand's is live, it is tempting to post from whichever one works. don't do it by default — a creator-facing feed and a developer-facing one want different things, and a hive+tailscale recipe trains the wrong one. if the subject is a creator offer — a bounty, an event, a program — you want **`freelabel-social`**, which maps live opportunity records (including the money) and speaks to that audience. ## related - `freelabel-social` — the creator-audience counterpart. same render and publish rails, sourced from live bounties and opportunities instead of recipes. - `carousel-announce` — carousels from diary entries and ship notes, ai-written. use that when there is no recipe; use this when there is. - `iris how-to publish` — get the recipe live first. a carousel whose cta 404s is worse than no post. - `editorial-ad`, `freelabel-ads` — other remotion surfaces sharing the same brand tokens.

entries.name: import-preline-to-genesis-ui
entries.describe: Import Preline Pro templates into the Genesis composable page builder UI. Handles the full pipeline — extract HTML patterns from Preline, build Vue 3 components, register in useComponentMap, update validator schema, add to showcase page, commit/push to iris-api, and seed locally. Pass an action or component idea as argument.
entries.haystack: import-preline-to-genesis-ui import preline pro templates into the genesis composable page builder ui. handles the full pipeline — extract html patterns from preline, build vue 3 components, register in usecomponentmap, update validator schema, add to showcase page, commit/push to iris-api, and seed locally. pass an action or component idea as argument. --- name: import-preline-to-genesis-ui description: import preline pro templates into the genesis composable page builder ui. handles the full pipeline — extract html patterns from preline, build vue 3 components, register in usecomponentmap, update validator schema, add to showcase page, commit/push to iris-api, and seed locally. pass an action or component idea as argument. allowed-tools: -
