read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - agent --- # import preline to genesis ui — component pipeline import preline pro template patterns into the genesis composable page builder. build, register, validate, and deploy new vue 3 page builder components for the iris page system. components are rendered by iris-api and configured via json page definitions. ## arguments `$arguments` — action or component description. examples: - `/build-components list` — list all registered page builder components - `/build-components audit` — compare preline templates vs existing components, find gaps - `/build-components build "faq accordion with categories"` — build a new component from description - `/build-components from-preline "shop/product-detail.html"` — extract and build from a specific preline template - `/build-components showcase add testimonialssection` — add a component instance to the showcase page - `/build-components showcase seed` — seed the showcase page locally - `/build-components validate` — run validator on showcase page - `/build-components count` — count total registered components ## key paths | path | purpose | |------|---------| | `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/resources/js/components/pagebuilder/` | vue 3 component files | | `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/resources/js/composables/usecomponentmap.ts` | component registration (async imports) | | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/pagescommand.php` | validator schema (`getcomponentschema()` + `$arrayprops`) | | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/pages/component-showcase.json` | showcase page json | | `preline-pro-templates/pro/` | preline pro html templates (reference library) | | `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/config/page-components.yaml` | component catalog (yaml docs) | ## preline pro template library source templates at `preline-pro-templates/pro/`: | directory | contains | |-----------|----------| | `agency/` | services, careers, case studies, news, team (10 pages) | | `startup/` | features, pricing, about, customers (6 pages) | | `shop/` | product listing, detail, cart, checkout, compare (30+ pages) | | `coffee-shop/` | listings, product detail, bag, checkout, confirmation (6 pages) | | `dashboard/` | kanban, todo, chat, inbox, files, profiles, settings (22+ pages) | | `payment/` | balances, cards, send/request money, kyc verification (30+ pages) | | `personal/` | portfolio, reviews, work (3 pages) | | `crm/` | customers, tasks, search (10 pages) | | `analytics/` | visitors, incidents, survey (5 pages) | | `ai-chat/` | chat interface, explore (3 pages) | | `cms/` | posts, drafts, create post (5 pages) | | `project/` | project details, setup wizard (4 pages) | ## component architecture pattern every pagebuilder component must follow this exact structure: ### key conventions - **theme mode**: always `'light' | 'dark'` prop, default `'dark'` - **accent color**: resolves in order: prop → css variable `--primary-color` → fallback `#34d399` - **dark mode classes**: `thememode === 'dark' ? 'text-white' : 'text-gray-900'` - **section wrapper**: `class="xx-section py-20 px-4"` with conditional `bg-black`/`bg-white` - **container**: `max-w-5xl mx-auto` or `max-w-6xl mx-auto` - **accent application**: `:style="{ color: resolvedaccent }"` on highlighted elements - **no external dependencies**: pure tailwind css, no ui libraries - **scoped styles**: only when needed (animations, scrollbar hiding) - **never use `this.$toast`**: not applicable (vue 3 composition api) - **default accent**: `#34d399` (emerald green) — not purple/indigo ## full pipeline: building a new component ### step 1: research (if from preline) ### step 2: build the vue component follow the architecture pattern above. key rules: - typescript interfaces for all props - `withdefaults` for sensible defaults - accent color resolution pattern (copy exactly) - full dark/light mode support on every text/bg/border element - responsive: mobile-first with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:` breakpoints ### step 3: register in usecomponentmap.ts location: `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/resources/js/composables/usecomponentmap.ts` add before the closing `};` of the componentmap object. ### step 4: update validator schema in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/pagescommand.php`: 1. add to `getcomponentschema()` array: 2. if component has a required array prop, add to `$arrayprops`: ### step 5: add to showcase page ### step 6: seed locally local showcase page id: **62** (created 2026-03-29) ### step 7: commit & push iris-api deploys from `main` with `deploy_on_push: true` on digitalocean. ## production deployment notes - **iris-api** deploys from `main` branch (changed from `feature/heartbeat-lead-management` on 2026-03-29) - **app id**: `68ad4e37-3502-4681-8f28-9c5725044dce` - **instance size**: `apps-s-1vcpu-2gb` (bumped from 1gb on 2026-03-29 due to oom with 30+ async component chunks) - **build failures at 6/9**: usually oom during container startup. check `doctl apps list-deployments` and force rebuild if needed - **rollback detection**: if active deploy shows `cause: automated rollback`, the previous build failed and production is running old code ## common commands ## existing component inventory (as of 2026-03-29) ### from preline (34 components built today): timelinecarousel, imagebanner, bloggrid, scatteredimagehero, servicelisting, pricingrows, testimonialssection, teamsection, contactsection, comparisonmatrix, logomarquee, mapsection, careerslisting, featureshowcase, clientgrid, announcementbanner, beforeafter, servicemenu, portfoliogallery, vehiclecard, vehiclegrid, productcard, productgrid, fundingtiers, eventgrid, shoppingcart, newslettersignup, membershipcards, eventcalendar, stepwizard, fileupload, protectionpicker, orderconfirmation ### pre-existing (built before today): hero, jumbotronhero, marketinghero, feedhero, scatteredimagehero, sitenavigation, sitefooter, irisnavigation, section, textblock, imageblock, imagegallery, videoblock, quoteblock, splitcontent, editorialsection, editorialcomparison, featuregrid, featurecardsgrid, featureiconsgrid, featurecomparisontable, featuretabs, accordionfeatures, codeshowcase, scrollshowcase, pricingplans, comparisoncards, statscounter, statssection, logostrip, processsteps, gettingstartedsteps, buttoncta, communitycta, benefitssection, faqaccordion, enrollmentform, workflowtrigger, bookingwizard, bookingcalendar, survey, dashboardprovider, dashboardlayout, statcard, kpigrid, datachart, datatable, apexchart, activityfeed, progresstracker, kanbanboard, chatpanel, projecttimeline, and more (80+ total in usecomponentmap.ts)

entries.name: iris-agreements
entries.describe: Get an NDA or BAA signed and get the audit trail that proves it — raise it, issue it, watch it move through draft, sent, opened and executed, and know which ones are still outstanding without asking anyone. From nothing to a countersigned agreement in one sitting.
entries.haystack: iris-agreements get an nda or baa signed and get the audit trail that proves it — raise it, issue it, watch it move through draft, sent, opened and executed, and know which ones are still outstanding without asking anyone. from nothing to a countersigned agreement in one sitting. --- name: iris-agreements description: get an nda or baa signed and get the audit trail that proves it — raise it, issue it, watch it move through draft, sent, opened and executed, and know which ones are still outstanding without asking anyone. from nothing to a countersigned agreement in one sitting. version: 2 args: name: type: string required: true description: counterparty full name, as it should appear on the agreement email: type: string required: false description: counterparty email — required to actually issue it, optional if you only want a draft type: type: string required: false description: nda or baa (default nda). baa is for anything touching phi. subject: type: string required: false description: what this agreement gates, in a few words — this is what makes the list readable later on-error: continue timeout: 300 --- # iris agreements **what it is:** the product that turns "we should get an nda signed" into a signing link, a status you can query, and an audit trail that survives someone asking six months later. **what it is not:** a contract drafter or legal advice. it issues agreements from templates the business already stands behind — nda and baa. if you need bespoke terms, that is a lawyer, and then this issues what they wrote. **why it exists as a product rather than an email:** an agreement sent by email has no state. nobody can answer *has she signed it?* without searching an inbox, and *which agreements are outstanding?* is unanswerable. agreements gives every one of them a lifecycle — **draft → sent → opened → executed**, with **revoked** as a real terminal state — and makes the whole set queryable. ## the lifecycle, and the two states people get wrong draft ──issue──> sent ──they open it──> opened ──they sign──> executed │ │ └──────────────────── revoke ─────────────────────────────────┘ - **`sent` is not `opened`.** sent means we emailed a link. opened means a human loaded it. if something has sat at `sent` for a week, the email probably went to spam — that is a different problem from someone who opened it and hesitated, and it needs a different follow-up. - **`opened` is not `executed`.** only `executed` is signed. anything gating access on an agreement must check for `executed` and nothing weaker. - **`revoke` closes the access it authorised.** it is not a delete — the record and its trail stay, which is the entire point of having an audit trail. ## before you start you need the counterparty's **full name** and, to issue rather than just draft, their **email**. everything else has a default: `--type nda`, `--disclosing iris`, `--term "one year"`, and `--expires` derived from the term. **pick `--type baa` if anything the counterparty touches is phi.** that is not a formatting difference, it is a different legal instrument, and choosing wrong is the one mistake here that matters. use `--tier phi` alongside it when the agreement gates phi-scoped access. ## steps ### step:existing do we already have one with this person? ### step:outstanding what is already waiting on someone ### step:raise raise it ### step:issue issue it — this emails a real person **this sends an email to the counterparty.** it is a `mode: human` step for that reason: everything before it is reversible and this is not. - `iris agreements issue <id>` — emails the signing link check before you run it: - **is the email address right?** a signing link to the wrong address is a disclosure, not a typo. - **is the type right?** nda where a baa was needed cannot be fixed by sending a second one — the work will already have started under the wrong instrument. - **is the term right?** `--term` defaults to one year and quietly sets `--expires`. the same command re-sends, so a bounced or lost email is `issue` again, not a new agreement. ### step:watch watch it move, and read the state honestly ### step:gate wire access to `executed`, and nothing weaker only if this agreement gates access to something. **the check is `status == executed`.** not "we sent it", not "they opened it", not "it exists". this is the same failure that has appeared repeatedly in this codebase: a permission that reads as granted because a record exists, rather than because the thing it represents actually happened. for phi, `--tier phi` on the agreement and an `executed` status are both required. either alone is not access. ### step:done confirm, then record what it gates

entries.name: iris-atlas
entries.describe: Your data, queryable — the layer that owns its own schema. Reach a board, define a typed dataset on it, write a record, read it back with filters and aggregates, and share it without handing over your account. From nothing to a queryable dataset in one sitting.
entries.haystack: iris-atlas your data, queryable — the layer that owns its own schema. reach a board, define a typed dataset on it, write a record, read it back with filters and aggregates, and share it without handing over your account. from nothing to a queryable dataset in one sitting. --- name: iris-atlas description: your data, queryable — the layer that owns its own schema. reach a board, define a typed dataset on it, write a record, read it back with filters and aggregates, and share it without handing over your account. from nothing to a queryable dataset in one sitting. version: 2 args: board: type: string required: true description: bloq/board id (a number, e.g. 638) or its name — the container everything else hangs off schema: type: string required: false description: dataset schema slug to define or inspect, e.g. bid-history. lowercase, hyphenated. share_with: type: string required: false description: email address to grant board access to — used only in the sharing step on-error: continue timeout: 300 --- # iris atlas **what it is:** the data layer — one of only three iris products that genuinely owns its schema. 12+ tables in fl-api (`atlas_schemas`, `atlas_records`, `atlas_record_field_index`, plus ledger, inventory, staff, zone and graph tables), served at `v1/atlas/*` in `fl-api/routes/api.php` (groups at ~2702, 2725, 2754, 2759) by `app/http/controllers/atlas/` over `app/services/atlas/`. define a shape once, put rows in it, and every row is filterable, searchable, aggregatable and serveable over rest — no migration. **what it is not:** - **not a notes app.** boards, lists and items are the *prose* half and a different storage engine from datasets. confusing the two is the most expensive mistake here. - **not multi-tenant.** atlas authorizes on `user_id` equality on the atlas row; board membership is not consulted anywhere in the dataset code path. see "the trap" — a wall, not a nuance. - **not a local spreadsheet.** `iris atlas export` gets your data off the servers; the queryable copy lives in fl-api. ## the vocabulary, because nothing else writes it down bloq / board ──has──> list ──has──> item the prose engine │ (cards, files, markdown, agents) └──tags──> schema ──has──> record the data engine └──── "dataset" ────┘ (typed rows, filterable, aggregatable) - **bloq / board** (`user_bloqs`) — the container, and **the only thing that can be shared**. exactly one owner: `user_bloqs.user_id`. `iris atlas list · get · members · invite · open`. - **list** (`user_bloq_lists`, fk → `user_bloqs`) and **item** (`user_bloq_items`, fk → the *list*) — columns and cards: free text, markdown, uploads. **an item has no `bloq_id`**; you reach the board through the list, which is why every item command wants a *list* id. - **schema** (`atlas_schemas`) — a dataset *definition*: slug, version, typed fields. `bloq_id` is **nullable**, so a schema can be tagged to a board or float free on the account (62 exist here; many read `bloq:—`). uniqueness is `(bloq_id, slug, version)`. - **record** (`atlas_records`) — one row against a schema. `schema_id` is a real fk with **on delete cascade**: dropping a schema takes every record with it. - **dataset** — not a table. it is the *pair*: schema plus records. that is what `iris atlas:datasets` operates on and what `atlas:datasets api <slug>` serves over rest. **items and records are different tables.** the only bridge is `user_bloq_items.atlas_schema_id` (nullable, no fk), which lets a card point at a *schema* — never at a record. a number you want to average is a record; a paragraph someone reads is an item. there is no convert. ## the trap: `editor` is not write access `iris atlas members <board>` will show a person as `[editor]`. that permission lives in `user_bloq_users` and governs **the board/list/item half only**. a membership check does exist — `bloqaccessscope::mayaccessbloq()`, "owner plus shared users" — and `bloqitemcontroller`, `bloqlistcontroller` and the genesis gated controllers all call it. **`atlasdatasetcontroller` never does.** every method there resolves the actor from the token and filters `where('user_id', $userid)` on the atlas row; `bloq_id` is a filter column, never a permission input. - **11 of 15 dataset methods are strictly owner-only** (`authuserid`): `listschemas`, `showschema`, `createschema`, `updateschema`, `deleteschema`, `createrecord`, `updaterecord`, `destroyrecord`, `upsertrecord`, `import`, `derive`. a member's write **404s as "schema not found"**, not 403 — it reads as *missing data* rather than *denied*. that is **#183281**. - **only 4 read methods widen at all** (`readuserid`): `listrecords`, `showrecord`, `summary`, `aggregate` — and only for an **internal service token** passing `as_user_id`, never for a human member. `listschemas` is not among them, which is exactly why a member's schema list comes back empty rather than denied: **#183303**. both confirmed in code today. - agents inherit that asymmetry deliberately: `v6toolregistry::executeanalyzedataset` passes `as_user_id`, while `executeupsertdatasetrecords` is commented "deliberately not modelled on executeanalyzedataset's as_user_id impersonation." **rule until those close: datasets belong to whoever created the board.** share the *output* — a feed token, a public item, the rest endpoint — not the write seat. ## steps ### step:orient which boards you own, and reach the one you named `is_owner` appears **only in `--json`** — the pretty listing does not show it, so an owned board and a shared one look identical until you ask. `iris atlas get` takes an id **or a name** and honours membership, so it succeeding proves nothing about whether the dataset steps will. that split is what this step exists to establish. ### step:schemas what datasets already exist here slugs are unique per `(bloq_id, slug, version)`, **not globally** — the same slug can live on two boards. once it does, every records command demands `--bloq <id>`; until then it silently resolves to whichever it finds, printing `resolved '<slug>' -> schema #n`. read that line. ### step:define define the shape — this creates a real, versioned schema skip if `${{args.schema}}` already appeared above. otherwise: - `iris atlas:datasets schemas create --name "bid history" --slug bid-history --bloq ${{args.board}} --fields '{"fields":[{"key":"zone","type":"text","label":"zone"},{"key":"amount","type":"number","label":"bid"}]}'` — defines it - `iris atlas:datasets schemas show ${{args.schema}}` — read it back, with version and record count - `iris atlas:datasets schemas update ${{args.schema}}` — **evolves** fields into a new version and keeps existing records; not a destructive edit four things that cost a 422 or an afternoon: - **valid types are `text number money date datetime enum boolean url email phone array object reference`.** `string` is **not** one, and the failure is the unhelpful `invalid schema definition`. confusingly, older schemas on this account have `"type":"string"` stored — they predate `atlasschemavalidator::validateschema` and cannot be recreated as written. - **`--fields` takes `{"fields":[…]}`, a bare `[…]`, or a path to a `.json` file.** an `enum` field must carry `options`. - **omitting `--bloq` creates an account-global schema** (`bloq_id null`). legitimate — half of them here are — but it will not show under `schemas list --bloq <id>` and nobody browsing the board will find it. - **`schemas delete` is a soft delete that still holds the slug.** recreating that slug restores and overwrites the trashed row rather than colliding. delete is not a clean slate. ### step:write put one record in, read it back, and query it `--where` and `-q/--search` are both served from `atlas_record_field_index`, maintained on write by `atlasfieldindexer` — so a field you never declared in the schema is stored but **not** filterable. ### step:share hand out the data without handing out your account four things get called "sharing", in increasing order of what you give away. all are externally visible acts, which is why this is a human step. - `iris atlas:datasets feeds create -s ${{args.schema}} --label "<who>" --filter region=north` — a **read-only token scoped to one dataset**, optionally pinned to a slice callers cannot widen. **shown once.** `--force` required with no terminal. - `iris atlas:datasets api ${{args.schema}}` — the rest surface for whoever is integrating. the post body **must** be wrapped `{"data":{…},"external_id":"…"}`; a flat body fails. - `iris atlas make-public <item-id>` — publishes one **item** (prose, not a record) at a public url; `make-private` revokes it. - `iris atlas invite ${{args.board}}` — a **passwordless tokenized link to the whole board**; `iris atlas links` lists them, `iris atlas revoke-link <id> <linkid>` kills one. anyone holding that url is inside the board — revoke it, do not "rotate" by minting a second. before you run any of them: - **a feed token is a bearer credential in a chat message.** prefer it anyway — scoped to one dataset and revocable (`feeds revoke <id>`), which board membership is not. - **`iris atlas add-member ${{args.board}} --email <address-or-${{args.share_with}}> --permission editor` does not grant dataset writes.** re-read "the trap". if they must write records, today they own the board or you run the write for them. - **`--notify` is off by default in the cli and one-shot upstream** — mail fires only on a *new* share, so re-running later to notify silently just changes the permission. ### step:verify confirm what is actually there the sibling `atlas:*` namespaces — `inventory`, `ledger`, `staff`, `comms`, `meetings`, `brand-kit`, `projections`, `item` — are the same `user_id`-scoped storage with purpose-built shapes, and every caveat above applies to them unchanged.

entries.name: iris-cli
entries.describe: One command line for everything IRIS, so you're not hunting across five different tools to chat with an agent, check a lead, or read an email. Product names you already know — Genesis, ReachR, Pulse — just work as aliases, no separate manual to learn. Pass an action or topic as argument.
entries.haystack: iris-cli one command line for everything iris, so you're not hunting across five different tools to chat with an agent, check a lead, or read an email. product names you already know — genesis, reachr, pulse — just work as aliases, no separate manual to learn. pass an action or topic as argument. --- name: iris-cli description: one command line for everything iris, so you're not hunting across five different tools to chat with an agent, check a lead, or read an email. product names you already know — genesis, reachr, pulse — just work as aliases, no separate manual to learn. pass an action or topic as argument. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task --- # iris cli — agent development kit (adk) & sdk interact with the iris platform from the command line. two clis exist: - **`iris` (typescript, primary)** — installed at `~/.iris/bin/iris`, the main user-facing cli - **`php bin/iris` (php sdk, legacy)** — at `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris`, being sunsetted ## typescript iris cli — key commands (v1.1.19+) ### schedules (autonomous agent management) ### pages (genesis composable page builder) ### integrations ### playbooks — how they associate to entities playbooks are keyed by **name** (not fk). source of truth = `.iris/playbooks/<name>/playbook.md`; `iris playbook sync` projects each into `.claude/skills/<name>/skill.md` (auto-generated — never hand-edit the skill.md). they live in fl-iris-api `playbooks` table + local disk, not fl-api. the only persisted first-class link is **bloq → playbook name** in `bloqs.config.playbooks[]` (no migration). publish-scoping (private/project/public) is specced in `playbook-publish-associations-handoff.md` (#167269) — the `playbooks` table's nullable `user_id` + `scopeforuser` or-null currently leaks orphan playbooks to every user. ### searching what you've written (important — reach for this first) `iris search <query>` searches item **titles and content across every board you own**, plus board names. use it before asking where something lives — it is the answer to "did we already write this down?" both sections are always reported, including at zero — an empty "items (0)" means the phrase is genuinely absent, not that the capability is missing. ### bounty os — ledger checks without ssh `iris bounty admin` exposes the read-only reconciliation verbs that used to require `railway ssh -s fl-api -- php artisan bounty:invariants`. money-moving and attribution-rewriting commands stay artisan-only on purpose. ### sending communications — always through the router `iris imessage send` and `iris mail send` post to the comms router so the message lands in `lead_comms` with attribution. if the cli prints `not logged`, the message went out and the ledger does not know — report it, do not assume it was fine. never start the imessage bridge provider to test sending — it blasts auto-replies to real contacts (#137256). see the `comms-router` how-to for signatures and known bypasses. ### sender identities — who a message goes out as `iris senders` registers the identity a message signs and sends as. created unverified and draft-only until verified; nothing can sign as an identity that has not been established as yours. a sender with no binding for the channel refuses rather than sending from the default mailbox. delegated senders (writing on someone's behalf) are verbatim-only by default — a model may not write under that identity unless `metadata.allow_generated` is set deliberately. each sender carries its own channel order; with none set it uses the channels it is bound to, so a sender bound only to `email` is never routed onto `apple_mail` and then refused. `prefer` rejects a channel with no binding. note `default` picks the default identity, `prefer` picks that identity's transport. `--sender` needs a lead (or a handle that resolves to one) — the ad-hoc handle path bypasses the channel bindings, so a sender there is refused rather than signed-and-misdelivered. an unverified sender is a 422, never a quiet fallback. ### macos native — apple mail & imessage (important) when asked to read emails, check messages, or look up communications — use these first. they read directly from macos apps (apple mail, messages.app). no oauth, no api limits, full bodies. **when to use macos native vs gmail api integration:** - **macos native (iris mail)**: full email bodies, attachments visible, works offline, no api limits. use this first. - **gmail api (iris integrations exec gmail)**: only returns snippets (truncated). use only when macos mail.app doesn't have the account. ### health & monitoring ### agent-first heartbeat architecture (new) agents can now define their own mission, identity, and tools: - `settings.system_prompt` → overrides generic system prompt (agent identity) - `initial_prompt` → injected as `<agent_mission>` in goal (what to do) - `settings.heartbeat_tools` → filters available tools (e.g. `["manageleads", "agent_memory"]`) all fall back to defaults when empty. existing agents unchanged. --- ## php sdk cli (legacy — being sunsetted) ## arguments `$arguments` — action and target. examples: - `/iris-cli` — show help / available commands - `/iris-cli setup` — run interactive setup to configure credentials - `/iris-cli chat 11 "hello"` — chat with agent id 11 - `/iris-cli eval 387` — evaluate agent 387 with core test suite - `/iris-cli sdk agents.list` — list all agents - `/iris-cli sdk leads.search query=acme` — search leads - `/iris-cli sdk bloqs.uploadfile 40 /path/to/doc.pdf` — upload file to knowledge base - `/iris-cli new-command phonecommand` — read and explain an existing command - `/iris-cli add-command mycommand` — help create a new cli command --- ## cli location & configuration **cli binary:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris` **run from project root:** **or from anywhere using the full path:** **configuration (`.env` file in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/`):** --- ## commands reference ### run — unified tool & integration executor the `run` command is the universal entry point for executing any v6 system tool or integration function. **how it works:** the command automatically routes based on the target name: - `hive` → distributed compute (nodes, tasks, campaigns, dispatch) - known integration type (gmail, copycat-ai, servis-ai, whatsapp, etc.) → `integrationregistry` - everything else → `v6toolregistry` (system tools) **oauth flow:** `iris run --connect gmail` → gets oauth url from fl-api → opens browser → user authorizes → provider redirects back → fl-api stores tokens → `iris run --list-connected` shows it **hive flow (cloud dispatch):** `iris run hive dispatch type=whatsapp_scrape prompt="..."` → dispatches to connected hive node → daemon picks up task → executes playwright locally → returns result **hive flow (local script):** `iris hive script push ./report.sh` → pushes script to node → executes immediately → persists on disk. then `iris hive schedule add report.sh --cron "0 9 * * *"` → node runs it daily at 9am via local cron, even if cloud is offline **two dispatchers, same executor:** cloud scheduling (fl-api cron → pusher → daemon) and local scheduling (node-cron → daemon) both feed the same task executor. cloud for ai workflows. local for scripts that must run regardless. **parameter format:** `key=value` pairs. quotes for values with spaces: `query="austin, tx"` ### setup & config ### chat with agents ### agent evaluation (adk) the `eval` command is the core adk evaluation harness. it runs structured test scenarios against agents to validate performance, prompt quality, and configuration. **evaluation test types:** | type | description | |------|-------------| | `core` (default) | 7 built-in scenarios covering general capability | | `custom` | custom scenarios defined in the agent config | | `comparison` | a/b test with and without web search | ### sdk method calls (`sdk:call`) the `sdk:call` command is a dynamic proxy to any sdk resource and method. format: `resource.method [params]`. ### cloud upload (files, images, content) **full documentation**: see `sdk/php/docs/cloud_upload.md` or [freelabel.net/p/iris-cloud-upload]( ### outreach (strategies, campaigns, send) three commands manage the full outreach pipeline: strategy templates, campaigns, and per-lead execution. #### `outreach:strategy` — multi-step strategy templates **merge fields** (usable in step scripts): `{name}`, `{first_name}`, `{company}`, `{email}`, `{phone}`, `{instagram}`, `{social_handle}`, `{price_bid}`, `{notes}` **step types**: `instagram`, `email`, `sms`, `phone`, `linkedin`, `visit`, `other` **categories**: `cold_outreach`, `follow_up`, `nurture`, `high_value`, `quick_touch`, `custom` #### `outreach:campaign` — campaign lifecycle management **campaign types**: `one_time`, `recurring`, `drip`, `broadcast` **channels**: `email`, `sms`, `instagram_dm`, `linkedin`, `multi_channel` #### `outreach:send` — per-lead outreach actions ### leads / crm (`leads` or `crm`) full crm lead management with list, search, show, notes, and stats. **filters for `list`:** | option | description | |--------|-------------| | `--status=x` | filter by status (new, won, follow up, lost, in negotiation, prospected, etc.) | | `--search=x` | search by name/email/company | | `--bloq=x` | filter by bloq/board id | | `--sort=x` | sort field: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `price_bid` (default: `updated_at`) | | `--order=x` | sort order: `asc` or `desc` (default: `desc`) | | `--page=n` | page number (default: 1) | | `--limit=n` | results per page (default: 25) | for lower-level sdk operations (create, update, delete, sub-resources): ### page theming / brand colors when managing pages for different brands, set accent colors explicitly in the page json rather than relying on component defaults. key props: - **`accentcolor`** — used by statssection, featuretabs, featuregrid, servicelisting, editorialsection, communitycta, processsteps, timelinecarousel, gettingstartedsteps, pricingrows - **`labelcolor`** — used by hero, quoteblock (for small label text above headings) - **`ctacolor`** — used by sitenavigation (cta button color) component defaults (when no color is passed): emerald green (`#34d399` / `text-emerald-400`). always override for brand-specific pages. ### other commands ### pages (composable page builder) full page management via rest api. no ssh, no tty, no seeders. see `/pages` skill for complete docs. ### shared partials — `iris partials` shared component configs referenced by pages via `$partial`. edit one partial, all consuming pages update instantly. resolved server-side by `pagecontroller::resolvepartials()`. page json references a partial like: `{ "type": "sitenavigation", "$partial": "vanguard-nav", "props": {} }`. page-level props override partial defaults. see `/pages` skill for full docs. ### entity sync (typescript cli — `iris-code`) pull, push, and diff agents, workflows, leads, and board items as local json files. mirrors the pages pull/push/diff pattern. requires `iris_api_key` and `iris_user_id` env vars (or `iris auth login`). **local storage convention:** #### agents — `iris agents` #### workflows — `iris workflows` #### leads — `iris leads` #### boards (bloqitems) — `iris boards` #### opportunities — `iris opportunities` (alias: `iris opps`) #### services — `iris services` #### products — `iris products` #### events — `iris events` #### venues — `iris venues` (alias: `iris studios`) #### programs & packages — `iris programs` **source files:** `iris-code/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/platform-{agents,workflows,leads,boards,opportunities,services,products,events,venues,programs}.ts` ### opportunities (marketplace job postings) manage marketplace opportunities (gig postings, hiring, freelance jobs). full crud, json pull/push, bulk seed, publish lifecycle. ### packages (platform pricing) manage platform pricing packages with local json as source of truth. push changes to production without ssh. --- ## available commands (full list) | command | description | |---------|-------------| | `run` | **unified executor** — call any tool or integration: `iris run gmail search_emails query="test"`, `iris run searchplaces query="pizza"` | | **typescript cli (iris-code)** | **entity sync commands — pull/push/diff local json** | | `iris agents pull/push/diff <id>` | sync agents as `.iris/agents/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete, chat | | `iris workflows pull/push/diff <id>` | sync workflows as `.iris/workflows/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete, run, status | | `iris leads pull/push/diff <id>` | sync leads as `.iris/leads/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, search, create, update, delete, note | | `iris boards pull/push/diff <id>` | sync board items as `.iris/boards/{bloqid}/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris opportunities pull/push/diff <id>` | sync opportunities as `.iris/opportunities/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, delete | | `iris services pull/push/diff <id>` | sync services as `.iris/services/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris products pull/push/diff <id>` | sync products as `.iris/products/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris events pull/push/diff <id>` | sync events as `.iris/events/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris venues pull/push/diff <id>` | sync venues as `.iris/venues/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete. alias: `iris studios` | | `iris programs pull/push/diff <id>` | sync programs as `.iris/programs/{id}-{slug}.json` (includes packages) — also: list, get, create, update, delete, packages, package-create/update/delete | | `setup` | interactive credential setup (creates .env) | | `config` | manage stored credentials | | `chat` | chat with an ai agent (real-time progress) | | `eval` | evaluate agent performance with test scenarios | | `sdk:call` | dynamic proxy to any sdk resource.method | | `agent` | agent management (create, list, update) | | `agent:create` | create a new agent | | `app` | app-level operations | | `automation` | workflow automation management | | `automation:test` | test an automation workflow | | `bloq:ingest` | ingest files into a knowledge base | | `bloq:ingest-status` | check ingestion job status | | `bloq:ingestion-jobs` | list ingestion jobs for a bloq | | `bloq:cancel-ingestion` | cancel an ingestion job | | `cloud:upload` | upload files to cloud storage, get cdn + share urls ([full docs]( | | `bloqs:members` / `members` / `team` | manage bloq team members (overview, list, add, invite, update, remove) | | `monitor` | platform health monitoring and heartbeat diagnostics (overview, agent, loops, kill) | | `deliver` | deliver files/artifacts to leads | | `demo-showcase` | run a demo showcase | | `diary` | view/manage agent daily diary (today, list, view, add) | | `integrations` | manage platform integrations | | `leads` / `crm` | lead/crm management — list, show, search, notes, stats (filterable, paginated) | | `leads:consolidate` | consolidate duplicate leads | | `outreach:strategy` | manage outreach strategy templates (list, show, create, update, apply, duplicate, delete, metadata) | | `outreach:campaign` | campaign lifecycle management (list, show, create, start, pause, resume, cancel, schedule, analytics, recipients) | | `outreach:send` | per-lead outreach actions (list, show, vary, personalize, copy, open, complete, send, apply, invalid) | | `memory:add` / `memory:list` / `memory:show` / `memory:compose` | agent memory management | | `opportunities` | marketplace opportunities — list, view, create, pull, push, seed, publish, unpublish, delete, applications | | `packages` | platform pricing management — list, pull, push, diff, set (local json → production sync) | | `pages` | page builder cli (see `/pages` skill for full docs) | | `payments` | stripe payment history (read-only view) | | `invoices` | invoice management — create, checkout, send (list/create/show/checkout/send subcommands) | | `phone` | voice agent phone management | | `profile` | profile management — show, get/set (dot-notation), links, memberships | | `remind-r` | reminder system | | `schedule` | agent scheduling | | `servis-ai` | servis.ai strategic partner integration | | `skills` | platform skills management | | `sop` | standard operating procedure management | | `token` | api token management | | `tools` | tool registry inspection | | `users` | user management | | `v6:chat` | v6 react loop chat | | `voice` | voice configuration | | `wallet` | wallet and credit balance | --- ## sdk structure (php) **source:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/` --- ## node.js sdk **location:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/node/` **package:** `@iris-ai/sdk` **language:** typescript with full type safety --- ## iris code (opencode fork) the iris code terminal ai assistant is a separate tool: **location:** `iris-code/` **install:** **key agents (press tab to switch):** - `build` — full access for development - `plan` — read-only mode for analysis - `general` — complex searches with `@general` --- ## creating a new cli command when asked to add a new command to the iris cli: ### step 1: read an existing similar command for reference ### step 2: create the new command class follow this structure in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/mycommand.php`: ### step 3: register the command in application.php add to the `getdefaultcommands()` or `configure()` method: --- ## steps ### 1. parse the argument determine what the user wants: | argument | action | |----------|--------| | (empty) | show all available commands with descriptions | | `setup` | guide through running `php bin/iris setup` | | `chat <id> "<msg>"` | run the chat command, show output | | `eval <id>` | run agent evaluation | | `sdk <resource.method> [params]` | run sdk:call command | | `new-command <name>` | read and explain an existing command file | | `add-command <name>` | create a new command class + register it | | any other command name | run or explain that command | ### 2. run cli commands always use the full path. run from within the sdk directory context: **important**: the cli requires a `.env` file in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/`. if it doesn't exist, run `php bin/iris setup` first. ### 3. working with command output most commands support `--json` for machine-readable output. use this when processing results programmatically. ### 4. adding new sdk capabilities when asked to extend the sdk: 1. check existing resource classes in `src/resources/` 2. follow the existing pattern (constructor receives iris client, methods map to api endpoints) 3. add corresponding cli command in `src/console/commands/` 4. register in `src/console/application.php` --- ## key notes - **cli binary is php** — requires php in path (use docker if not installed locally) - **credentials**: stored in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/.env`, set via `php bin/iris setup` - **all commands support `--api-key` and `--user-id`** flags to override .env credentials - **`sdk:call` is the swiss army knife** — any sdk method is accessible via `resource.method` - **`eval` is the adk harness** — use it to validate agent quality before deploying to production - **node sdk** exists at `fl-docker-dev/sdk/node/` for typescript projects - **iris cli** (`iris-code/`) is the terminal ai coding assistant (typescript, built on opencode fork). branded "iris cli" everywhere — never "iris code" --- ## building & releasing the iris cli **repo:** `freelabel/iris-opencode` (git remote in `iris-code/`) ### branching strategy - **`dev`** — default branch. all work goes here. multiple sessions can push freely. - **`main`** — protected, releases only. requires a pr from `dev`. - never push directly to `main`. ### release flow ### local build (for testing) ### version bumping version lives in `packages/opencode/package.json`. bump it in the release commit: ### important - gh release titles must say **"iris cli"**, not "iris code" - the `--skip-install` flag avoids playwright-core resolution errors from root node_modules - build produces binaries for all platforms (linux, darwin, windows × arm64, x64) - **never force-push tags** — it corrupts github's release ordering and causes `iris update` to downgrade customers ### release emergency runbook #### `iris update` is downgrading customers **symptom**: customer runs `iris update` and goes from v1.3.63 → v1.3.52 (or any older version). **cause**: a force-pushed tag recreated an old github release, and github's `/releases/latest` api returns it based on creation timestamp, not semver. **fix**: **prevention**: never `git push --tags --force`. if you need to re-tag, delete the old tag first: #### customer gets `[1] killed iris` **symptom**: binary downloaded but macos kills it immediately on execution. **cause**: macos gatekeeper quarantine attribute (`com.apple.quarantine`) on downloaded binary. **fix (v1.3.64+)**: the installer now strips quarantine automatically via `xattr -cr`. **customer recovery** (if they're on an older version that can't self-update): this is the only fix they need. one command, no tech knowledge. do not ask them to run `xattr` manually. #### `iris --version` shows `0.0.0-dev-*` **cause**: a local `bun run build --single --install` overwrote the release binary with a dev build. **fix**: `iris update` or manually download the release binary: #### hotfix needed but pre-push hook blocks **symptom**: typescript errors in unrelated files block `git push origin main`. **fix**: for emergency hotfixes only: then immediately fix the ts errors and push a clean commit. do not leave `--no-verify` pushes as the last commit. #### ci builds but release doesn't appear **cause**: tag didn't trigger the workflow, or workflow failed. **fix**:

entries.name: iris-cli-roadmap
entries.describe: Manage the IRIS CLI roadmap — track parity between the canonical iris-cli (Node/opencode fork) and the PHP SDK CLI being sunsetted, decide where new features go, and run the migration. Pass an action as argument (status, gap, port, add, audit, sunset-check, naming).
entries.haystack: iris-cli-roadmap manage the iris cli roadmap — track parity between the canonical iris-cli (node/opencode fork) and the php sdk cli being sunsetted, decide where new features go, and run the migration. pass an action as argument (status, gap, port, add, audit, sunset-check, naming). --- name: iris-cli-roadmap description: manage the iris cli roadmap — track parity between the canonical iris-cli (node/opencode fork) and the php sdk cli being sunsetted, decide where new features go, and run the migration. pass an action as argument (status, gap, port, add, audit, sunset-check, naming). allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- # iris cli roadmap manages the migration of cli features from the **php sdk cli** (sunsetting) to **`iris-cli`** (the canonical node/opencode fork). tracks parity, prioritizes ports, routes new feature decisions, and gates the eventual removal of the php cli. ## ⚠️ naming — read this first, it is the entire point of this skill there has been confusion about which thing is called what. **lock these definitions in:** | name | what it actually is | lifecycle | repo path | |---|---|---|---| | **`iris-cli`** | node cli built on the opencode fork. **the canonical iris command line going forward.** | growing → permanent | `iris-code/packages/opencode/` (repo: `freelabel/iris-opencode`) | | **`php-sdk`** | php integration library + thin cli wrapper. the cli portion is **being sunsetted**; the sdk library stays forever. | cli shrinks to zero, sdk lives on | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/` | | **`node-sdk`** | typescript sdk library (no cli). | lives alongside php-sdk | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/node/` | **aliases that have caused confusion in the past:** - ❌ "iris-opencode" — internal nickname for the iris-cli source repo. don't use externally; it's just `iris-cli`. - ❌ "iris-cli (php)" — was an early name for the php sdk's bundled cli. officially this is now **`php-sdk` cli** or **php-sdk** for short. treat any reference to "iris-cli" without a qualifier as meaning the **node** one. - ❌ "v1 / v2" — was considered for naming the two clis. **rejected.** naming by purpose ages better than naming by version. there's no v1; there's `php-sdk` (sunset) and `iris-cli` (canonical). **strategic direction:** 1. build out `iris-cli` to feature parity with `php-sdk` cli 2. stop adding new features to `php-sdk` cli (defaults go to iris-cli) 3. when parity is reached + nobody is using `php-sdk` cli commands → delete the php cli portion entirely 4. `php-sdk` becomes pure sdk library, no cli binary **known follow-up (out of scope for this skill):** the existing `.claude/skills/iris-cli/skill.md` currently points at the php cli binary (`fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris`) and contradicts the naming above. it needs to be repointed at `iris-code/packages/opencode/bin/iris` once iris-cli reaches enough parity that pointing users at it won't strand them. track this in `parity.yaml` under `meta.followups`. --- ## arguments `$arguments` — action and optional target. examples: - `/iris-cli-roadmap` or `/iris-cli-roadmap status` — show current state of the migration - `/iris-cli-roadmap naming` — print the naming table above (for when someone is confused) - `/iris-cli-roadmap gap` — show what's in `php-sdk` cli that's missing from `iris-cli` - `/iris-cli-roadmap gap <command>` — detail on a specific gap - `/iris-cli-roadmap port <command>` — walk through porting a single command from php-sdk → iris-cli - `/iris-cli-roadmap add <feature>` — decision tree: where should this new feature go? - `/iris-cli-roadmap audit` — re-extract both clis' command lists and show diffs vs `parity.yaml` - `/iris-cli-roadmap sunset-check` — are we ready to delete the php cli? run the gate checklist. - `/iris-cli-roadmap parity-only-php` — list php-sdk-only commands (the gap) - `/iris-cli-roadmap parity-only-node` — list iris-cli-only commands (the lead) --- ## source files (where to read/write actual code) ### `iris-cli` (node — canonical) - **command directory:** `iris-code/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/` - **platform commands** (the ones that map to php-sdk cli features): files prefixed `platform-*.ts` - **native opencode commands** (coding agent stuff, not in scope for parity): `acp.ts`, `agent.ts`, `auth.ts`, `debug/`, `generate.ts`, `github.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `models.ts`, `run.ts`, `serve.ts`, `session.ts`, `transcribe.ts`, `tui/`, `web.ts`, `upgrade.ts`, `uninstall.ts`, `pr.ts`, `stats.ts`, `import.ts`, `export.ts` - **binary:** `iris-code/packages/opencode/bin/iris` (after build) or installed at `~/.iris/bin/iris` - **build:** `cd iris-code/packages/opencode && bun run build -- --single` then copy `dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/iris` to `~/.iris/bin/iris` - **repo:** `git@github.com:freelabel/iris-opencode.git` ### `php-sdk` cli (sunsetting) - **command directory:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/` - **naming convention:** `<name>command.php` - **binary:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris` - **run:** `php fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris <command>` or via the symlink at `~/.iris/sdk/bin/iris` ### parity matrix (this skill's source of truth) - **file:** `.claude/skills/iris-cli-roadmap/parity.yaml` - hand-curated. the `audit` action re-extracts both clis' command lists and reports what's drifted from the yaml, but does not auto-edit it. --- ## how each action works ### `status` — current state of the migration read `parity.yaml`. print: - total commands in php-sdk cli - total commands in iris-cli (platform-*) - how many are at parity (in both, or in iris-cli only) - how many are gaps (php-sdk-only, not yet ported) - the top 5 gaps marked `priority: high` in the yaml - last `audit` timestamp from `meta.last_audit` ### `naming` print the naming table from the top of this file. use this when anyone in the codebase or in conversation is confused about which thing is which. ### `gap` — what's in php-sdk cli but missing from iris-cli read `parity.yaml`. list all entries where `iris_cli: missing`. show: - command name (php-sdk side) - what it does (one-line `description` from the yaml) - priority (`high` / `medium` / `low`) - notes (any porting blockers, dependencies) if `<command>` argument provided, show the full entry for that command including `php_sdk_path` and any porting notes. ### `port <command>` — walk through porting one command for the given command name: 1. read `parity.yaml` entry for it. confirm it's marked `iris_cli: missing`. 2. read the php source file at `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/<name>command.php`. summarize: - what it does - which iris api endpoints it calls - required arguments / options - any auth/setup prerequisites 3. identify which iris-cli `platform-*.ts` file it should live in (existing file? new file?) 4. look at a similar existing iris-cli command for the structural template 5. write the new typescript command, register it in the appropriate root command's `.command()` chain 6. build iris-cli (`bun run build -- --single`), install to `~/.iris/bin/iris` 7. test it manually 8. update `parity.yaml`: change `iris_cli: missing` → `iris_cli: <new-file>.ts`, set `ported_at` to today's date 9. commit to `iris-opencode` with message `port <command> from php-sdk cli` ### `add <feature>` — decision tree for new features when someone wants to add a new cli feature, route them: 1. **default: add it to `iris-cli`.** always. 2. **exceptions where you'd add to `php-sdk` cli instead:** - the feature is *only* needed by an existing php sdk consumer who can't be migrated - the feature wraps a php-only library or workflow (extremely rare) - there's a hard deadline and porting it later is acceptable 3. **if both:** add to iris-cli first, then mirror to php-sdk cli as a thin wrapper that just calls the same fl-api endpoint. mark it in `parity.yaml` with `port_strategy: dual`. 4. **never:** add a feature to `php-sdk` cli that doesn't exist in iris-cli without first checking with the team. every such addition makes the sunset further away. when invoked, ask the user the 3 questions above and write a recommendation. ### `audit` — re-extract both clis' command lists run the `audit.sh` script in this skill folder: it outputs: - all `*command.php` files in php-sdk (normalized to lowercase command names) - all `platform-*.ts` files in iris-cli (normalized similarly) - diff vs `parity.yaml`: - **new in php-sdk** (added to php cli but not in yaml — should be either ported immediately or formally added to the gap list) - **new in iris-cli** (added to node but not in yaml — likely already-ported, update the yaml to reflect reality) - **vanished from php-sdk** (was in yaml, no longer in source — was it deleted? rename?) - **vanished from iris-cli** (was marked as ported, file gone — regression?) then prompt the user to update `parity.yaml` accordingly. ### `sunset-check` — are we ready to delete the php cli? run the gate checklist: 1. ✅ **parity reached:** `gap` returns zero entries marked `priority: high` or `medium` 2. ✅ **usage zero:** check fl-api logs for any api calls coming from php-sdk cli's user agent string in the last 30 days (`php-sdk-cli/*`). if any, list which users. 3. ✅ **docs updated:** all `docs/`, `readme.md`, and `claude.md` mentions of `iris-cli` referring to php have been updated to point at the node cli. grep for `bin/iris` and `php.*iris` patterns. 4. ✅ **existing iris-cli skill updated:** `.claude/skills/iris-cli/skill.md` repointed at the node binary. 5. ✅ **announcement sent:** check `parity.yaml.meta.sunset_announced_at` is set. 6. ✅ **composer package marked:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/composer.json` has `"deprecated-cli": true` or similar marker for one full release cycle. if all 6 are green, output the deletion plan. if any are red, list what's blocking. ### `parity-only-php` / `parity-only-node` quick filters on the yaml. the first lists everything that's only in php-sdk (the gap). the second lists everything that's only in iris-cli (features that exist on node but never existed on php — proves the migration isn't a regression). --- ## decision shortcuts (for quick chats with the user) **"should i add this command to iris-cli or the php one?"** → iris-cli. always. run `add <feature>` if you need the formal decision tree, but the default answer is iris-cli unless you can name a specific reason it can't go there. **"why does the iris-cli skill point at the php binary?"** → historical. the existing `.claude/skills/iris-cli/skill.md` was written when "iris-cli" meant the php one. it needs to be repointed once iris-cli is parity-complete. tracked in `parity.yaml.meta.followups`. **"how do i run the canonical iris-cli right now?"** → `iris <command>` (installed at `~/.iris/bin/iris` from the iris-opencode build). the php one is `php fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris <command>`. if both binaries exist on the user's path, the node one wins because of installer precedence. **"is the php cli dead?"** → not yet. it's the production tool today. it's being sunsetted gradually as iris-cli reaches parity. use it freely, but don't add new features to it without checking the parity matrix. --- ## files in this skill - `skill.md` — this file (entry point + naming definitions) - `parity.yaml` — the parity matrix (hand-curated, source of truth) - `audit.sh` — re-extracts both clis' command lists for diffing against the yaml ## verification after any action that updates `parity.yaml`, run `audit` to confirm the yaml still matches reality. if the audit reports drift, fix the yaml before proceeding.

entries.name: iris-discord-agents
entries.describe: Manage, debug, and maintain Discord bot agents connected to the IRIS V6 engine. Covers bridge config, workflow_channels, agent selection, deployment, and production debugging. Pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "debug", "add-bot", "update-agent").
entries.haystack: iris-discord-agents manage, debug, and maintain discord bot agents connected to the iris v6 engine. covers bridge config, workflow_channels, agent selection, deployment, and production debugging. pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "debug", "add-bot", "update-agent"). --- name: iris-discord-agents description: manage, debug, and maintain discord bot agents connected to the iris v6 engine. covers bridge config, workflow_channels, agent selection, deployment, and production debugging. pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "debug", "add-bot", "update-agent"). allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task --- # iris discord agents — setup, debugging & maintenance manage discord bots that connect to the iris v6 engine via the coding-agent-bridge. ## arguments `$arguments` — action to perform. examples: - `/iris-discord-agents status` — check bridge health, bot connections, and recent logs - `/iris-discord-agents debug` — investigate why the bot isn't responding - `/iris-discord-agents add-bot <bloq_id>` — wire up a new discord bot for a bloq - `/iris-discord-agents update-agent <agent_id> <model>` — change which model an agent uses - `/iris-discord-agents deploy` — sync bridge code to droplet and restart - `/iris-discord-agents logs` — tail production logs (bridge + iris-api worker) --- ## architecture overview ### two routing modes | mode | trigger | agent used | scope | |------|---------|------------|-------| | **god mode** | dm to bot (no guild_id) | user's general agent (`user->generalagent()`) | full cross-bloq access | | **project mode** | @mention in server | agent from `workflow_channels.agent_id` | bloq-scoped only | --- ## key infrastructure ### bridge (droplet) - **location**: `fl-web-prod` droplet at `134.199.214.232` - **code**: `/opt/coding-agent-bridge/production.js` - **config**: `/opt/coding-agent-bridge/.env` - **process manager**: pm2 (`pm2 list`, `pm2 logs coding-agent-bridge`) - **source**: `fl-docker-dev/coding-agent-bridge/production.js` **key env vars:** ### resilience (3 layers) 1. **pm2 auto-restart** — restarts on crash (built-in) 2. **systemd pm2-root.service** — restarts pm2 on server reboot 3. **cron health check** — `*/5 * * * * curl -sf > /dev/null || pm2 restart coding-agent-bridge` ### iris-api (v6 engine) - **app id**: `68ad4e37-3502-4681-8f28-9c5725044dce` - **branch**: `beta/heartbeat-groundhog` (deploy_on_push: true) - **worker**: `fl-iris-worker` (processes async queue jobs) ### database tables - **`iris_db.workflow_channels`** — maps discord servers/dms to bloqs/agents with bot credentials - **`freelabelnet.bloq_agents`** — agent configs including model (stored in `config` json as `$.model`) --- ## common operations ### check status ### deploy bridge code changes ### deploy iris-api changes ### change agent model **supported models for discord agents:** - `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning` — xai grok (recommended, fast with reasoning) - `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning` — xai grok (faster, no reasoning) - `gpt-4o` — openai (caution: production key may be exhausted) - `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` — google gemini (automatic fallback if openai fails) ### add a new discord bot for a bloq ### remove a discord bot --- ## debugging guide ### bot not responding at all 1. **check bridge health:** - is `messaging.discord.status` = "running"? - is the bot `ready: true`? 2. **check bridge logs for forward errors:** - `unexpected token '<'` = bridge pointing at frontend url, not api - `forward error` = iris-api endpoint unreachable or returning errors 3. **check iris-api logs:** - `skip_reason: "not_mentioned"` = bot @mention format mismatch (check bot_id in workflow_channels config) - `channel not found` = no workflow_channels record for this guild_id - `500` responses = check for php exceptions in the log ### bot accepts message but no reply 1. **check worker logs for job failures:** 2. **common failures:** - `serializesmodels` crash = virtual channel without db id (must use firstorcreate) - `unknown named parameter` = reactloopservice signature mismatch - `class not found` = missing model class (wrap in try/catch) - `failed to read fastcgi header` = http timeout (sync processing took too long — must use async queue) 3. **check the ai is responding:** - `openai quota exhausted` = key dead, falling back to gemini - `making chat request` with correct model = ai is being called - `execution complete` with `response_length > 0` = ai responded 4. **check discord api response sending:** - if missing: bot_token may be wrong or discord api rejecting the message ### bot responds but wrong agent - **dms** always route to `user->generalagent()` (god mode). to change which agent handles dms, update the general agent's config/model. - **server @mentions** use the agent from `workflow_channels.agent_id`. check: ### bot responds but wrong model check the agent's model in the config json: the v6aiservice model resolution chain: 1. agent's `config.model` → used directly 2. if openai model + quota exhausted → falls back to `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` 3. grok models (`grok-*`) → routed to ` via `xai_api_key` --- ## key files ### bridge (node.js) | file | purpose | |------|---------| | `fl-docker-dev/coding-agent-bridge/production.js` | main bridge — discord gateway connection, message forwarding, history fetching | | `/opt/coding-agent-bridge/.env` (droplet) | runtime config — api urls, bot tokens, bloq ids | ### iris-api (php/laravel) | file | purpose | |------|---------| | `app/http/controllers/v6/unifiedchannelcontroller.php` | entry point — detects channel type, finds workflow_channels record, dispatches job | | `app/services/v6/channels/adapters/discordadapter.php` | parses discord payloads, sends responses via discord rest api | | `app/services/v6/channels/channelmessagerouter.php` | god mode vs project mode routing, onevent progress callbacks | | `app/services/v6/channels/parsedmessage.php` | value object for parsed messages | | `app/jobs/processchannelmessage.php` | async queue job — calls router + sends response | | `app/services/v6/reactloopservice.php` | core ai execution — tool calling, rag, conversation history | | `app/services/v6/v6aiservice.php` | ai provider routing — openai, grok (xai), gemini fallback | ### database | table | db | purpose | |-------|----|---------| | `workflow_channels` | `iris_db` | discord server/dm → bloq/agent mapping with bot_token | | `bloq_agents` | `freelabelnet` | agent configs including model (`config->$.model`) | --- ## progress updates (tool call visibility) the bot posts progress messages to discord as it works: this is powered by the `onevent` callback in `channelmessagerouter::makediscordprogresscallback()`. tool emoji mappings: | tool | emoji | |------|-------| | managebloqitemstool | 📋 | | searchknowledgebasetool | 🔍 | | activitylog | 📅 | | workflow-composer | ⚙️ | | composepage | 🎨 | | agent_memory | 🧠 | | httprequest | 🌐 | | marketplacepurchasetool | 🛒 | --- ## production database access --- ## current bot inventory | bot | discord user | bloq | agent | model | server | |-----|-------------|------|-------|-------|--------| | iris ai#8500 | `1466253034584670464` | 38 | 473 (dj ghost, server) / 69 (general, dms) | `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning` | freelabel (`872124790876549170`) | --- ## known issues & workarounds 1. **externalaccount model not found** — warning on every dm (non-fatal). the `externalaccounts` relationship on user references a model that doesn't exist. caught by try/catch, falls back to channel owner. 2. **openai quota exhausted** — production openai key is dead. agents using `gpt-4o` fall back to `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`. use grok models to avoid this entirely. 3. **billing tracking 401** — `fl_raichu_api_token` in iris-api is expired. ai usage isn't tracked for billing. needs a fresh passport token from fl-api. 4. **bloqrag/searchknowledgebasetool 429** — uses openai embeddings which also fail with the dead key. rag search returns errors but the agent continues with other tools. 5. **no ui for discord agent management** — `workflow_channels` mapping is db-only. no frontend settings page exists yet for linking discord servers to bloqs/agents.

entries.name: iris-genesis
entries.describe: Ship a page on IRIS Genesis from nothing — pick the lane, create it, edit it, prove it renders, and control who can reach it. The path that ends in a URL a stranger can open, and the four states along it that look alike and are not.
entries.haystack: iris-genesis ship a page on iris genesis from nothing — pick the lane, create it, edit it, prove it renders, and control who can reach it. the path that ends in a url a stranger can open, and the four states along it that look alike and are not. --- name: iris-genesis description: ship a page on iris genesis from nothing — pick the lane, create it, edit it, prove it renders, and control who can reach it. the path that ends in a url a stranger can open, and the four states along it that look alike and are not. version: 2 args: slug: type: string required: true description: the page slug — lowercase, hyphenated, e.g. `atlas-console-v4`. it is the url and the identity; every command takes it, never a file path. title: type: string required: false description: page title, used only when creating. defaults to the slug. expect: type: string required: false description: a phrase that must appear in the rendered text — this is what proves the page works. leave it empty and the verify step shows you what to pass. on-error: continue timeout: 600 --- # iris genesis — from nothing to a page a stranger can open **what it is:** the page system — composable pages, sites, and a stored **component library**. `iris genesis` and `iris pages` are the same command group. it owns `pages`, `page_versions`, `page_sites`, `page_partials`, `page_views`, `page_analytics` and `page_share_links`, plus `code_components` / `code_component_versions` behind the library. **what it is not: a static site generator.** a page is a **json document in a database**, rendered on request and **cached**. no build, and no file that is the truth — `./pages/<slug>.json` is a working copy. nor is it git: `versions` and `rollback` exist, but there is no branch, no merge, and `pull` overwrites local edits without asking. ## the two lanes — choose before writing a line composable standalone (render_mode: "html") json_content.components: [...] json_content: raw css + html platform components, props, slots your own document, your own css inherits the genesis shell + theme inherits nothing genesis create / push genesis publish-html --file x.html verify --lane composable verify --lane bespoke not two styles of one thing — moving between them is a rewrite. assert which renderer served the request with `verify --lane`; a page that fell back to the wrong lane still renders *something*. ## four states that look alike exists ──> published ──> reachable ──> rendering what you wrote │ │ │ └─ the cache was purged │ │ └─ visibility public/unlisted, no otp gate │ └─ status == published (`create` already did this) └─ a row with a slug - **`create` publishes.** no draft on the way in: it returns `status: published`, `visibility: public`, and a stranger gets http 200 immediately. verified 2026-09-02. - **`push` un-publishes.** pushing local json to a **live** page drops it to `draft` and the url starts returning **404**. `--publish` is what you wanted, every time. - **published is not rendering your change.** `set` edits the record; the cache keeps serving the old render, and nothing in the output distinguishes the two. - **404 does not mean broken.** draft, `private`, and a nonexistent slug 404 identically — `check-public` is the only command that says what a stranger actually gets. ## steps ### step:surface what already exists under this name a local file **older than the remote** is the trap: `push` sends it and quietly reverts someone's work. `diff` before any push — `push --force` exists because stale shadows happened (#181601). ### step:create pick the lane, then create it — this is a publish **composable** if the page assembles platform components and should inherit the shell and theme; **standalone** if it is a document whose typography the shell must not touch. two component surfaces, easily confused: `component-registry` lists the ~239 **built-in** types from the api, `library list` the **stored** library published from `.vue` files. **`create` makes the page world-readable and indexable the moment it returns** — no draft on the way in, and no `--draft` flag. that is why this step is human. - `iris genesis create --slug <slug> --title "<title>"` — creates and publishes - `iris genesis unpublish <slug>` — run immediately if you did not want it public yet - `iris genesis duplicate <source> --slug <new>` — start from a page that already works - `iris genesis publish-html <slug> --file ./x.html --dry-run` — standalone lane, reads only before you run any of them: - **score the design standard first.** `iris how-to view genesis-design-standard` — 9–10 ship · 6–8 revise · 0–5 redesign. check 01 predicts the rest: *could this design move to a different subject unchanged?* if yes it is a template, ≤4, and only a restart rescues it. and no webfont cdns — the csp blocks them and it silently falls back to arial. - **is the slug the url you want forever?** renaming means a new page and a dead link. - **is anything here not for the public?** client names, prices, phi, an internal roadmap. - **`--owner-type`/`--owner-id` default to `bloq`/`38`** — set them now for a client workspace. - **`publish-html` discards the document skeleton**, splitting the file into `css` and `html`; check the dry run's byte counts, and use `--no-publish` to land it as a draft. ### step:state read the real state, then pick an edit path ### step:push push — this takes a live page offline skip to `step:verify` if you edited with `set`. **a plain `push` on a published page returns "pushed → draft" and the public url starts 404ing.** confirmed 2026-09-02: `published` → `draft`, `check-public` 200 → 404, and the only signal was the word "draft" inside a success message. if a push took the page dark, the fix is `iris genesis publish <slug>`, not another push. - `iris genesis diff <slug>` — always, first - `iris genesis push <slug> --publish` — the one you want on anything already live - `iris genesis push <slug>` — draft-only; correct when staging for review - `iris genesis preview <slug>` — a logged-out link that works while unpublished, **expiring on the next save** - `iris genesis push <slug> --live` — skips draft; the help calls it dangerous, believe it ### step:verify purge the cache, then prove it renders **cache-clear first, always** — equally required after a `visibility` or `requires_auth` change. this is where "i changed it and nothing happened" comes from: the record updated, the cache answered, both worked correctly, and the page is wrong. **`verify` matches rendered text, not html.** an id, class or `data-` attribute **will not match** — measured: `--expect "…-hero"` failed against a page whose dom contained `id="…-hero"`. it exits **1** on failure, which makes it scriptable; on a draft it exits 1 too, correctly diagnosing the 404. also worth passing: `--lane composable|bespoke`, `--min-words` (an empty render that returned 200), `--not-expect` (placeholder text that shipped). ### step:reach who can reach it, and what a component change reaches `published` and `visibility` are separate axes and people collapse them. every change below needs `iris genesis cache-clear <slug>` after it or nothing changes. - `iris genesis visibility <slug>` — reads it, and prints every url that currently works - `iris genesis visibility <slug> unlisted` — `/p/` still works, just not discoverable - `iris genesis visibility <slug> private` — **takes the `/p/` urls away entirely**, dead not delisted, leaving share links as the only way in - `iris genesis preview <slug>` — a logged-out link for one person; **dies on the next save** - `iris genesis share <slug>` — a `/s/{token}` capability link, works while unpublished, **lives forever until revoked**: no login, no allowlist, forwarded means shared. audit and kill with `share:list <slug>` / `share:revoke <token>`. - `iris genesis ungate <slug>` — lifts a `requires_auth` gate, clearing both flags in the order that works and then purging; by hand it does not stick **and if you are touching the library rather than one page: `iris genesis library publish <slug>` changes every live page naming that component immediately** — no push, no publish, no cache-clear on those pages. run `iris genesis library usage <slug>` first; it names the consumers and prints "republishing this component changes n page(s) immediately." adding a required prop to a component with three consumers is a breaking change to three pages that will not tell you they broke. `library show` reads its declared api, `library rollback` restores a version and is itself undoable. ### step:done what is true, and what does not behave as documented

entries.name: iris-heartbeat
entries.describe: Hand an agent a project instead of a task. Give it a schedule, a diary it reads before it acts, and a mode that decides how much it may do on its own — then read the fleet honestly enough to tell a working agent from one that has been dark for four months.
entries.haystack: iris-heartbeat hand an agent a project instead of a task. give it a schedule, a diary it reads before it acts, and a mode that decides how much it may do on its own — then read the fleet honestly enough to tell a working agent from one that has been dark for four months. --- name: iris-heartbeat description: hand an agent a project instead of a task. give it a schedule, a diary it reads before it acts, and a mode that decides how much it may do on its own — then read the fleet honestly enough to tell a working agent from one that has been dark for four months. version: 2 args: agent: type: string required: false description: agent id to inspect or configure. omit to work the whole fleet. mode: type: string required: false description: heartbeat mode to set — off, passive, reactive, autonomous, briefing, co-pilot. omit to only read. hours: type: string required: false description: window in hours for the fleet views (default 24). widen it before concluding anything is quiet. on-error: continue timeout: 300 --- # iris heartbeat **what it is:** autonomous agent scheduling with continuity. an agent wakes on a cadence, reads the diary of what the last wake did, looks at the project as it stands now, acts with full tool access, and writes the entry its successor will read. sold standalone as `iris-heartbeat-monthly`, $149/mo, compute class *heavy* — the price of a thing that thinks unattended. **what it is not: a cron.** a cron re-runs a command. heartbeat's product is the *diary* — what makes wake #40 aware of wake #39. strip that out and you have the scheduler iris already had. **nor is it pulse** ($99/mo, `iris-pulse-monthly`), which scores relationships and accounts. two skus, two subjects, one unfortunate word. ## the name collision — the single biggest trap here **`iris heartbeat` is not this product.** it hits `/api/v1/users/{id}/heartbeat` → `clientreadinessservice::foruserheartbeat()`, a **filtered subset of pulse's signal registry**; `iris heartbeat signals` prints two columns headed `pulse (agency)` and `heartbeat (you)`. one registry, two audience flags, nothing to do with agents. **this product's command is `iris monitor`** (`/api/v6/agents/heartbeat-status`), plus `iris schedules`, `iris agents update`, `iris diary`. `iris health` reaches only one of `doctor`/`monitor`/`heartbeat` — a ratcheted collision in `command-collisions.test.ts`. the word means a *third* thing in `fl-iris-api` (compute-node check-ins), which is why `routes/console.php` named its scheduler check `liveness` instead. ## the six modes off excluded from every fleet view. the only mode that means "not running". passive observes and records. no action. reactive acts when something happens to the project, not on a clock. briefing read-only morning digest — inbox, calendar, project — synthesised and sent. co-pilot decides, then files a task for a human to approve before anything executes. autonomous acts. full tool access, no approval gate. **`co-pilot` exists in the database and cannot be set from the cli.** the enum was widened by `2026_05_26_000001_add_copilot_mode_and_workflow_to_heartbeat.php`; `platform-agents.ts` still lists five choices and rejects the sixth, though four production agents run it. until that catches up, set it via `put /api/v1/bloqs/agents/{id}/heartbeat`. ## the states everyone misreads - **`last_heartbeat_at: null` is not broken.** `briefing` and `reactive` never stamp it — null is their normal steady state. reading null as dead condemns seven healthy agents. - **a mode is a setting, not a pulse.** `autonomous` with a four-month-old `last_heartbeat_at` is the #179799 failure: jobs due on time, skipped on time, output zero. reads *configured*, is *dark*. - **heartbeat has no cron of its own, on purpose.** it rides `agents:process-jobs --sync --limit=50` every minute, same pipeline as every other agent job. `kernel.php` calls it "the canary": if heartbeats stop, agent scheduling is broken, and a private cron would have hidden that. - **`due_within_30min` includes long-overdue jobs** — "due soon *or* past due". read the timestamp. - **the 2-hour staleness threshold is `health:check`'s, not the agent's.** anything legitimately on `every_8_hours` trips it six times a day. the breaker window is 7 days. ## steps ### step:fleet read the fleet, then split it by whether anything actually ran ### step:read sort the quiet ones — no command does this for you every agent in the dark list is one of three things, needing opposite responses. - **finished.** a campaign agent whose campaign ended. correct state is `off`, not dark — `iris agents update <id> --heartbeat-mode off`. left on, it inflates every alert count. - **starved.** its schedule is paused, failed, or its owner bloq went away. look at the schedules, not the agent: `iris monitor agent <id>`. - **broken.** dispatch is failing. look for `consecutive_failures` and a tripped breaker; `iris agents update <id> --reset-health` clears it once you know why. **do not widen cadence to make a quiet agent look busier.** it burns compute against a fault still there — one heartbeat schedule ran 70 times in two weeks, spent ~3.5m tokens, wrote zero rows. ### step:agent one agent — its schedules, then its diary ### step:mode set the mode — this decides how much it may do unsupervised **`autonomous` grants full tool access on a clock with no approval gate** — a real capability pointed at real accounts, which is why this step is not a script. - `iris agents update <id> --heartbeat-mode passive` — observes, records, acts on nothing - `iris agents update <id> --heartbeat-mode briefing` — read-only digest; safest useful mode - `iris agents update <id> --heartbeat-mode autonomous` — acts, unattended - `iris monitor briefing --agent-id <id> --time 08:00` — briefing with a delivery time - `co-pilot` is **not settable here** — the cli choices omit it; use the api route before autonomous, confirm all three: **the mission is bounded** (`--initial-prompt` runs *every* wake — a vague one re-decides the goal and drifts); **tools are an allowlist** (`--heartbeat-tools`, `config.tools` — otherwise it inherits whatever is enabled);
