entries.describe: Fix Light Mode — Elon Web UI Component
entries.haystack: fix-light-mode fix light mode — elon web ui component <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: fix-light-mode description: fix hardcoded dark-mode tailwind classes in vue components so they render correctly in light mode. pass a file path or component name as argument. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run fix-light-mode ` # fix light mode — elon web ui component fix a vue component so it properly supports light mode by replacing hardcoded dark tailwind classes with dynamic `islightmode` ternaries. ## arguments `$arguments` — path to a vue file or component name to fix. if a component name is given, search `fl-docker-dev/fl-elon-web-ui/components/` for it. ## reference read the full guide at: `fl-docker-dev/fl-elon-web-ui/docs/light_mode_fix_guide.md` ## steps ### 1. read the target file read the full contents of the component specified in `$arguments`. if only a name is given, use glob to find it under `fl-docker-dev/fl-elon-web-ui/components/`. ### 2. audit for hardcoded dark classes look for these patterns in the template section: - `bg-gray-800`, `bg-gray-900`, `bg-gray-700` — dark backgrounds - `text-white`, `text-gray-100`, `text-gray-300` — light text that won't show on white - `border-gray-700`, `border-gray-600` — dark borders - `hover:bg-gray-700`, `hover:bg-gray-600` — dark hover states - `bg-gradient-to-br from-gray-800 to-gray-900` — dark gradients - `placeholder-gray-500` on dark bg check if these are already inside `:class` ternaries using `islightmode`. if they are, skip them. only fix hardcoded (non-conditional) dark classes. ### 3. check for existing `islightmode` look in the `computed` section of the script block. **if it exists and uses `domainnavigationservice.ispathwaysdomain()`** — replace it with the themeservice pattern: **if it exists and already uses themeservice** — leave it as-is. **if it doesn't exist** — add it to the `computed` block. **if the component uses `effectivelightmode` (like agentgallery)** — fix the fallback detection to use themeservice instead of `ispathwaysdomain()`. ### 4. replace hardcoded classes with ternaries use these mappings: | dark class | light equivalent | |---|---| | `bg-gray-800` | `bg-white` | | `bg-gray-900` | `bg-gray-50` | | `bg-gray-700` | `bg-gray-100` | | `bg-gradient-to-br from-gray-800 to-gray-900` | `bg-white border border-gray-200` | | `bg-gradient-to-br from-gray-900 via-gray-800 to-gray-900` | `bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-50 to-purple-50` | | `text-white` | `text-gray-900` | | `text-gray-100` | `text-gray-900` | | `text-gray-300` | `text-gray-600` | | `text-gray-400` | `text-gray-500` | | `border-gray-700` | `border-gray-200` | | `border-gray-600` | `border-gray-300` | | `hover:bg-gray-700` | `hover:bg-gray-100` | | `hover:bg-gray-600` | `hover:bg-gray-200` | | `hover:text-gray-300` | `hover:text-gray-700` | | `bg-blue-600 bg-opacity-30` | `bg-blue-100` | | `bg-red-900 bg-opacity-30` | `bg-red-100` | **template pattern — static to dynamic:** before: after (split static/dynamic): keep non-theme classes (flex, padding, margin, width, etc.) in the static `class` attribute. move only theme-dependent classes into `:class`. ### 5. remove unused imports if you replaced `domainnavigationservice.ispathwaysdomain()` usage and nothing else in the file uses it, remove: ### 6. run eslint fix after all edits, run: ### 7. verify re-read the file briefly to confirm: - no duplicate `islightmode` computed properties - no unused imports - all previously hardcoded dark classes now have light alternatives - eslint passes clean ## important notes - **never use `this.$toast`** — use the messagesutility mixin from `utils/mixins/messages.js` - **use `$api` not `$axios`** for authenticated api calls - **nuxt 2 / vue 2 only** — use options api, not composition api - if a child component needs light mode awareness, prefer passing `:is-light-mode="islightmode"` as a prop - some components may have too many elements to ternary — consider `:global(.theme-light)` css overrides instead (see `workspacetoolslist.vue` for an example)

entries.name: fleet-intake
entries.describe: Fleet intake
entries.haystack: fleet-intake fleet intake --- name: fleet-intake description: get a vehicle into a rental fleet so it is bookable, attributable and visible — vin, owner, rate, and a photograph of the right car. includes the verified photo library and the four gates it took to stop showing customers the wrong vehicle, because each check we added let through something that satisfied more checks than the last failure did --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run fleet-intake ` # fleet intake the process for putting one vehicle into a rental fleet correctly. written 2026-09-01 out of catodrive, where 104 vehicles were added without one. what that cost, measured rather than remembered: **37 cars with no owner on file**, **43 vins that will not decode**, **101 with no photograph**, **zero owner emails**, and a second abandoned inventory of 75 title-only rows on a different board. every one of those is cheap at intake and expensive in bulk. two of those are now fixed, and the fix took a day rather than the minute it would have cost at intake: vin decoding is at 91 of 100 and every vehicle has a generation-matched photograph. the steps below carry what that took. owner attribution is still open. ## the rule **a vehicle is not in the fleet when the row exists. it is in the fleet when it can be booked, attributed and seen.** those are three different checks and the row passes none of them by default. ## steps ### 1 · capture what only the handover can give you ask for these while the car and its owner are in front of you. everything else is derivable. | field | why it cannot wait | |---|---| | `vin` | 17 characters, and the only source of the specs. wrong now = undecodable forever | | `plate` | how operations identifies the car on the road | | `owner` | who gets paid | | `owner_email` | who can sign in and see it — a name is not an identity | | `rate_cents` | what it earns. no rate = the charge gate cannot price it | if the whole fleet shares one price, set it once as the page default instead of per row: `php artisan fleet:default-rate {{app}} --set=65`. **type the vin, do not read it aloud.** two catodrive vins contain the letter `o` where a zero belongs, which is a transcription error that survives every later check and simply fails to decode. ### 2 · decode the vin into specs php artisan fleet:decode-vin {{app}} --dry-run # see what would change php artisan fleet:decode-vin {{app}} fills body class, fuel, drivetrain, doors, seats, transmission from the vin. idempotent — re-running reports "already complete" and changes nothing. if it does not decode, the vin is wrong. fix it now. a vehicle with no body class shows a generic placeholder and cannot be filtered by type. #### recovering a fleet that was already imported badly catodrive arrived with 43 of 103 rows undecodable. broken down, that is a different problem in each third, and only the first is hopeless: | cause | count | recoverable | |---|---|---| | no vin at all | 35 | only from a sibling, or by asking the owner | | contains `i`, `o` or `q` | 6 | yes — the standard excludes those letters | | 18 characters | 2 | sometimes — a doubled character | php artisan fleet:decode-vin {{app}} --dry-run --repair-vin --infer-siblings php artisan fleet:decode-vin {{app}} --repair-vin --infer-siblings `--repair-vin` retries the transcription-damaged ones. **it only keeps a repair when vpic's answer agrees with the make and model already on the row** — and that cross-check is the whole thing. without it this is a machine that invents plausible vins: every substitution decodes to *something*, and the wrong something is indistinguishable from the right one. the original is kept as `vin_original`. `--infer-siblings` fills `body_class` from another vehicle of the same make and model whose vin did decode. a 2025 tiguan with no vin is the same body class as the 2023 tiguan two rows up, and that is evidence sitting in the dataset rather than an assumption about the nameplate. only `body_class` is inherited — trim, engine and drivetrain vary within a nameplate and body class does not — and the source row id is stamped as `body_class_source` so the inference is auditable. an inferred value is never itself used as a source for another inference. together those took catodrive from **57 to 91 of 100** rows with a body class. the remaining nine were singletons with no vin and no sibling; nameplate matching in step 4 covers them anyway. ### 3 · attribute it to a person who can sign in php artisan fleet:owner-email {{app}} --list php artisan fleet:owner-email {{app}} --set="owner name=email@example.com" without `owner_email` the fleet-owner portal has nothing to scope by, so the owner sees nothing and has to ask an operator for every answer. **`—` is not blank.** 36 catodrive vehicles carry a dash as their owner, and a check written as `empty($owner)` reports a fully-attributed fleet. test for the placeholder explicitly. ### 4 · give it a photograph **a real photograph of the actual car, from the owner, is still the only right answer.** it is the tile someone picks a specific vehicle by and pays against. nothing below replaces it. php artisan fleet:prep {{app}} --photos # dry run php artisan fleet:prep {{app}} --photos --execute what that does is fill the gap where no real photo exists, from a library of **verified representative images** — and the rules it follows are the entire reason it is safe, because the first version of it was not. **a generic car is a wrong car. a labelled representative image is not a generic car.** the distinction is that the second one is a photograph of *this make, this model, this generation*, carries a visible "representative image · make model" badge, and never overwrites `image`. that is what every rental company means by "or similar". an unlabelled stand-in under a specific vin is a misrepresentation, and the label is not optional. the library is the atlas dataset `vehicle-images`, not a list in a source file: iris atlas:datasets records list --schema=vehicle-images adding an image is a dataset write, not a deploy. each row carries the classifier's verdict, its confidence, the model that produced it and the date, alongside the licence and the photographer. that last part is a **licence obligation** where the asset is cc by-sa — the credit rendered on the card is a term of use, not decoration, and must not be removed to tidy the tile. **four gates decide what the library will serve, and none of them may be removed.** they are written up in full under *the photo library* below — read that before changing any of this. each was added because something got past the one before it: *somebody looked at the image*, *the make not just the body type*, *the generation*, *presentability*. two are fleet-specific and worth naming here: - **a taos photograph classifies as `crossover` while vpic calls the car an suv.** same-make must outrank exact-body or most of the volkswagens get a stranger's photo — and volkswagens are 55 of these 100 cars. - **generation matters more than it sounds.** a 1996 first-generation honda odyssey passes make, model and body at 0.95 confidence and is thirty years wrong. the photo's generation window must contain the model year. **fail closed, always.** where nothing qualifies, write nothing and let the card keep its own body-shape silhouette. a 30-year-old photo of the right nameplate is not a degraded answer, it is the bug. the silhouette is a holding position, not a solution — but it is an honest one. php artisan fleet:prep {{app}} --reset-unverified --execute run that when the library changes. withdrawing a bad image from the api response stops it being *seen*, not *stored*, and `--photos` skips any row that already has the field — so without a reset the wrong value becomes permanent by omission. it strips anything the library would no longer choose **for that specific vehicle**, then `--photos` re-fills correctly. `--reverify` asks the classifier again at write time. it is **off by default** and should stay that way: it called a genuine buick envista a hyundai, and when the vision account ran out of credit it reported every remaining car as "refused". a classifier you cannot reach is not a car that does not match. ### 5 · verify all three claims. do not assume any of them this is the step the catodrive fleet never had, and it is why the problems were found by a client instead of by us. **bookable** — search dates the car is free and confirm it appears; then search dates it is taken and confirm it is marked, not hidden: curl -s "$api/api/v1/public/booking/{{app}}/fleet?start=&end=" \ | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d['meta'])" **attributable** — the owner tile must not have grown: curl -s "$api/api/v1/app-data/{{app}}/fleet-stats" -h "cookie: atlas_session=$tok" `missing owner` is on the operator dashboard for exactly this reason: a number nobody can see is a number nobody fixes. **visible** — open the page in a browser and look at the tile. not the json. a zero-width field, a broken image and a correct payload look identical from curl, and that is how a booking flow shipped with invisible date fields. ### 6 · one inventory, not two confirm the vehicle went into the collection the product actually reads — the dashboard app's `fleet` — and not a second list that merely looks like inventory. catodrive accumulated 75 title-only rows on a separate board that no page has ever read. two inventories means one of them is lying, and nobody knows which. ## the photo library, and why it is built the way it is everything below generalises past cars — it is the shape of any **acquire → classify → verify → store → serve** pipeline for assets you did not create and are about to show a paying customer. it lives here rather than in a playbook of its own because this is where it was learned and this is where it is used. ### the central finding **adding a verification gate does not converge on correct. it moves the failure to whatever the gate is not asking about — and the next bad asset arrives carrying more passing checks than the last one, so your confidence rises while the thing stays wrong.** four failures in a single day, each past everything that came before it: | # | gate added | what got past the previous gates | |---|---|---| | 1 | look at the image | a yellow porsche filed under `minivan`. five urls re-labelled by body type, none opened | | 2 | match the make, not just the body | a correctly-verified ford expedition stored on a vw tiguan | | 3 | match the generation | a **1996** honda odyssey. right make, right model, right body, **confidence 0.95** | | 4 | presentability | a wet night shot of the wrong regional variant; a grubby decade-old car with the driver visible | read row 3 again. right make, right model, right body type, 95% confident, thirty years old. **it was found by downloading six files and looking at them, and by nothing else.** no re-run of the checks would ever have said so, because the checks were the thing that was wrong. the corollary is uncomfortable and worth internalising: **when a check passes, that is evidence about the check as much as about the asset.** budget for opening a real sample by hand, and treat every caught failure as proof the suite is incomplete rather than as the last bug. ### store the verdict, not just the asset **a hardcoded list cannot record why an entry is trusted, so every entry looks equally authoritative — and typically only some were ever checked.** give each asset a row: iris atlas:datasets records list --schema=vehicle-images iris atlas:datasets import ./assets.json -s vehicle-images # upserts on external_id every row carries `source_url`; `cdn_url` (your own copy, preferred at read time); `licence` and `attribution`; `verdict` and `confidence`; `verifier` and `verified_at`; `usable`; and whatever your gates check — generation window, market — **as fields, not prose**. a rule that has to regex a sentence stops working the first time the wording changes. **keep the rejects**, with `usable: false` and a note saying what the thing actually is. a known-bad asset nobody wrote down is one somebody re-adds next quarter. **adding an asset is a data write, not a deploy.** if a new photo needs a release, the library will not be maintained. > atlas gotcha: `iris atlas:datasets schemas update` mints a **new** schema id and leaves existing > records pointing at the old one, so a reader resolving "the newest version" sees zero rows. > reading *every* version instead resurrects rows a re-import was meant to replace. the rule with > both properties: walk versions newest-first and stop at the first that returns rows. ### design the gates against the subject ask what a customer would notice, in the order they would notice it, and store the evidence for each as a field. - **is it the right *thing*?** category alone is never enough — the category is exactly what lets a porsche be a minivan. - **is it the right *one*?** the specific make and model. usually the half a customer recognises. - **is it the right *vintage*?** the quietest failure, because everything else passes. - **would we *show* it?** lighting, framing, clutter, people in frame, regional variant. for vintage, the asset's window must **contain** the target with about two years of grace — not six, which passes a 2013 car for a 2025 one. **grace at the boundary is for when nothing better exists; it must never win a tie against something that actually fits.** rank containment first, confidence second. ### fail closed, and say which kind of failure it is **returning nothing must be the easy path.** a near-miss is not a degraded answer, it is the bug: a 30-year-old photo of the right model is worse than a placeholder, because the placeholder is honest and the photo is a claim. the consumer must treat `null` as "show the empty state", never as "find something close". then distinguish these three, because collapsing them is its own bug: | state | honest response | |---|---| | the checker disagreed | `refused` — and say what it saw | | the checker was unreachable | `checker down` — quota, network, credentials. **not** a failed check | | nothing in the library qualifies | `no match` — and name the gap so someone can fill it | the middle row is the one everyone gets wrong. when the vision account ran out of credit mid-run, every remaining car came back "refused" — a checker we could not reach, reported as a car that did not match. **print coverage before results.** a pass that quietly fills 40 slots and silently skips 6 reads as a success. ### verify at acquisition, not on every write once the verdict is stored with its model and date, re-running the checker at write time buys little and costs real money and reliability — see `--reverify` above. where you do keep a runtime check, check the claim you are **actually making** (the library row's own attributes), not a field on the target record that may be absent. a check against a field you do not have passes by vacancy, and passing by vacancy is how the first bad photo shipped. memoise per asset: 22 records sharing one photograph should cost one call. ### host your own copy until `cdn_url` is filled you are hotlinking somebody else's uptime, bandwidth policy and url structure. note that some hosts (wikimedia among them) reject requests with no `user-agent`. browsers send one so pages render fine, while your scripts and thumbnailers get a 403 and you debug it as a broken asset. ### before calling the library done - [ ] **open a real sample by hand.** not the json. not the verdict. the file - [ ] every served asset carries its licence and attribution, and the attribution renders - [ ] every gate input is a queryable field, not prose in a summary - [ ] rejects are stored as rejects, not deleted - [ ] `null` renders an honest empty state; nothing substitutes a near-miss - [ ] an unreachable checker reports distinctly from a failed check - [ ] a run prints its coverage gaps, not only its successes - [ ] look at the rendered page in a browser — a correct payload and a broken `` are identical from `curl` ## the failure modes, named - **a placeholder is not a blank** — `—` passes an emptiness check and reads as data - **a row is not a vehicle** — it is bookable, attributable and visible, or it is a draft - **a generic car is a wrong car** — under a specific vin, an unlabelled stand-in is a misrepresentation. a labelled, generation-matched representative image is not the same thing - **a verdict is not a photograph** — make, model and body can all be right at 0.95 confidence and the car still be from 1996. open the file - **an unreachable checker is not a failed check** — say classifier down, never a bare refusal - **a gate that stops catching things is not obsolete** — that is what working looks like - **a near-miss is not a fallback** — it is the bug wearing the fix's clothes - **a constant cannot say why** — if the store cannot hold a verdict, nobody can audit it - **silence is not disagreement** — a missing field is not evidence of a mismatch; refusing on absent data empties the library for everything you never captured - **a name is not an identity** — an owner without an email cannot be shown their own cars - **two inventories** — the second one is always the stale one, and always looks fine

entries.name: freelabel-ads
entries.describe: FREELABEL — ad from idea to published post
entries.haystack: freelabel-ads freelabel — ad from idea to published post <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: freelabel-ads description: take an ad from an idea to a published post — brief, branded creative, caption, a human approval gate, then publish to the brand's own connected accounts. stops at the gate by default; publishing is a separate, deliberate act. creative comes from the existing campaign-image tools, publishing from the ownership-enforced social layer. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run freelabel-ads <topic>` > steps: check-accounts → brief → creative → caption → review → publish # freelabel — ad from idea to published post chains three things that already exist and had never been connected: the campaign-image tools that render branded creative, the agent that writes copy, and the ownership-enforced publishing layer. ## what this can and cannot do it makes **organic ad-shaped posts** — a branded graphic plus a caption, published to an account you own. it does **not** buy placement. there is no x ads or meta marketing connection in the stack, so "boost this" remains a human action in the platform's own ui. measurement is lopsided and worth knowing before you plan around it: upload-post reports analytics for **instagram, tiktok, linkedin and facebook — not x**. an x campaign is publish-and-look, not publish-and-measure, until x's own api is wired. ## why it stops before publishing `action` defaults to `review`, and the gate is a real `mode: human` pause rather than a printed warning. an ad is the one kind of post where the caption, the image and the account must all be right at once, and a model that can publish will publish on the first ask — that is exactly what happened the first time the agent tool was tested. so the run assembles everything, shows it, and stops. `--action=publish` is a second, deliberate decision. ## steps

entries.name: freelabel-bounty-ads
entries.describe: Bounty Ad — Render + Post to Instagram/X
entries.haystack: freelabel-bounty-ads bounty ad — render + post to instagram/x <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: freelabel-bounty-ads description: render a branded bounty/promo ad (remotion socialpost) and post it to instagram + x. turns a preset into a live social post in two commands. built to drive creators into live ugc bounties, but works for any promo. pass an action (e.g. "render", "post", "render-and-post", "dry-run", "list"). allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run freelabel-bounty-ads ` > run this playbook: `iris playbook run freelabel-bounty-ads` # bounty ad — render + post to instagram/x create a branded ad (video + story + still) with remotion and publish it to instagram + x through the existing upload-post integration. built for driving creators/tastemakers into live bounties (ugc rewards), but works for any promo. the whole loop is two steps: **render a preset → post the file.** both are one command. ## arguments `$arguments` — action and parameters. examples: - `/freelabel-bounty-ads render <preset>` — render square video + 9:16 story + still from a preset - `/freelabel-bounty-ads post <file|url> --caption="..."` — host on r2 + post to ig + x - `/freelabel-bounty-ads render-and-post <preset> --caption="..."` — do both - `/freelabel-bounty-ads dry-run <file>` — host on r2, print the cdn url, do not post - `/freelabel-bounty-ads list` — list presets + the live bounties worth advertising --- ## 1. render the ad (remotion) ad content is a preset json in `remotion/presets/*.json`: `{ brand, headline, roles[], eventinfo, ctatext, contacthandle }`. copy an existing `bounty-*.json`, change the values. **important — render via the minimal entry.** the main `remotion/src/root.tsx` has missing carousel imports that break the whole bundle. always render through `src/bounty-index.ts` (registers only the socialpost compositions): requires `remotion/public/social-post-audio.mp3` (drop a licensed music bed; a silent placeholder renders fine — generate with `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i anullsrc -t 15 public/social-post-audio.mp3`). run `npm install` in `remotion/` first if `node_modules` is missing. ## 2. post to instagram + x (`social:post-video`) the `social:post-video` artisan command hosts a local file on cloudflare r2 (`cdn.heyiris.io`) then posts via `uploadpostservice` (per-platform isolation + retries reused). r2 + upload-post keys are **prod-only**, so run with `railway run` to inject them into the local command (which has the rendered file): **always pass `--board=545 --user-id=193`** (the "freelabel creative" board). this auto-registers the creative in review studio as a tracked, reviewable item (pending on host, → approved on successful post) so nothing generated is ever untracked. add `--campaign=<id>` to group it. use `--dry-run --board=545 --user-id=193` to host + register for review without posting. - `--dry-run` hosts + prints the url without posting (always do this first). - route x through **`freelabelnet`** (has x connected). ig-only handles (`@thediscoverpage_`) skip x gracefully. - accepts a public url directly (skips hosting): `social:post-video --user=freelabelnet`. - confirm final status (async worker): `get with header `authorization: apikey $upload_post_api_key`. --- ## live bounties to advertise | bounty | rate | apply link | |--------|------|-----------| | #532 summer vibes clip campaign | $5 / 1k views ($1000 pool) | freelabel.net/marketplace/opportunity/532 | | #523 song wars content team | $0.50 / 1k | freelabel.net/marketplace/opportunity/523 | | #519 artists wanted | $0.10 / 1k | freelabel.net/marketplace/opportunity/519 | **always use the `freelabel.net` domain in ad copy** (brand-facing). it 301-redirects to the live marketplace page with the path preserved — confirmed working. do not use `web.freelabel.net` or `web.heyiris.io` directly in captions. ## key files - `remotion/presets/bounty-*.json` — ad content (copy + edit to make a new ad) - `remotion/src/bountyroot.tsx` + `src/bounty-index.ts` — clean render entry (bypasses broken root.tsx) - `fl-api/app/console/commands/postvideotosocial.php` — the post command - `fl-api/config/uploadpost.php` — brand → social handle routing ## proof it works first real post (2026-07-06): the summer vibes bounty ad went live on ig `instagram.com/reel/dadtuo3jhti` + x `x.com/freelabelnet/status/2074165976648634831`.

entries.name: freelabel-social
entries.describe: FREELABEL → Social
entries.haystack: freelabel-social freelabel → social <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: freelabel-social description: turn a live bounty, opportunity, event or program into freelabel-branded social content for x and instagram. the creator-audience counterpart to howto-social — same render and publish rails, different source and different voice. money numbers are mapped from the record, never written by a model. pass an opportunity/bounty id, or "list" to see what is live. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run freelabel-social ` # freelabel → social `howto-social` posts iris developer recipes to a developer audience. this is the other half: **freelabel content for creators** — bounties they can earn from, events they can play, programs they can join. same render and publish rails. different source, different voice, and one extra rule that does not apply on the iris side: **the numbers are real money, so they get mapped, never generated.** ## arguments `$arguments` — an opportunity/bounty id, or `list`. - `/freelabel-social 519` — artists wanted — song wars live 2 - `/freelabel-social list` — what is live right now - `/freelabel-social event 41` — event promo ## the rails already exist. audited 2026-08-21. nothing here needs building. know what is already there before adding anything: | rail | command | state | |---|---|---| | brand tokens | `remotion/src/brands.ts` | 9 brands: freelabel, discover, beatbox, emc_radio, capital_collective, noys, creative_gs, vanguard, heyiris | | bounties | `iris bounty list` | live — real budgets and spend | | opportunities | `iris opportunities list/get/pull` | live | | events | `iris events list/get/pull` | live | | programs | `iris programs list/get/pull` | live | | carousel from a record | `iris deliver:carousel --from opportunity:<id>` | exists, **ai-written** | | single promo image | `iris remotion still socialpost…` | exists | | ad with an approval gate | `iris playbook run freelabel-ads` | v2, multi-platform, ownership-enforced | | bounty promo, two commands | `iris playbook run freelabel-bounty-ads` | exists | | publish | `iris x post --brand freelabel --also instagram` | @freelabelnet **connected** | | asset hosting | `iris cloud:upload <file>` | returns a cdn url | `freelabel` and `discover` both post as **@freelabelnet** and both are connected. `heyiris` and `capital_collective` are **disabled**. ## 🔴 the money rule an opportunity record carries `budget_pool_cents`, `budget_remaining_cents`, `budget_spent_cents`, `days_until_deadline`, `application_deadline`, `bounty_type`, `compensation_model` and `applicant_count`. **read those fields. do not let a model phrase them.** `iris deliver:carousel --from opportunity:<id>` and `remotion auto-carousel` write copy with a model. that is fine for a headline and fatal for a rate. a hallucinated `$0.50/1k views` on a post promising creators money is a commitment you did not make, to an audience that will screenshot it. put them on the stats slide verbatim, converted from cents. if a number is missing, **leave the slide off** — an empty stat is better than a confident wrong one. this is the same principle `howto-social` uses for recipe copy, and it matters more here because the downside is financial. ## voice — freelabel is not iris | | iris | freelabel | |---|---|---| | audience | operators, developers | creators, artists, producers | | proof | "here is the command" | "here is what it pays" | | cta | read the recipe | apply / submit / pull up | | tone | precise, technical, no fluff | direct, warm, concrete | | handle | @heyiris.io *(disabled)* | @freelabelnet | lead with the offer, not the mechanism. a creator does not care that the payout is computed from a views ledger; they care that 1,000 views pays them something and the deadline is friday. never post an iris recipe from @freelabelnet just because that account is connected. wrong audience, and it trains the feed on the wrong thing. `howto-social` documents the same fork. ## the pipeline for anything with an offer in it, prefer `freelabel-ads` — it has a **human approval gate** built in and stops there by default. publishing is a separate, deliberate act. that is the right default when the post promises money. ## ⚠️ verify the render before uploading `iris remotion carousel` shipped a version that rendered the composition's **demo content** and reported success — props were passed as an inline string, remotion could not parse them, and every slide read *"5 ways to grow your brand on social media"* under `done. 9 slides saved`. it also resolved a relative `-o` against the remotion package, printing that same success line over an empty directory. both fixed in cli **v1.3.198**. regardless: 1. **open `slide-0.png` and read it.** a green run is not evidence. 2. **`ls slides/<name>/*.png | wc -l` must be 9.** 3. **check the money on the stats slide against the record**, not against the props you wrote. ## batch by what is live, not by what exists do not promote a bounty whose `budget_remaining_cents` is 0 — creators will submit work that cannot be paid. filter on remaining budget and `days_until_deadline > 0` before rendering anything. ## related - `howto-social` — the iris/developer counterpart. same rails, different audience. - `freelabel-ads` — idea → creative → caption → **approval gate** → publish. use for offers. - `freelabel-bounty-ads` — preset → socialpost → ig + x in two commands. - `carousel-announce` — diary-sourced carousels, ai-written. - `discover-publish` — multi-brand publishing across beatbox, discover, emc radio, capital collective and freelabel.

entries.describe: Gate audit — is this a control, or only a record?
entries.haystack: gate-audit gate audit — is this a control, or only a record? <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: gate-audit description: prove a security or compliance control actually enforces. most gates are records, not controls — and the evidence that would prove it is usually written by nobody's reader. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run gate-audit <control>` > steps: locate → events → evidence → three-zeros → verdict → writeup # gate audit — is this a control, or only a record? a gate that records decisions and applies none is not a weak control. it is **not a control**, and describing it as one to a client, an auditor or a court is the actual risk. this playbook finds out which one you have, in any stack, and it is built around the three ways this particular check lies. run it before you say a thing is protected. run it again before you flip enforcement on. ## steps

entries.name: general-relativity-demo
entries.describe: General relativity, checked against reality
entries.haystack: general-relativity-demo general relativity, checked against reality <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: general-relativity-demo description: watch a 56-year astronomical mystery get solved on your own machine, down to the arcsecond. simulate a planet's orbit the way newton's gravity predicts it and the way einstein's does, and see general relativity's extra term land on the exact anomaly that convinced physicists einstein was right in 1915 — real orbital data, one equation, no black box. pass a planet name as argument. allowed-tools: - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run general-relativity-demo ` > steps: simulate # general relativity, checked against reality in 1859, the astronomer le verrier noticed that mercury's orbit was precessing — its perihelion, the closest point to the sun, slowly rotates around the sun over time. that much was expected: the gravity of every other planet tugs on mercury and makes its ellipse rotate. le verrier calculated that effect precisely, using nothing but newton's law of gravity, and it came up short. mercury precesses about 43 arcseconds per century faster than newtonian gravity, accounting for every known planet, can explain. for 56 years nobody could close that gap. the leading guess was an undiscovered planet, closer to the sun than mercury, tugging on it — they even named it *vulcan* and searched for it. it was never found, because it does not exist. in november 1915, einstein worked out that his new theory of gravity predicted an *extra* term in a planet's precession that newton's theory simply does not have — and when he computed it for mercury, it came out to almost exactly 43 arcseconds per century, with no free parameter he could have tuned to force the match. it was the first real experimental confirmation of general relativity. this playbook computes that number itself, from the planet's own real orbital measurements, so you can watch it land on the historical value rather than take anyone's word for it. ## arguments `$arguments` — which inner planet's orbit to simulate: `mercury`, `venus`, `earth`, or `mars`. defaults to mercury, the historical case. ## steps

entries.name: genesis-guide
entries.describe: Genesis Guide — building UI on IRIS
entries.haystack: genesis-guide genesis guide — building ui on iris <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: genesis-guide description: build pages and apps on iris genesis without guessing at a system that shifts underneath you — wire your own components to live data, score the design against the house standard before you publish, and prove it renders in a browser instead of trusting a green check. pass a topic such as design, component, bind, publish, or verify. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task - skill --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run genesis-guide ` # genesis guide — building ui on iris a page binds an address. where the rows live sits behind it. that one separation dissolves the question that blocks most genesis work — *"should the data live at the item level or the bloq level?"* it is unanswerable because it conflates how a page **addresses** rows with where rows are **stored**. this guide covers the whole path: the design standard, authoring a component, binding it to live data, publishing, and the browser verification that keeps going wrong. ## arguments `$arguments` — a topic: - `/genesis-guide design` — the design standard. mandatory before any html or css. - `/genesis-guide model` — the addressing model; read this before designing anything. - `/genesis-guide component` — author a component. - `/genesis-guide bind` — attach data to it. - `/genesis-guide publish` — compile, store, push, cache-clear. - `/genesis-guide verify` — prove it works (the part that keeps going wrong). - `/genesis-guide gaps` — what is not built yet, so you do not plan around it. --- ## 1. the model — read this first **a page binds an address. where the rows live sits behind it.** | address | rows are | backed by | writable | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `item:181094` | the table a **card carries** | `bloq_items.content.dataset` | no | | `list:2115` | the **cards in a list** | `bloq_items` | yes | | `bloq:620` | the **cards in a workspace** | `bloq_items`, `list` is a field | yes, with a list | | `dataset:sessions` | **typed records** | `atlas_schemas` + `atlas_records` | yes, gated | `item:` treats a card as a **container of rows**. `list:` and `bloq:` treat cards **as** rows. `list:` is not its own provider — it is `bloq:` with a filter, which is why a board component binds the workspace **once** and groups by the `list` field instead of binding a column at a time. ### which to reach for the line is **who reads a row**, not where it is stored. 560 generated rows should not be 560 draggable cards. a curated todo list should not need a schema migration. both are servable; neither has to become the other. ### two backing modes - **`mode_query`** — rows have their own table. sql does search, sort, count, paging. - **`mode_materialised`** — rows live inside one record. php does the same work, and the provider **must** declare `maxrows()`. past the cap the read is **refused, not truncated** — a silently short answer is indistinguishable from a correct one. --- ## 2. design — mandatory, before any html or css ** not advisory. score every page against it **before publishing**: one point each, **9–10 ship · 6–8 revise · 0–5 redesign.** **a1 is the predictor.** *could this design be moved onto a different subject unchanged?* if yes, it is a template, it will score ≤4, and local fixes will not rescue it — restart from the subject. ### if the page renders data, it must pass the second instrument too eleven more checks, and they are the ones real pages fail: d1 and d8 are the ones a component author owns: **a genesis component is bound to live data**, so the empty state, the loading state and the malformed row are yours, not the page's. ### genesis-specific non-negotiables each was learned by shipping something broken: - **theme comes from the host, not the os.** inside a genesis page, switch on `html.dark` — never `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`. a block that follows the os renders dark inside a light page. (artifacts are the opposite: they own their document and *do* use `prefers-color-scheme`.) - **a `customhtml` block must not paint its own `background`.** it becomes a slab floating on the page ground. - **namespace every selector.** `customhtml` injects via `v-html` with no isolation — a bare `body`, `section` or `table` rule leaks into the host page. - **no webfont cdns.** the csp blocks them and it falls back to arial *silently*. build stacks from faces that ship on macos and windows, or inline a data uri. - **nothing owns its outer space.** components ship `margin: 0`; the container owns rhythm via `gap`. 4px unit, 8px base, air is opt-in. ### and the one that keeps being skipped **render-verify in a real browser.** grepping strings out of the served html is not verification — point a10 exists because that failed in production. `iris pages screenshot <slug>`, then *look at the image*. --- ## 3. authoring a component options api, always. that is a **security** decision, not a style one: `<script setup>` is a module body whose safety depends on anticipating every global, while an options object reaches state through `this`, so the legal name set is *closed* — derived from your own source. there is no `window`, `document`, `fetch` or `localstorage`, and no route to one. data arrives through `$dataset` / `$datasets`, bound **on the page** — a component can never name a feed it was not given, which is the property everything else rests on. refused, each for a reason someone found the hard way: `v-html`, `<component :is>`, imports, `this` as a value, computed access via a variable, non-literal `data()`, webfont cdns, remote `url()` in css, `constructor` / `__proto__` / `object.values(this)` chains. **check before publishing:** --- ## 4. binding data or an atlas dataset, singular or named: `emitto` routes an event into page state; `bindstate` feeds page state into another component's prop. both live in the page json, so the wiring between two components is readable without opening either one. ### search, sort, write — all server-side filtering `rows` in the browser searches only the page already loaded — a term matching row 300 of 500 returns nothing and **looks exactly like no match**. `sort` is validated against declared fields; a refused key is named in `meta.sort_ignored`, so a dropped sort cannot pass as an honoured one. **the gate rule, and it is not negotiable:** a **collection never serves an ungated visitor**. it has neither a public flag nor per-column visibility — the two things that make an atlas dataset safe to expose. an atlas dataset marked public can render publicly; a collection cannot. both the ssr path and the query/create lane enforce this identically, because two lanes with different rules is how the same data ends up both gated and not. --- ## 5. publish every component compiles **before** anything is stored, so one failure aborts the batch having written nothing. re-running is idempotent; replacing someone else's component under that name returns **409** unless you pass `"replace": true`. **push from the repo root.** `iris pages push` reads `./pages` from the working directory, and `fl-iris-api` has a stale shadow `pages/` that will silently win and ship an old page. --- ## 6. verify — the part that keeps going wrong **a screenshot you actually look at.** not `mounted: true`, not a grep of the served html. grepping a page lies in both directions, repeatedly: a gated page returns 200 carrying the otp gate's markup and reads as an empty page; a symbol grep confirms a deploy that never happened; an href escaped inside page json reads as missing. for anything with a viewport, the instrument is your eyes. then: **check the instrument before believing a null result.** run a known-good control. a filtered command that prints nothing may be measuring nothing. --- ## 7. open gaps — do not plan around these - **no container primitive** (#181954 / #181956). the component host renders `display: contents` and has no box, so edge-to-edge is the default outcome for a *correctly written* component. this is why every polished page in production is still nav + one customhtml blob. it is a limit of the **page layer**, not the format — and it is what a spatial canvas would have to be built on. - **no markdown primitive.** `list:` / `bloq:` bind prose cards, and `v-html` is banned — so a board renders titles with blank bodies today. the fix is a trusted `<markdown>` primitive rendered by runtime code, which is a **new trusted surface** and deserves the stress-test treatment the compiler got. - **`textblock.maxwidth` is declared and ignored** (#181955). asked 72rem, rendered 848px. - **no per-record update on collections.** the contract has no stable row identity — a card-carried table is positional rows in a json blob. the endpoint answers **501**, not a misleading 422. - **no cli verb to declare a bloq schema.** `bloqs.custom_fields_config` is the slot; setting it currently needs the api. - **`stale: true`** is set on components compiled under an older compiler. nothing acts on it. --- ## the two page lanes, and when each wins **composable** — `codecomponent` naming stored components. a page carries **no executable code** (the console page is 1.8 kb of json), which is what makes it safe to hand to a non-trusted owner, and what lets the same components render on two pages that know nothing about them. blocked today on layout — see the container gap. **bespoke** — `render_mode: html`, one hand-written block. full layout control, and currently the only way to get a polished marketing page. costs: the page owns its own ground (`html` and `body` are transparent), every selector must be namespaced because `v-html` injects without isolation, theme comes from `html.dark` and **never** `prefers-color-scheme`, and no webfont cdn will load. pick composable when the page is a **surface over data**. pick bespoke when it is a **document someone will read**. both score against **both** instruments before publishing. a composable page does not get an exemption because its parts are components. --- ## reference - contract, diagrams, use cases — - how-to — - studio (compiles as you type) — - worked example — - same components, second page — - design standard —

entries.describe: Genesis regression suite
entries.haystack: genesis-regression genesis regression suite <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: genesis-regression description: run the genesis sdk regression suite before publishing anything — compiler, runtime, markdown, harness, auditor, schemas and the php collection/composition/trace tests, all offline. use it before any component publish, page push or deploy that touches genesis. pass an action such as run, why, or add to extend coverage. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run genesis-regression ` # genesis regression suite **run this before you publish a component, push a page, or deploy anything touching genesis.** no server, no deploy, no browser, no database. about fifteen seconds. ## arguments `$arguments` — `run` · `why` · `add` · `gaps` ## what it covers | suite | checks | answers | | --- | --- | --- | | `compiler:check` | 85 | what a component may not do — every escape it has ever caught | | `runtime:check` | — | the controlled scope, compiler deliberately bypassed | | `markdown:check` | 49 | injection cannot be expressed, not merely filtered | | `harness:check` | 36 | behaviour: binding, nesting, actions, chat ordering | | `audit:check` | 19 | is it any *good* — raw values, empty states, null props | | `schemas:check` | — | declared props match their generated json | | phpunit | 70 | collections, graph gating, composition paths, trace origin | ## why one command, and why it is not just `genesis:check` `genesis:check` ran only the javascript half. on 2026-08-24 a rewrite of `findcomponent()` read one of three possible page shapes — `fetchpage()` returns a page record, so components live under `json_content` — and broke `$dataset` reads, writes and actions on **every page**, including pages that had been working all day. it was committed and deployed. **nothing anyone runs would have caught it**, because the failing code was php and the command people run is javascript. a suite split across two runners is a suite half of which nobody runs. `genesis:test` is both halves. ## what it does not cover, stated so it is not assumed - **layout.** happy-dom has no layout engine. widths, overflow, gutters and clipping are still a screenshot question — `iris pages screenshot <slug>` and *look at the image*. - **gated paths end to end.** a collection write needs an atlas session, which no offline test can mint. prove those in-container: `php artisan collections:read|write`, `atlas:graph`. - **the live agent.** `$actions` is exercised against a recorded fake, not a real reactloop run. ## before publishing — the order that catches things step 2 matters more than it looks: republishing a component changes every page naming it, immediately. version history exists, so it is recoverable — but a rollback changes all of them a second time. ## adding coverage put a test where the bug was, not where it was convenient: - **a compiler rule** → `scripts/check-code-component-compiler.mjs`, with a fixture that must trip it and a clean one that must not. a check that never fires converts "unchecked" into "passed". - **component behaviour** → `scripts/check-harness.mjs`. mounts the real compiler output through the real runtime; records every platform call, so "did it write" is answerable with no database. - **a quality rule** → `scripts/genesis-audit.mjs` + a control in `check-audit.mjs`. - **server-side shape or gating** → `tests/unit/{collections,graph,genesis}`. this is where today's regression belonged and where nothing was looking. ## the pattern behind most of these tests nearly every bug this suite guards was the same shape: **a true-looking answer to a question nobody asked.** a count of the unfiltered set. a refused sort silently answered with id order. a search that filtered nothing and returned everything. a component that rendered as empty because its artifact never resolved. a run whose origin was hardcoded. none of them threw. all of them looked fine. that is what the assertions are actually for.

neither has to become the other. ### two backing modes - **`mode_query`** — rows have their own table. sql does search, sort, count, paging. - **`mode_materialised`** — rows live inside one record. php does the same work, and the provider **must** declare `maxrows()`. past the cap the read is **refused, not truncated** — a silently short answer is indistinguishable from a correct one. ### what this replaced all of it existed only to reconcile two stores, and none of it is needed: a promotion pipeline (card grid → atlas), `atlas_schemas.bloq_item_id`, a `source_hash` + drift detector, schema inference with per-field overrides, a demotion policy. **nothing migrates.** --- ## 1b. design — mandatory, before any html or css ** not advisory. score every page against it **before publishing**: one point each, **9–10 ship · 6–8 revise · 0–5 redesign.** **a1 is the predictor.** *could this design be moved onto a different subject unchanged?* if yes, it is a template, it will score ≤4, and local fixes will not rescue it — restart from the subject. ### if the page renders data, it must pass the second instrument too eleven more checks, and they are the ones real pages fail: d1 and d8 are the ones a component author owns: **a genesis component is bound to live data**, so the empty state, the loading state and the malformed row are yours, not the page's. ### genesis-specific non-negotiables each was learned by shipping something broken: - **theme comes from the host, not the os.** inside a genesis page, switch on `html.dark` — never `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`. a block that follows the os renders dark inside a light page. the container owns rhythm via `gap`. 4px unit, 8px base, air is opt-in. ### and the one that keeps being skipped **render-verify in a real browser.** grepping strings out of the served html is not verification — point a10 exists because that failed in production. `iris pages screenshot <slug>`, then *look at the image*. --- ## 2. authoring a component options api, always. that is a **security** decision, not a style one: `<script setup>` is a module body whose safety depends on anticipating every global, while an options object reaches state through `this`, so the legal name set is *closed* — derived from your own source. there is no `window`, `document`, `fetch` or `localstorage`, and no route to one. data arrives through `$dataset` / `$datasets`, bound **on the page** — a component can never name a feed it was not given, which is the property everything else rests on. refused, each for a reason someone found the hard way: `v-html`, `<component :is>`, imports, `this` as a value, computed access via a variable, non-literal `data()`, webfont cdns, remote `url()` in css, `constructor` / `__proto__` / `object.values(this)` chains. **check before publishing:** --- ## 3. binding data or an atlas dataset, singular or named: `emitto` routes an event into page state; entries.name: geometric-reasoning-briefing
entries.describe: Geometric reasoning — research briefing
entries.haystack: geometric-reasoning-briefing geometric reasoning — research briefing <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: geometric-reasoning-briefing description: a tiny lab claims its small models out-reason giants 60-1000x by training the actual geometry of thought instead of scaling data. the claim is unverified and the company name is uncertain, but the evaluation trick they use to prove it is real, reusable, and worth stealing for our own eval harness today. pass a question about the claim or the technique as argument. allowed-tools: - read - webfetch - websearch - write --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run geometric-reasoning-briefing ` # geometric reasoning — research briefing **source:** a ~54-minute interview (youtu.be/4s8i22ybg2c), transcribed via `iris transcribe`. full transcript archived at ` **confidence: low-to-medium, name now confirmed.** this is one interview with one founder about their own unpublished work. the company is **sophontic** (sophontic.ai) — confirmed by web search after the asr transcript garbled it five different ways ("sofontic" / "phontik" / "sofantek"); their own site independently confirms the geometric-reasoning framing, the rejection of the scale paradigm, and an unreleased "perturbation-paradigm eval kit," which lines up with the interview. that's real corroboration of the *positioning* — it is not a third-party benchmark or a reproduction of the *result*. no paper, no independent eval, no reproduction exists in what we have. **treat the company and the technique as real; treat the 60x-1000x number as their own unverified claim until an outside benchmark exists.** ## arguments `$arguments` — what to focus on: the core claim, the evaluation technique, or the strategic read for iris. leave blank for the full briefing below. --- ## 1. the claim, in plain terms mainstream ai training treats reasoning as an emergent side effect of scale: feed a model enough data and enough compute, and something that looks like thought shows up as a "mysterious emergent property." the guest's argument is that this is backwards. reasoning, in his framing, is a **geometric structure** — a specific mathematical shape — that already exists inside a model's internal (latent/vector) space. instead of hoping that shape emerges from brute-force scale, his lab studies it directly, empirically, inside the latent space itself, and trains it into the model from the foundation up. the claimed result: very small models (laptop-scale, discussed as possibly under 10b — even under 1b — parameters) **out-reasoning models 100-1000x larger** on rigorous reasoning tests. the founder is explicit that the exact multiplier is unresolved — "somewhere between 60 times and three orders of magnitude" — and says so on his own website as the conservative number. that candor is a point in the claim's favor; a huckster picks the biggest number and doesn't hedge it. ## 2. the technique that's real regardless of the bigger claim: perturbation testing this is the part worth adopting **whether or not the geometric-reasoning story holds up**, because it's a testing method, not a training claim, and we can verify it ourselves. **the problem it targets:** standard ai evals can be gamed by memorization. a model that has seen a problem (or something close to it) in training can answer correctly without having reasoned about it at all — and most benchmarks can't tell the difference, because they only score whether the final answer matches. **the fix — "the perturbation paradigm":** take a problem the model gets right, then make a small, targeted change to it that flips the correct answer (change a number, swap two words that alter the logic) without changing the problem's surface difficulty. a model that memorized the original still gives the original answer — now wrong. a model that actually reasoned through the structure gets the new one right, because it re-derives the answer instead of recalling it. **why this matters to us specifically:** the pricing-model audit (see `price-your-business` and the underlying iris labs cost review) already surfaced that our own eval harness (`eval:v6`) has no cost column and no `--model` flag — we can rank model quality but not quality-per-dollar, and we can't hold a test set constant while swapping models. perturbation testing is a cheap, orthogonal upgrade to add on top of that fix: it would tell us whether a model routed into production is actually reasoning about a client's case/lead/document, or pattern-matching a similar one it's seen before. worth prototyping against one of our own agent eval suites independent of whether we ever look at this lab again. ## 3. the strategic argument, and why it's worth taking seriously even if the number is wrong independent of whether "60x to 1000x" survives scrutiny, the founder makes three structural arguments that are worth engaging with on their own merits: - **"frozen giants."** a frontier model is trained once, at enormous cost, to a stable state, then frozen — what looks like "learning" in a chat session (memory, context) is closer to sticky notes for someone with amnesia than actual learning. if small models can genuinely reason, the barrier to *continual* learning drops with them — a model that keeps adapting on ordinary hardware, not one re-trained from scratch by a lab with a nation-state budget. - **concentration risk.** only a handful of organizations can afford frontier-scale training, which means only a narrow slice of human thought gets instilled into the systems everyone increasingly relies on — a "monoculture," in his phrase, at exactly the layer where diversity is usually what keeps a system resilient. - **precedent for small-and-real over big-and-scaled.** the protein-folding model that drove real biotech breakthroughs was under 100m parameters — "a toy" by frontier standards — and it worked because it was small enough to genuinely iterate and specialize, not despite being small. none of this requires believing the specific multiplier. it's a coherent argument for why "small, real reasoning beats large, statistical pattern-matching" is a plausible direction, and it's the same direction iris hive already bets on: run real work on hardware you own instead of paying for a data center, and treat model routing (not raw scale) as the lever that actually controls cost and capability — which is close to word-for-word what the pricing-model audit found about our own routing decisions in §04-05. ## 4. what to actually do with this 1. **done — the source is confirmed.** sophontic (sophontic.ai) is a real, findable research company matching the interview's claims. still watch for an independent benchmark or paper before treating the 60x-1000x figure as anything more than their own number. 2. **prototype perturbation testing on one existing eval suite** — this doesn't require the bigger claim to be true to be worth doing. 3. **do not cite the 60x-1000x figure externally** (a pitch deck, a client conversation) without independent confirmation. internally, it's a reason to watch the space; externally, an unverified single-source number stated as fact is exactly the kind of claim this team has burned time chasing down before (see the pricing-model audit's own §16 on rejecting an outside review's claims that didn't survive checking against our own numbers). ## the shape of the mistake this briefing is trying to avoid the easy failure here is treating "a founder said an impressive number in an interview" as equivalent to "a benchmarked, reproduced result." the founder himself doesn't make that mistake — he publishes the conservative number and says the truth is somewhere in a range he hasn't pinned down. this briefing tries to hold the same line: separate the part that's a genuinely reusable technique (perturbation testing — adopt it) from the part that's an unverified claim from one interview (the multiplier and the company itself — verify before repeating).

entries.describe: Heartbeat Debug — Production Debugging Skill
entries.haystack: heartbeat-debug heartbeat debug — production debugging skill <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: heartbeat-debug description: debug, diagnose, and manage the heartbeat agent system in production. use when heartbeats aren't running, agents are looping, circuit breakers trip, or you need to inspect/kill/restart heartbeat jobs. pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "diagnose", "kill", "logs"). allowed-tools: - read - bash - grep - glob - task --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run heartbeat-debug ` # heartbeat debug — production debugging skill debug and manage the autonomous agent heartbeat system across fl-api and iris-api. ## arguments `$arguments` — action to perform. examples: - `/heartbeat-debug status` — quick health overview of all heartbeat agents - `/heartbeat-debug diagnose` — full diagnostic (loop detection, rapid-fire, token burn) - `/heartbeat-debug diagnose 11` — diagnose specific agent - `/heartbeat-debug logs` — tail production heartbeat logs - `/heartbeat-debug kill 248` — emergency kill a runaway agent - `/heartbeat-debug run 766` — manually trigger heartbeat for agent - `/heartbeat-debug history 766` — view recent execution history - `/heartbeat-debug circuit-breaker 11` — check/reset circuit breaker - `/heartbeat-debug scheduler` — check if scheduler is running - `/heartbeat-debug jobs` — list all heartbeat scheduled jobs - `/heartbeat-debug pause 764` — safely pause a heartbeat (won't resurrect) - `/heartbeat-debug resume 764` — resume a paused heartbeat - `/heartbeat-debug model 604 grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning xai` — change agent model --- ## architecture quick reference ### infrastructure (railway — april 2026) | service | role | db | production url | |---------|------|-----|----------------| | **fl-api** | orchestrator — schedules jobs, runs `agents:process-jobs` every minute | `freelabelnet` | `raichu.heyiris.io` (railway) | | **iris-api** | executor — builds prompts, calls llms, writes results back | `iris_db` + `fl_api` connection to `freelabelnet` | `freelabel.net` (railway) | | **iris-worker** | queue worker — processes `runworkspaceagenticjob` for heartbeat execution | same as iris-api | railway (separate service) | ### flow ### key principles 1. heartbeat runs through `agents:process-jobs`, not its own cron. if heartbeat stops, the scheduling infrastructure is broken. 2. the scheduler is the **universal cron harness** for all job types. 3. `executeagentjob` has a **staleness guard** — if the job status is no longer "running" when the queue worker picks it up, it skips execution. this prevents backlog floods. 4. `tries = 1` — no laravel retry. retries on scheduled jobs cause duplicates. --- ## iris cli commands (preferred) --- ## action implementations ### 1. `status` — quick health overview --- ### 2. `diagnose` — full diagnostic --- ### 3. `pause` — safely pause a heartbeat (won't resurrect) **critical: you must do both steps or the heartbeat will resurrect within minutes.** there are **three resurrection paths** in processagentjobs.php that recreate paused jobs: 1. `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` — creates new job if none found (checks completed/cancelled/paused) 2. `resetstuckjobs()` — auto-recovers paused heartbeats after 1 hour (checks for "auto-paused" in last_error) 3. `heartbeatservice::enableheartbeat()` — `updateorcreate` always sets status='scheduled' **the only reliable way to stop a heartbeat: set `heartbeat_mode = 'off'` on the agent and cancel the job.** just setting `status = 'paused'` is not enough — the job will be recreated within minutes by `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` or un-paused by `resetstuckjobs()`. ### 4. `resume` — resume a paused heartbeat --- ### 5. `model` — change agent model **critical bug (as of april 2026): agent model is stored in two columns — `settings` and `config`.** - `settings.model` — written by ui and `iris` cli - `config.model` — read by `heartbeatexecutorservice` (line 182) - if only `settings` is updated, heartbeats keep using the old model (defaults to `gpt-4.1-nano`) - v6 `reactloopservice` reads `config` first, `settings` as fallback (line 272) **bug filed as #67225. until fixed, always update both columns:** note: `config` column may be `[]` (empty array) not `{}` (empty object). if `json_set` fails, use: **recommended models:** - `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning` / `xai` — $0.20/m input, fast, good for heartbeats - `gpt-4.1-nano` / (default openai) — $0.10/m input, cheapest - `gpt-5-nano` / (default openai) — slightly better reasoning --- ### 6. `kill` — emergency kill agent --- ### 7. `run` — manually trigger heartbeat --- ### 8. `history` — view recent executions --- ### 9. `scheduler` — check scheduler health **known issue (fixed april 23, 2026):** `start-queue-worker.sh` had `set -e` + `curl` to `/workspace/yt-dlp`. if `/workspace` doesn't exist (railway), the queue worker enters fatal state on every deploy. jobs accumulate in redis indefinitely. fix: removed `set -e`, added `mkdir -p /workspace`, made installs non-fatal. --- ### 10. `jobs` — list all heartbeat jobs --- ## known bugs & fixes (april 2026) ### fixed: queue worker crash on railway deploy **commit:** `7e3704f5` | **severity:** critical `start-queue-worker.sh` had `set -e` + curl to `/workspace/yt-dlp`. `/workspace` doesn't exist on railway → exit code 23 → fatal state. jobs accumulate in redis forever. when worker restarts, all backlogged jobs fire at once. **fix:** removed `set -e`, added `mkdir -p /workspace`, non-fatal installs. ### fixed: backlog flood / duplicate dispatches **commit:** `8d703ce7` | **severity:** high dead queue worker → scheduler keeps queuing `executeagentjob` to redis → auto-recovery resets job → another dispatch → hundreds of jobs in redis → worker restarts → all fire simultaneously. **fix:** staleness guard in `executeagentjob.handle()` — checks `$job->status !== 'running'` before executing. `tries = 1` prevents laravel retry. ### fixed: dead iris-api url **commit:** `7e3704f5` | **severity:** high `irisapiservice.php` hardcoded `iris-api.freelabel.net` (dead after railway migration). changed to `heyiris.io`. ### fixed: scheduler logs invisible **commit:** `d7b5928d` | **severity:** medium `agents:process-jobs` output went to file only. now uses `tee >&2` to write to both file and stderr (railway captures). ### fixed: paused heartbeats resurrecting **commits:** `be6101cb`, `9d868493` | **severity:** high two code paths ignored paused status: 1. `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` — excluded completed/cancelled but not paused → created new jobs 2. `resetstuckjobs()` — treated all paused heartbeats as "dead" → un-paused after 1 hour **fix:** added `'paused'` to exclusion list. `resetstuckjobs` now distinguishes auto-paused (system, from failures) vs manually paused (user). **however:** these fixes are insufficient. there are additional resurrection paths (heartbeatservice `updateorcreate`, syncagentrecurringtasks). the **only reliable way** to stop a heartbeat is setting `heartbeat_mode = 'off'` on the agent and cancelling the job. see the `pause` action above. ### open: agent model split (settings vs config) **bug:** #67225 | **severity:** high `bloq_agents` has `settings.model` and `config.model`. heartbeatexecutorservice reads `config.model`, ui writes `settings.model`. workaround: update both columns. see the `model` action above. ### open: chain som_batch → inbox_scan 422 **fix deployed:** `ea1a463` on iris-api — added `inbox_scan` to nodetaskcontroller validation. --- ## common production scenarios ### heartbeat not running 1. check agent: `heartbeat_mode` must not be 'off' 2. check job exists: `iris schedules list` — look for the agent 3. check scheduler: `railway logs --service fl-api | grep agents:process-jobs` 4. check queue worker: `railway logs --service fl-api | grep "fatal\|queue-worker"` — if fatal, redeploy 5. check queue backlog: `echo "llen queues:agent-jobs" | railway connect redis` 6. check iris-worker: `railway logs --service fl-iris-worker | grep runworkspaceagenticjob` ### agent running too often (spam) 1. check if there are duplicate jobs for the same agent: 2. check queue backlog: `echo "llen queues:agent-jobs" | railway connect redis` 3. if backlog > 0, flush it: `echo "del queues:agent-jobs" | railway connect redis` 4. cancel duplicates, keep one per agent 5. check if `heartbeat_mode` is set — `ensureheartbeatjobsexist` creates new jobs for any agent with mode != 'off' ### agent using wrong model / getting 429 1. check both columns: `select json_extract(settings,'$.model'), json_extract(config,'$.model') from bloq_agents where id = x` 2. if `config.model` is null → heartbeat defaults to `gpt-4.1-nano` regardless of `settings.model` 3. update both: see `model` action above 4. 429 = credits exhausted on that provider. switch provider or top up credits. ### agent won't stop (keeps resurrecting) 1. **don't just pause the job** — it will come back within minutes 2. set `heartbeat_mode = 'off'`: `update bloq_agents set heartbeat_mode = 'off' where id = x` 3. cancel the job: `update bloq_scheduled_jobs set status = 'cancelled' where agent_id = x and task_name = 'heartbeat'` 4. both steps are required. see `pause` action above. ### post-deploy: queue worker dead 1. check: `railway logs --service fl-api | grep "fatal\|exit status"` 2. if you see `exit status 23` or `entered fatal state` → queue worker crashed during startup 3. usually caused by missing `/workspace` directory or failed curl downloads 4. fix: ensure `start-queue-worker.sh` doesn't have `set -e` and all installs are non-fatal 5. redeploy: `railway redeploy --service fl-api --yes` --- ## database schema reference ### bloq_agents (fl-api) ### bloq_scheduled_jobs (fl-api) --- ## key files ### fl-api - `app/console/commands/processagentjobs.php` — core scheduler + `ensureheartbeatjobsexist()` + `resetstuckjobs()` - `app/jobs/executeagentjob.php` — queue job with staleness guard + type routing - `app/services/agentjobschedulerservice.php` — `getduejobs()`, `markjobcompleted()`, `calculatenextrun()` - `app/services/heartbeatservice.php` — `enableheartbeat()` with `updateorcreate` (resurrection path #3) - `app/services/irisapiservice.php` — bridge to iris-api (`dispatchdirecttask`, `dispatchhivetask`) - `app/console/kernel.php` — `agentjobscheduler()` scheduling config - `start-queue-worker.sh` — queue worker startup (installs yt-dlp/ffmpeg) - `start-scheduler.sh` — scheduler startup (schedule:run loop) ### iris-api - `app/services/heartbeatexecutorservice.php` — prompt builder + llm execution (reads `config.model`) - `app/services/v6/reactloopservice.php` — v6 agentic workflow engine - `app/services/v6/v6aiservice.php` — model→provider routing (openai/xai/openrouter) - `app/http/controllers/api/nodetaskcontroller.php` — hive task dispatch validation --- ## active agents reference (april 2026) | agent id | name | model | provider | frequency | schedule id | |----------|------|-------|----------|-----------|-------------| | 604 | delo alert trading simulator | grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | xai | every 4 hours | #764 | | 605 | delo backtester | grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | xai | daily | #766 | | 606 | delo oversight | grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning | xai | every 4 hours | #768 | **disabled agents** (heartbeat_mode = 'off'): 315 (legal reviewer), 366 (ayala+goodbuy), 593 (platform updates bot), 594 (leads crm digest), 595 (delo alert assistant), 596 (dent society), 597 (cottonwood creek), 598 (ayala engineering) --- ##
