entries.name: hive-secure-mesh
entries.describe: Hive Secure Mesh — Tailscale as the road, Hive as the work
entries.haystack: hive-secure-mesh hive secure mesh — tailscale as the road, hive as the work <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: hive-secure-mesh description: bring a machine onto the secure mesh (tailscale) and make it a hive node — onboard, lock down with a least-privilege acl, connect, enroll, and diagnose. use when a machine that is not on your network needs to be reachable (remote desktop, a gui-only app like quickbooks, a localhost-only database) or needs to run hive tasks. pass an action as argument (onboard, status, lockdown, connect, enroll, doctor, explain). allowed-tools: - read - bash - grep --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run hive-secure-mesh ` # hive secure mesh — tailscale as the road, hive as the work brings a machine anywhere in the world onto an encrypted mesh **without opening a single port to the internet**, restricts who may reach it, and optionally makes it a hive node so iris can dispatch work to it. ## the model, in three layers each layer is a separate decision, and diagnosing from the bottom up is what makes failures obvious. being on the mesh does not grant access — the acl does. being reachable does not make a machine a hive node — enrolling does. ## two rails, and picking the right one **this playbook is the tailnet rail.** there is a second, independent rail: the daemon, where the machine dials *out* to iris over pusher and executes `nodetask`s. it needs no tailscale and no open ports. - need iris to **run something** on a machine? → daemon rail (`iris daemon start`) - need a human or session to **reach the machine itself** — rdp, a gui app, a localhost-only port? → tailnet rail (this playbook) - both? they compose and do not conflict. the trap: **a node reachable over tailscale does not mean its daemon is running**, and a running daemon does not mean the machine is on the tailnet. independent rails, independent failures. ## quick reference

entries.name: howto-social
entries.describe: How-To → Social
entries.haystack: howto-social how-to → social <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: howto-social description: turn a published how-to recipe into an instagram carousel and an x post, with no ai writing step. a recipe is already structured content, so the slides are a mapping of it rather than a model's summary — which means the post cannot say something the recipe does not. pass a recipe slug (e.g. "hive-tailscale", "remote-support-a-family-pc"), or "all" to batch the library. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run howto-social ` # how-to → social every published recipe at `heyiris.io/how-to` is a finished piece of content with a real use case, correct copy, and a link that goes somewhere. this turns one into 9 carousel slides and an x post. **the content step uses no model.** a recipe already carries title, summary, category, level, duration, tags, section headings and a code block, and `carouselslide`'s schema wants exactly those fields. generating slides from it is a mapping, not an inference — so the post cannot drift from what the recipe actually says. use `iris remotion auto-carousel` when you have only a topic; use this when you have the article. ## arguments `$arguments` — a recipe slug, or `all`. - `/howto-social hive-tailscale` - `/howto-social remote-support-a-family-pc` - `/howto-social all` — batch every published recipe find slugs with `iris how-to list` (grouped by category) or browse `heyiris.io/how-to`. ## the pipeline `--also instagram,threads` on `iris x post` cross-posts in one call. ## check the account before you render not every brand account is connected at any given moment, and the state changes — a dated list here would be wrong within a week. read the command output, not this paragraph. **that matters for this playbook specifically.** these recipes are product content for a developer audience. posting them from a different brand's account is a brand decision, not a fallback — ask before doing it. if the intended account is disconnected, fix the connection rather than quietly posting as someone else. ## verify the slides before posting. do not skip this. **`iris remotion carousel` used to render the composition's demo content and report success.** the shell wrapper passed props as an inline string (`--props "$json"`); remotion could not parse it and silently fell back to placeholder copy, so every slide read *"5 ways to grow your brand on social media"* while the command printed `done. 9 slides saved`. fixed in cli **v1.3.198** by passing a props file per slide. two habits survive the fix, because the failure mode is a wrong post rather than an error: 1. **open slide-0.png and read it.** if it says anything about growing your brand on social media, the props did not bind. a green run is not evidence. 2. **count the files.** `ls slides/<slug>/*.png | wc -l` should be 9. the same wrapper also resolved a relative `-o` against the remotion package instead of your cwd, printing `9 slides saved` over an empty directory. also fixed in v1.3.198, but count anyway. ## what lands on which slide | slide | content | source field | |---|---|---| | 0 | category badge, headline, opening paragraph | `category`, title, first `##` section | | 1–2 | section highlights | first three `##` headings + text | | 3 | terminal card | first fenced code block, capped at 52 columns | | 4–7 | checklist, tags, stats | `tags`, `level`, `duration_min`, section headings | | 8 | cta | `heyiris.io/how-to/<slug>` + `iris how-to view <slug>` | code lines are cut at 52 columns on purpose — the card wraps mid-word past that and reads as broken rather than dense. ## the x caption assembled from the recipe's own words: headline, first sentence, canonical url, up to three tags. it refuses to exceed 280 including the link, dropping the sentence before the link. read it before posting. it is faithful to the recipe by construction, but "faithful" and "good opening line" are different bars, and a recipe whose first sentence is throat-clearing will produce a flat post. rewrite the caption freely — the slides are the part that must stay accurate. ## batch mode generate props for everything, then render selectively. rendering 46 recipes is ~9 stills each and is not something to kick off without a reason. **pick by category, not alphabetically.** `iris how-to list --category "getting started"` is the set worth posting first — they are the recipes a new reader can act on immediately. ## wrong audience is a failure mode, not a fallback these recipes are developer content. when the intended account is disconnected and another brand's is live, it is tempting to post from whichever one works. don't do it by default — a creator-facing feed and a developer-facing one want different things, and a hive+tailscale recipe trains the wrong one. if the subject is a creator offer — a bounty, an event, a program — you want **`freelabel-social`**, which maps live opportunity records (including the money) and speaks to that audience. ## related - `freelabel-social` — the creator-audience counterpart. same render and publish rails, sourced from live bounties and opportunities instead of recipes. - `carousel-announce` — carousels from diary entries and ship notes, ai-written. use that when there is no recipe; use this when there is. - `iris how-to publish` — get the recipe live first. a carousel whose cta 404s is worse than no post. - `editorial-ad`, `freelabel-ads` — other remotion surfaces sharing the same brand tokens.

entries.haystack: import-preline-to-genesis-ui import preline to genesis ui — component pipeline <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: import-preline-to-genesis-ui description: import preline pro templates into the genesis composable page builder ui. handles the full pipeline — extract html patterns from preline, build vue 3 components, register in usecomponentmap, update validator schema, add to showcase page, commit/push to iris-api, and seed locally. pass an action or component idea as argument. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - agent --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run import-preline-to-genesis-ui ` # import preline to genesis ui — component pipeline import preline pro template patterns into the genesis composable page builder. build, register, validate, and deploy new vue 3 page builder components for the iris page system. components are rendered by iris-api and configured via json page definitions. ## arguments `$arguments` — action or component description. examples: - `/build-components list` — list all registered page builder components - `/build-components audit` — compare preline templates vs existing components, find gaps - `/build-components build "faq accordion with categories"` — build a new component from description - `/build-components from-preline "shop/product-detail.html"` — extract and build from a specific preline template - `/build-components showcase add testimonialssection` — add a component instance to the showcase page - `/build-components showcase seed` — seed the showcase page locally - `/build-components validate` — run validator on showcase page - `/build-components count` — count total registered components ## key paths | path | purpose | |------|---------| | `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/resources/js/components/pagebuilder/` | vue 3 component files | | `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/resources/js/composables/usecomponentmap.ts` | component registration (async imports) | | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/pagescommand.php` | validator schema (`getcomponentschema()` + `$arrayprops`) | | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/pages/component-showcase.json` | showcase page json | | `preline-pro-templates/pro/` | preline pro html templates (reference library) | | `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/config/page-components.yaml` | component catalog (yaml docs) | ## preline pro template library source templates at `preline-pro-templates/pro/`: | directory | contains | |-----------|----------| | `agency/` | services, careers, case studies, news, team (10 pages) | | `startup/` | features, pricing, about, customers (6 pages) | | `shop/` | product listing, detail, cart, checkout, compare (30+ pages) | | `coffee-shop/` | listings, product detail, bag, checkout, confirmation (6 pages) | | `dashboard/` | kanban, todo, chat, inbox, files, profiles, settings (22+ pages) | | `payment/` | balances, cards, send/request money, kyc verification (30+ pages) | | `personal/` | portfolio, reviews, work (3 pages) | | `crm/` | customers, tasks, search (10 pages) | | `analytics/` | visitors, incidents, survey (5 pages) | | `ai-chat/` | chat interface, explore (3 pages) | | `cms/` | posts, drafts, create post (5 pages) | | `project/` | project details, setup wizard (4 pages) | ## component architecture pattern every pagebuilder component must follow this exact structure: ### key conventions - **theme mode**: always `'light' | 'dark'` prop, default `'dark'` - **accent color**: resolves in order: prop → css variable `--primary-color` → fallback `#34d399` - **dark mode classes**: `thememode === 'dark' ? 'text-white' : 'text-gray-900'` - **section wrapper**: `class="xx-section py-20 px-4"` with conditional `bg-black`/`bg-white` - **container**: `max-w-5xl mx-auto` or `max-w-6xl mx-auto` - **accent application**: `:style="{ color: resolvedaccent }"` on highlighted elements - **no external dependencies**: pure tailwind css, no ui libraries - **scoped styles**: only when needed (animations, scrollbar hiding) - **never use `this.$toast`**: not applicable (vue 3 composition api) - **default accent**: `#34d399` (emerald green) — not purple/indigo ## full pipeline: building a new component ### step 1: research (if from preline) ### step 2: build the vue component follow the architecture pattern above. key rules: - typescript interfaces for all props - `withdefaults` for sensible defaults - accent color resolution pattern (copy exactly) - full dark/light mode support on every text/bg/border element - responsive: mobile-first with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:` breakpoints ### step 3: register in usecomponentmap.ts location: `fl-docker-dev/fl-iris-api/resources/js/composables/usecomponentmap.ts` add before the closing `};` of the componentmap object. ### step 4: update validator schema in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/pagescommand.php`: 1. add to `getcomponentschema()` array: 2. if component has a required array prop, add to `$arrayprops`: ### step 5: add to showcase page ### step 6: seed locally local showcase page id: **62** (created 2026-03-29) ### step 7: commit & push iris-api deploys from `main` with `deploy_on_push: true` on digitalocean. ## production deployment notes - **iris-api** deploys from `main` branch (changed from `feature/heartbeat-lead-management` on 2026-03-29) - **app id**: `68ad4e37-3502-4681-8f28-9c5725044dce` - **instance size**: `apps-s-1vcpu-2gb` (bumped from 1gb on 2026-03-29 due to oom with 30+ async component chunks) - **build failures at 6/9**: usually oom during container startup. check `doctl apps list-deployments` and force rebuild if needed - **rollback detection**: if active deploy shows `cause: automated rollback`, the previous build failed and production is running old code ## common commands ## existing component inventory (as of 2026-03-29) ### from preline (34 components built today): timelinecarousel, imagebanner, bloggrid, scatteredimagehero, servicelisting, pricingrows, testimonialssection, teamsection, contactsection, comparisonmatrix, logomarquee, mapsection, careerslisting, featureshowcase, clientgrid, announcementbanner, beforeafter, servicemenu, portfoliogallery, vehiclecard, vehiclegrid, productcard, productgrid, fundingtiers, eventgrid, shoppingcart, newslettersignup, membershipcards, eventcalendar, stepwizard, fileupload, protectionpicker, orderconfirmation ### pre-existing (built before today): hero, jumbotronhero, marketinghero, feedhero, scatteredimagehero, sitenavigation, sitefooter, irisnavigation, section, textblock, imageblock, imagegallery, videoblock, quoteblock, splitcontent, editorialsection, editorialcomparison, featuregrid, featurecardsgrid, featureiconsgrid, featurecomparisontable, featuretabs, accordionfeatures, codeshowcase, scrollshowcase, pricingplans, comparisoncards, statscounter, statssection, logostrip, processsteps, gettingstartedsteps, buttoncta, communitycta, benefitssection, faqaccordion, enrollmentform, workflowtrigger, bookingwizard, bookingcalendar, survey, dashboardprovider, dashboardlayout, statcard, kpigrid, datachart, datatable, apexchart, activityfeed, progresstracker, kanbanboard, chatpanel, projecttimeline, and more (80+ total in usecomponentmap.ts)

entries.name: iris-agreements
entries.describe: IRIS Agreements
entries.haystack: iris-agreements iris agreements <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-agreements description: get an nda or baa signed and get the audit trail that proves it — raise it, issue it, watch it move through draft, sent, opened and executed, and know which ones are still outstanding without asking anyone. from nothing to a countersigned agreement in one sitting. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-agreements <name>` > steps: existing → outstanding → raise → issue → watch → gate → done # iris agreements **what it is:** the product that turns "we should get an nda signed" into a signing link, a status you can query, and an audit trail that survives someone asking six months later. **what it is not:** a contract drafter or legal advice. it issues agreements from templates the business already stands behind — nda and baa. if you need bespoke terms, that is a lawyer, and then this issues what they wrote. **why it exists as a product rather than an email:** an agreement sent by email has no state. nobody can answer *has she signed it?* without searching an inbox, and *which agreements are outstanding?* is unanswerable. agreements gives every one of them a lifecycle — **draft → sent → opened → executed**, with **revoked** as a real terminal state — and makes the whole set queryable. ## the lifecycle, and the two states people get wrong draft ──issue──> sent ──they open it──> opened ──they sign──> executed │ │ └──────────────────── revoke ─────────────────────────────────┘ - **`sent` is not `opened`.** sent means we emailed a link. opened means a human loaded it. if something has sat at `sent` for a week, the email probably went to spam — that is a different problem from someone who opened it and hesitated, and it needs a different follow-up. - **`opened` is not `executed`.** only `executed` is signed. anything gating access on an agreement must check for `executed` and nothing weaker. - **`revoke` closes the access it authorised.** it is not a delete — the record and its trail stay, which is the entire point of having an audit trail. ## before you start you need the counterparty's **full name** and, to issue rather than just draft, their **email**. everything else has a default: `--type nda`, `--disclosing iris`, `--term "one year"`, and `--expires` derived from the term. **pick `--type baa` if anything the counterparty touches is phi.** that is not a formatting difference, it is a different legal instrument, and choosing wrong is the one mistake here that matters. use `--tier phi` alongside it when the agreement gates phi-scoped access. ## steps

entries.name: iris-atlas
entries.describe: IRIS Atlas
entries.haystack: iris-atlas iris atlas <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-atlas description: your data, queryable — the layer that owns its own schema. reach a board, define a typed dataset on it, write a record, read it back with filters and aggregates, and share it without handing over your account. from nothing to a queryable dataset in one sitting. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-atlas <board>` > steps: orient → schemas → define → write → share → verify # iris atlas **what it is:** the data layer — one of only three iris products that genuinely owns its schema. 12+ tables in fl-api (`atlas_schemas`, `atlas_records`, `atlas_record_field_index`, plus ledger, inventory, staff, zone and graph tables), served at `v1/atlas/*` in `fl-api/routes/api.php` (groups at ~2702, 2725, 2754, 2759) by `app/http/controllers/atlas/` over `app/services/atlas/`. define a shape once, put rows in it, and every row is filterable, searchable, aggregatable and serveable over rest — no migration. **what it is not:** - **not a notes app.** boards, lists and items are the *prose* half and a different storage engine from datasets. confusing the two is the most expensive mistake here. - **not multi-tenant.** atlas authorizes on `user_id` equality on the atlas row; board membership is not consulted anywhere in the dataset code path. see "the trap" — a wall, not a nuance. - **not a local spreadsheet.** `iris atlas export` gets your data off the servers; the queryable copy lives in fl-api. ## the vocabulary, because nothing else writes it down bloq / board ──has──> list ──has──> item the prose engine │ (cards, files, markdown, agents) └──tags──> schema ──has──> record the data engine └──── "dataset" ────┘ (typed rows, filterable, aggregatable) - **bloq / board** (`user_bloqs`) — the container, and **the only thing that can be shared**. exactly one owner: `user_bloqs.user_id`. `iris atlas list · get · members · invite · open`. - **list** (`user_bloq_lists`, fk → `user_bloqs`) and **item** (`user_bloq_items`, fk → the *list*) — columns and cards: free text, markdown, uploads. **an item has no `bloq_id`**; you reach the board through the list, which is why every item command wants a *list* id. - **schema** (`atlas_schemas`) — a dataset *definition*: slug, version, typed fields. `bloq_id` is **nullable**, so a schema can be tagged to a board or float free on the account (62 exist here; many read `bloq:—`). uniqueness is `(bloq_id, slug, version)`. - **record** (`atlas_records`) — one row against a schema. `schema_id` is a real fk with **on delete cascade**: dropping a schema takes every record with it. - **dataset** — not a table. it is the *pair*: schema plus records. that is what `iris atlas:datasets` operates on and what `atlas:datasets api <slug>` serves over rest. **items and records are different tables.** the only bridge is `user_bloq_items.atlas_schema_id` (nullable, no fk), which lets a card point at a *schema* — never at a record. a number you want to average is a record; a paragraph someone reads is an item. there is no convert. ## the trap: `editor` is not write access `iris atlas members <board>` will show a person as `[editor]`. that permission lives in `user_bloq_users` and governs **the board/list/item half only**. a membership check does exist — `bloqaccessscope::mayaccessbloq()`, "owner plus shared users" — and `bloqitemcontroller`, `bloqlistcontroller` and the genesis gated controllers all call it. **`atlasdatasetcontroller` never does.** every method there resolves the actor from the token and filters `where('user_id', $userid)` on the atlas row; `bloq_id` is a filter column, never a permission input. - **11 of 15 dataset methods are strictly owner-only** (`authuserid`): `listschemas`, `showschema`, `createschema`, `updateschema`, `deleteschema`, `createrecord`, `updaterecord`, `destroyrecord`, `upsertrecord`, `import`, `derive`. a member's write **404s as "schema not found"**, not 403 — it reads as *missing data* rather than *denied*. that is **#183281**. - **only 4 read methods widen at all** (`readuserid`): `listrecords`, `showrecord`, `summary`, `aggregate` — and only for an **internal service token** passing `as_user_id`, never for a human member. `listschemas` is not among them, which is exactly why a member's schema list comes back empty rather than denied: **#183303**. both confirmed in code today. - agents inherit that asymmetry deliberately: `v6toolregistry::executeanalyzedataset` passes `as_user_id`, while `executeupsertdatasetrecords` is commented "deliberately not modelled on executeanalyzedataset's as_user_id impersonation." **rule until those close: datasets belong to whoever created the board.** share the *output* — a feed token, a public item, the rest endpoint — not the write seat. ## steps

entries.haystack: iris-budget iris budget — what money exists and what it may do <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-budget description: the iris/free label operating budget — what money exists, which card it sits on, what it may be spent on, and the checks to run before proposing any spend. covers the two column virtual cards (iris + fl ads $50/week, bounty os $400/month), bounty escrow state, why ad spend is blocked on attribution, and the ledger discipline. pass an action as argument (e.g. "status", "escrow", "propose <thing>", "ads", "audit"). allowed-tools: - read - grep - glob - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-budget ` # iris budget — what money exists and what it may do the operating budget, the reasoning behind it, and the checks to run **before** proposing a spend. this is the authority on the figures; if a document or an agent disagrees with it, this wins and the other should be corrected. ## arguments | argument | does | |---|---| | `status` (default) | print both budgets, the period each covers, and what is committed | | `escrow` | show every live bounty's declared pool vs escrowed, and what to back next | | `ads` | answer "can we spend the ads budget yet" honestly | | `propose <thing>` | walk the justification checklist and write a ledger entry | | `audit` | re-verify every number in this playbook against live data | ## the money two ring-fenced virtual debit cards on **column n.a.** real money, not a paper limit. | card | budget | period | purpose | |---|---|---|---| | **iris + fl ads** | **$50** | per **week** | paid distribution and promotion | | **bounty os** | **$400** | per **month** | escrowing bounty pools so work can be paid | **the periods differ. do not average them into one number.** an unspent week or month does not roll over. the bounty os card was briefly set to a $400 *weekly* limit — about 4.3x the intent — and was corrected to monthly on 2026-08-20. if a bounty os week approaches $400, that is a red flag, not headroom. these replaced a $1,000 "discretionary budget" that existed only on paper. a budget nobody will release never tests anything; $100, then this, is money that can actually be drawn. ## standing rules 1. **nobody but alex moves money.** tobi (agent #642) has spend authority on paper and no payment tool — `config.tools` has no budget, ledger or card access. agents propose; alex releases. 2. **a limit is a ceiling, not a target.** a period ending at $0 spent is a good period unless something needed buying. 3. **justify before proposing**: what it buys, why now, and the cost of not doing it. 4. **the ledger is the bloq, not the card.** every proposed or approved expense gets an item in bloq #532 → "finance & budget" (#1545). the card cannot show a monthly running balance. 5. **paid advertising is a last resort, never the lead.** having a card for it changes nothing. collect revenue already won, wire billing, activate affiliates first. ## bounty os ($400/month) — the constraint is escrow, not ideas run `iris opportunities get <id> --json` and read `funding.escrowed_cents`, not `budget_pool_cents`. a declared pool is a promise; escrow is money. as of 2026-08-20 every live bounty declared a pool and held **$0**: | # | bounty | declared | escrowed | |---|---|---|---| | 692 | ugc reward (per views) | $250 | $0 | | 693 | deep-dive tutorial | $600 | $0 | | 695 | qualified introduction | $1,000 | $0 | | 696 | playbook bounty | $1,000 | $0 | | 662 | agentic graphic designer | unpriced | — (still in preview) | $2,850 declared. at $400/month, backing all of it takes **about seven months**, so they cannot all be promoted at once and choosing which to back is a real decision. **escrow before promotion, always.** a bounty nobody can be paid from is worse than no bounty: the first person to finish the work finds out, and then tells people. recommended first month: fully escrow **#692 ($250)**, leaving $150. it is the cheapest complete backing available and it is the one bounty whose result settles something (below). ## iris + fl ads ($50/week) — do not spend it on ads yet two concrete blockers, neither of which is money: 1. **no ad-buying integration exists on any channel.** spending means a human in an ad manager, not the platform. that is allowed — just never describe it as automated. (#164644 has been open since 12 jul; its own stated goal was per-post analytics "to decide which posts to promote as ads".) 2. **attribution does not exist.** `som_leads` has one free-text `source` field and nothing ties a view or click to a signup; `bounty_content_submissions` records creator, url and views — enough to pay, with no link to a lead. $50/week buys impressions and **no knowledge**. the unblock is a per-campaign code that survives into `som_leads.source`. that is engineering, not money, and it is the smallest item on the list. ### the highest-value use of $50 is buying a number, not attention bounty #692 pays $0.50 per 1,000 verified views, so **$50 buys 100,000 views** and the rail counts them itself. every acquisition figure in the pricing model rests on one unmeasured rate — view → signup → paid, assumed 0.1% × 5%. cac of $10 against $2,754 for ads, the 561-creator constraint, the whole ladder: all derived from that guess. **run it twice before believing it.** a single unrepeated result is an anecdote. ## before proposing any spend 1. is the thing it buys **measurable**? if not, say so in the proposal rather than implying it. 2. is there an **unspent commitment** ahead of it? escrow on a promoted bounty outranks new work. 3. what is the **cost of not doing it** this period? if the answer is "nothing", wait. 4. write the ledger entry **before** the money moves, not after. ## audit — re-verify rather than trust this page ## the trap that has already bitten once **the budget figure lives in more than one place.** on 2026-08-20 only tobi's `initial_prompt` was updated and the agent kept answering "$1,000", because a knowledge-base note in bloq #532 ("budget policy") is *retrieved* and outranked the prompt. when a figure changes, change **all** of: this playbook, tobi's `initial_prompt`, and the budget policy item in bloq #532 → #1545. otherwise the agent will confidently cite the one you forgot, and it will sound just as certain.
