entries.haystack: iris-cli iris cli — agent development kit (adk) & sdk <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-cli description: one command line for everything iris, so you're not hunting across five different tools to chat with an agent, check a lead, or read an email. product names you already know — genesis, reachr, pulse — just work as aliases, no separate manual to learn. pass an action or topic as argument. allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-cli ` # iris cli — agent development kit (adk) & sdk interact with the iris platform from the command line. two clis exist: - **`iris` (typescript, primary)** — installed at `~/.iris/bin/iris`, the main user-facing cli - **`php bin/iris` (php sdk, legacy)** — at `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris`, being sunsetted ## typescript iris cli — key commands (v1.1.19+) ### schedules (autonomous agent management) ### pages (genesis composable page builder) ### integrations ### playbooks — how they associate to entities playbooks are keyed by **name** (not fk). source of truth = `.iris/playbooks/<name>/playbook.md`; `iris playbook sync` projects each into `.claude/skills/<name>/skill.md` (auto-generated — never hand-edit the skill.md). they live in fl-iris-api `playbooks` table + local disk, not fl-api. the only persisted first-class link is **bloq → playbook name** in `bloqs.config.playbooks[]` (no migration). publish-scoping (private/project/public) is specced in `playbook-publish-associations-handoff.md` (#167269) — the `playbooks` table's nullable `user_id` + `scopeforuser` or-null currently leaks orphan playbooks to every user. ### searching what you've written (important — reach for this first) `iris search <query>` searches item **titles and content across every board you own**, plus board names. use it before asking where something lives — it is the answer to "did we already write this down?" both sections are always reported, including at zero — an empty "items (0)" means the phrase is genuinely absent, not that the capability is missing. ### bounty os — ledger checks without ssh `iris bounty admin` exposes the read-only reconciliation verbs that used to require `railway ssh -s fl-api -- php artisan bounty:invariants`. money-moving and attribution-rewriting commands stay artisan-only on purpose. ### sending communications — always through the router `iris imessage send` and `iris mail send` post to the comms router so the message lands in `lead_comms` with attribution. if the cli prints `not logged`, the message went out and the ledger does not know — report it, do not assume it was fine. never start the imessage bridge provider to test sending — it blasts auto-replies to real contacts (#137256). see the `comms-router` how-to for signatures and known bypasses. ### sender identities — who a message goes out as `iris senders` registers the identity a message signs and sends as. created unverified and draft-only until verified; nothing can sign as an identity that has not been established as yours. a sender with no binding for the channel refuses rather than sending from the default mailbox. delegated senders (writing on someone's behalf) are verbatim-only by default — a model may not write under that identity unless `metadata.allow_generated` is set deliberately. each sender carries its own channel order; with none set it uses the channels it is bound to, so a sender bound only to `email` is never routed onto `apple_mail` and then refused. `prefer` rejects a channel with no binding. note `default` picks the default identity, `prefer` picks that identity's transport. `--sender` needs a lead (or a handle that resolves to one) — the ad-hoc handle path bypasses the channel bindings, so a sender there is refused rather than signed-and-misdelivered. an unverified sender is a 422, never a quiet fallback. ### macos native — apple mail & imessage (important) when asked to read emails, check messages, or look up communications — use these first. they read directly from macos apps (apple mail, messages.app). no oauth, no api limits, full bodies. **when to use macos native vs gmail api integration:** - **macos native (iris mail)**: full email bodies, attachments visible, works offline, no api limits. use this first. - **gmail api (iris integrations exec gmail)**: only returns snippets (truncated). use only when macos mail.app doesn't have the account. ### health & monitoring ### agent-first heartbeat architecture (new) agents can now define their own mission, identity, and tools: - `settings.system_prompt` → overrides generic system prompt (agent identity) - `initial_prompt` → injected as `<agent_mission>` in goal (what to do) - `settings.heartbeat_tools` → filters available tools (e.g. `["manageleads", "agent_memory"]`) all fall back to defaults when empty. existing agents unchanged. --- ## php sdk cli (legacy — being sunsetted) ## arguments `$arguments` — action and target. examples: - `/iris-cli` — show help / available commands - `/iris-cli setup` — run interactive setup to configure credentials - `/iris-cli chat 11 "hello"` — chat with agent id 11 - `/iris-cli eval 387` — evaluate agent 387 with core test suite - `/iris-cli sdk agents.list` — list all agents - `/iris-cli sdk leads.search query=acme` — search leads - `/iris-cli sdk bloqs.uploadfile 40 /path/to/doc.pdf` — upload file to knowledge base - `/iris-cli new-command phonecommand` — read and explain an existing command - `/iris-cli add-command mycommand` — help create a new cli command --- ## cli location & configuration **cli binary:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris` **run from project root:** **or from anywhere using the full path:** **configuration (`.env` file in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/`):** --- ## commands reference ### run — unified tool & integration executor the `run` command is the universal entry point for executing any v6 system tool or integration function. **how it works:** the command automatically routes based on the target name: - `hive` → distributed compute (nodes, tasks, campaigns, dispatch) - known integration type (gmail, copycat-ai, servis-ai, whatsapp, etc.) → `integrationregistry` - everything else → `v6toolregistry` (system tools) **oauth flow:** `iris run --connect gmail` → gets oauth url from fl-api → opens browser → user authorizes → provider redirects back → fl-api stores tokens → `iris run --list-connected` shows it **hive flow (cloud dispatch):** `iris run hive dispatch type=whatsapp_scrape prompt="..."` → dispatches to connected hive node → daemon picks up task → executes playwright locally → returns result **hive flow (local script):** `iris hive script push ./report.sh` → pushes script to node → executes immediately → persists on disk. then `iris hive schedule add report.sh --cron "0 9 * * *"` → node runs it daily at 9am via local cron, even if cloud is offline **two dispatchers, same executor:** cloud scheduling (fl-api cron → pusher → daemon) and local scheduling (node-cron → daemon) both feed the same task executor. cloud for ai workflows. local for scripts that must run regardless. **parameter format:** `key=value` pairs. quotes for values with spaces: `query="austin, tx"` ### setup & config ### chat with agents ### agent evaluation (adk) the `eval` command is the core adk evaluation harness. it runs structured test scenarios against agents to validate performance, prompt quality, and configuration. **evaluation test types:** | type | description | |------|-------------| | `core` (default) | 7 built-in scenarios covering general capability | | `custom` | custom scenarios defined in the agent config | | `comparison` | a/b test with and without web search | ### sdk method calls (`sdk:call`) the `sdk:call` command is a dynamic proxy to any sdk resource and method. format: `resource.method [params]`. ### cloud upload (files, images, content) **full documentation**: see `sdk/php/docs/cloud_upload.md` or [freelabel.net/p/iris-cloud-upload]( ### outreach (strategies, campaigns, send) three commands manage the full outreach pipeline: strategy templates, campaigns, and per-lead execution. #### `outreach:strategy` — multi-step strategy templates **merge fields** (usable in step scripts): `{name}`, `{first_name}`, `{company}`, `{email}`, `{phone}`, `{instagram}`, `{social_handle}`, `{price_bid}`, `{notes}` **step types**: `instagram`, `email`, `sms`, `phone`, `linkedin`, `visit`, `other` **categories**: `cold_outreach`, `follow_up`, `nurture`, `high_value`, `quick_touch`, `custom` #### `outreach:campaign` — campaign lifecycle management **campaign types**: `one_time`, `recurring`, `drip`, `broadcast` **channels**: `email`, `sms`, `instagram_dm`, `linkedin`, `multi_channel` #### `outreach:send` — per-lead outreach actions ### leads / crm (`leads` or `crm`) full crm lead management with list, search, show, notes, and stats. **filters for `list`:** | option | description | |--------|-------------| | `--status=x` | filter by status (new, won, follow up, lost, in negotiation, prospected, etc.) | | `--search=x` | search by name/email/company | | `--bloq=x` | filter by bloq/board id | | `--sort=x` | sort field: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `price_bid` (default: `updated_at`) | | `--order=x` | sort order: `asc` or `desc` (default: `desc`) | | `--page=n` | page number (default: 1) | | `--limit=n` | results per page (default: 25) | for lower-level sdk operations (create, update, delete, sub-resources): ### page theming / brand colors when managing pages for different brands, set accent colors explicitly in the page json rather than relying on component defaults. key props: - **`accentcolor`** — used by statssection, featuretabs, featuregrid, servicelisting, editorialsection, communitycta, processsteps, timelinecarousel, gettingstartedsteps, pricingrows - **`labelcolor`** — used by hero, quoteblock (for small label text above headings) - **`ctacolor`** — used by sitenavigation (cta button color) component defaults (when no color is passed): emerald green (`#34d399` / `text-emerald-400`). always override for brand-specific pages. ### other commands ### pages (composable page builder) full page management via rest api. no ssh, no tty, no seeders. see `/pages` skill for complete docs. ### shared partials — `iris partials` shared component configs referenced by pages via `$partial`. edit one partial, all consuming pages update instantly. resolved server-side by `pagecontroller::resolvepartials()`. page json references a partial like: `{ "type": "sitenavigation", "$partial": "vanguard-nav", "props": {} }`. page-level props override partial defaults. see `/pages` skill for full docs. ### entity sync (typescript cli — `iris-code`) pull, push, and diff agents, workflows, leads, and board items as local json files. mirrors the pages pull/push/diff pattern. requires `iris_api_key` and `iris_user_id` env vars (or `iris auth login`). **local storage convention:** #### agents — `iris agents` #### workflows — `iris workflows` #### leads — `iris leads` #### boards (bloqitems) — `iris boards` #### opportunities — `iris opportunities` (alias: `iris opps`) #### services — `iris services` #### products — `iris products` #### events — `iris events` #### venues — `iris venues` (alias: `iris studios`) #### programs & packages — `iris programs` **source files:** `iris-code/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/platform-{agents,workflows,leads,boards,opportunities,services,products,events,venues,programs}.ts` ### opportunities (marketplace job postings) manage marketplace opportunities (gig postings, hiring, freelance jobs). full crud, json pull/push, bulk seed, publish lifecycle. ### packages (platform pricing) manage platform pricing packages with local json as source of truth. push changes to production without ssh. --- ## available commands (full list) | command | description | |---------|-------------| | `run` | **unified executor** — call any tool or integration: `iris run gmail search_emails query="test"`, `iris run searchplaces query="pizza"` | | **typescript cli (iris-code)** | **entity sync commands — pull/push/diff local json** | | `iris agents pull/push/diff <id>` | sync agents as `.iris/agents/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete, chat | | `iris workflows pull/push/diff <id>` | sync workflows as `.iris/workflows/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete, run, status | | `iris leads pull/push/diff <id>` | sync leads as `.iris/leads/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, search, create, update, delete, note | | `iris boards pull/push/diff <id>` | sync board items as `.iris/boards/{bloqid}/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris opportunities pull/push/diff <id>` | sync opportunities as `.iris/opportunities/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, delete | | `iris services pull/push/diff <id>` | sync services as `.iris/services/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris products pull/push/diff <id>` | sync products as `.iris/products/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris events pull/push/diff <id>` | sync events as `.iris/events/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete | | `iris venues pull/push/diff <id>` | sync venues as `.iris/venues/{id}-{slug}.json` — also: list, get, create, update, delete. alias: `iris studios` | | `iris programs pull/push/diff <id>` | sync programs as `.iris/programs/{id}-{slug}.json` (includes packages) — also: list, get, create, update, delete, packages, package-create/update/delete | | `setup` | interactive credential setup (creates .env) | | `config` | manage stored credentials | | `chat` | chat with an ai agent (real-time progress) | | `eval` | evaluate agent performance with test scenarios | | `sdk:call` | dynamic proxy to any sdk resource.method | | `agent` | agent management (create, list, update) | | `agent:create` | create a new agent | | `app` | app-level operations | | `automation` | workflow automation management | | `automation:test` | test an automation workflow | | `bloq:ingest` | ingest files into a knowledge base | | `bloq:ingest-status` | check ingestion job status | | `bloq:ingestion-jobs` | list ingestion jobs for a bloq | | `bloq:cancel-ingestion` | cancel an ingestion job | | `cloud:upload` | upload files to cloud storage, get cdn + share urls ([full docs]( | | `bloqs:members` / `members` / `team` | manage bloq team members (overview, list, add, invite, update, remove) | | `monitor` | platform health monitoring and heartbeat diagnostics (overview, agent, loops, kill) | | `deliver` | deliver files/artifacts to leads | | `demo-showcase` | run a demo showcase | | `diary` | view/manage agent daily diary (today, list, view, add) | | `integrations` | manage platform integrations | | `leads` / `crm` | lead/crm management — list, show, search, notes, stats (filterable, paginated) | | `leads:consolidate` | consolidate duplicate leads | | `outreach:strategy` | manage outreach strategy templates (list, show, create, update, apply, duplicate, delete, metadata) | | `outreach:campaign` | campaign lifecycle management (list, show, create, start, pause, resume, cancel, schedule, analytics, recipients) | | `outreach:send` | per-lead outreach actions (list, show, vary, personalize, copy, open, complete, send, apply, invalid) | | `memory:add` / `memory:list` / `memory:show` / `memory:compose` | agent memory management | | `opportunities` | marketplace opportunities — list, view, create, pull, push, seed, publish, unpublish, delete, applications | | `packages` | platform pricing management — list, pull, push, diff, set (local json → production sync) | | `pages` | page builder cli (see `/pages` skill for full docs) | | `payments` | stripe payment history (read-only view) | | `invoices` | invoice management — create, checkout, send (list/create/show/checkout/send subcommands) | | `phone` | voice agent phone management | | `profile` | profile management — show, get/set (dot-notation), links, memberships | | `remind-r` | reminder system | | `schedule` | agent scheduling | | `servis-ai` | servis.ai strategic partner integration | | `skills` | platform skills management | | `sop` | standard operating procedure management | | `token` | api token management | | `tools` | tool registry inspection | | `users` | user management | | `v6:chat` | v6 react loop chat | | `voice` | voice configuration | | `wallet` | wallet and credit balance | --- ## sdk structure (php) **source:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/` --- ## node.js sdk **location:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/node/` **package:** `@iris-ai/sdk` **language:** typescript with full type safety --- ## iris code (opencode fork) the iris code terminal ai assistant is a separate tool: **location:** `iris-code/` **install:** **key agents (press tab to switch):** - `build` — full access for development - `plan` — read-only mode for analysis - `general` — complex searches with `@general` --- ## creating a new cli command when asked to add a new command to the iris cli: ### step 1: read an existing similar command for reference ### step 2: create the new command class follow this structure in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/mycommand.php`: ### step 3: register the command in application.php add to the `getdefaultcommands()` or `configure()` method: --- ## steps ### 1. parse the argument determine what the user wants: | argument | action | |----------|--------| | (empty) | show all available commands with descriptions | | `setup` | guide through running `php bin/iris setup` | | `chat <id> "<msg>"` | run the chat command, show output | | `eval <id>` | run agent evaluation | | `sdk <resource.method> [params]` | run sdk:call command | | `new-command <name>` | read and explain an existing command file | | `add-command <name>` | create a new command class + register it | | any other command name | run or explain that command | ### 2. run cli commands always use the full path. run from within the sdk directory context: **important**: the cli requires a `.env` file in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/`. if it doesn't exist, run `php bin/iris setup` first. ### 3. working with command output most commands support `--json` for machine-readable output. use this when processing results programmatically. ### 4. adding new sdk capabilities when asked to extend the sdk: 1. check existing resource classes in `src/resources/` 2. follow the existing pattern (constructor receives iris client, methods map to api endpoints) 3. add corresponding cli command in `src/console/commands/` 4. register in `src/console/application.php` --- ## key notes - **cli binary is php** — requires php in path (use docker if not installed locally) - **credentials**: stored in `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/.env`, set via `php bin/iris setup` - **all commands support `--api-key` and `--user-id`** flags to override .env credentials - **`sdk:call` is the swiss army knife** — any sdk method is accessible via `resource.method` - **`eval` is the adk harness** — use it to validate agent quality before deploying to production - **node sdk** exists at `fl-docker-dev/sdk/node/` for typescript projects - **iris cli** (`iris-code/`) is the terminal ai coding assistant (typescript, built on opencode fork). branded "iris cli" everywhere — never "iris code" --- ## building & releasing the iris cli **repo:** `freelabel/iris-opencode` (git remote in `iris-code/`) ### branching strategy - **`dev`** — default branch. all work goes here. multiple sessions can push freely. - **`main`** — protected, releases only. requires a pr from `dev`. - never push directly to `main`. ### release flow ### local build (for testing) ### version bumping version lives in `packages/opencode/package.json`. bump it in the release commit: ### important - gh release titles must say **"iris cli"**, not "iris code" - the `--skip-install` flag avoids playwright-core resolution errors from root node_modules - build produces binaries for all platforms (linux, darwin, windows × arm64, x64) - **never force-push tags** — it corrupts github's release ordering and causes `iris update` to downgrade customers ### release emergency runbook #### `iris update` is downgrading customers **symptom**: customer runs `iris update` and goes from v1.3.63 → v1.3.52 (or any older version). **cause**: a force-pushed tag recreated an old github release, and github's `/releases/latest` api returns it based on creation timestamp, not semver. **fix**: **prevention**: never `git push --tags --force`. if you need to re-tag, delete the old tag first: #### customer gets `[1] killed iris` **symptom**: binary downloaded but macos kills it immediately on execution. **cause**: macos gatekeeper quarantine attribute (`com.apple.quarantine`) on downloaded binary. **fix (v1.3.64+)**: the installer now strips quarantine automatically via `xattr -cr`. **customer recovery** (if they're on an older version that can't self-update): this is the only fix they need. one command, no tech knowledge. do not ask them to run `xattr` manually. #### `iris --version` shows `0.0.0-dev-*` **cause**: a local `bun run build --single --install` overwrote the release binary with a dev build. **fix**: `iris update` or manually download the release binary: #### hotfix needed but pre-push hook blocks **symptom**: typescript errors in unrelated files block `git push origin main`. **fix**: for emergency hotfixes only: then immediately fix the ts errors and push a clean commit. do not leave `--no-verify` pushes as the last commit. #### ci builds but release doesn't appear **cause**: tag didn't trigger the workflow, or workflow failed. **fix**:

entries.name: iris-cli-roadmap
entries.describe: IRIS CLI Roadmap
entries.haystack: iris-cli-roadmap iris cli roadmap <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-cli-roadmap description: manage the iris cli roadmap — track parity between the canonical iris-cli (node/opencode fork) and the php sdk cli being sunsetted, decide where new features go, and run the migration. pass an action as argument (status, gap, port, add, audit, sunset-check, naming). allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-cli-roadmap ` # iris cli roadmap manages the migration of cli features from the **php sdk cli** (sunsetting) to **`iris-cli`** (the canonical node/opencode fork). tracks parity, prioritizes ports, routes new feature decisions, and gates the eventual removal of the php cli. ## ⚠️ naming — read this first, it is the entire point of this skill there has been confusion about which thing is called what. **lock these definitions in:** | name | what it actually is | lifecycle | repo path | |---|---|---|---| | **`iris-cli`** | node cli built on the opencode fork. **the canonical iris command line going forward.** | growing → permanent | `iris-code/packages/opencode/` (repo: `freelabel/iris-opencode`) | | **`php-sdk`** | php integration library + thin cli wrapper. the cli portion is **being sunsetted**; the sdk library stays forever. | cli shrinks to zero, sdk lives on | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/` | | **`node-sdk`** | typescript sdk library (no cli). | lives alongside php-sdk | `fl-docker-dev/sdk/node/` | **aliases that have caused confusion in the past:** - ❌ "iris-opencode" — internal nickname for the iris-cli source repo. don't use externally; it's just `iris-cli`. - ❌ "iris-cli (php)" — was an early name for the php sdk's bundled cli. officially this is now **`php-sdk` cli** or **php-sdk** for short. treat any reference to "iris-cli" without a qualifier as meaning the **node** one. - ❌ "v1 / v2" — was considered for naming the two clis. **rejected.** naming by purpose ages better than naming by version. there's no v1; there's `php-sdk` (sunset) and `iris-cli` (canonical). **strategic direction:** 1. build out `iris-cli` to feature parity with `php-sdk` cli 2. stop adding new features to `php-sdk` cli (defaults go to iris-cli) 3. when parity is reached + nobody is using `php-sdk` cli commands → delete the php cli portion entirely 4. `php-sdk` becomes pure sdk library, no cli binary **known follow-up (out of scope for this skill):** the existing `.claude/skills/iris-cli/skill.md` currently points at the php cli binary (`fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris`) and contradicts the naming above. it needs to be repointed at `iris-code/packages/opencode/bin/iris` once iris-cli reaches enough parity that pointing users at it won't strand them. track this in `parity.yaml` under `meta.followups`. --- ## arguments `$arguments` — action and optional target. examples: - `/iris-cli-roadmap` or `/iris-cli-roadmap status` — show current state of the migration - `/iris-cli-roadmap naming` — print the naming table above (for when someone is confused) - `/iris-cli-roadmap gap` — show what's in `php-sdk` cli that's missing from `iris-cli` - `/iris-cli-roadmap gap <command>` — detail on a specific gap - `/iris-cli-roadmap port <command>` — walk through porting a single command from php-sdk → iris-cli - `/iris-cli-roadmap add <feature>` — decision tree: where should this new feature go? - `/iris-cli-roadmap audit` — re-extract both clis' command lists and show diffs vs `parity.yaml` - `/iris-cli-roadmap sunset-check` — are we ready to delete the php cli? run the gate checklist. - `/iris-cli-roadmap parity-only-php` — list php-sdk-only commands (the gap) - `/iris-cli-roadmap parity-only-node` — list iris-cli-only commands (the lead) --- ## source files (where to read/write actual code) ### `iris-cli` (node — canonical) - **command directory:** `iris-code/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/` - **platform commands** (the ones that map to php-sdk cli features): files prefixed `platform-*.ts` - **native opencode commands** (coding agent stuff, not in scope for parity): `acp.ts`, `agent.ts`, `auth.ts`, `debug/`, `generate.ts`, `github.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `models.ts`, `run.ts`, `serve.ts`, `session.ts`, `transcribe.ts`, `tui/`, `web.ts`, `upgrade.ts`, `uninstall.ts`, `pr.ts`, `stats.ts`, `import.ts`, `export.ts` - **binary:** `iris-code/packages/opencode/bin/iris` (after build) or installed at `~/.iris/bin/iris` - **build:** `cd iris-code/packages/opencode && bun run build -- --single` then copy `dist/opencode-darwin-arm64/bin/iris` to `~/.iris/bin/iris` - **repo:** `git@github.com:freelabel/iris-opencode.git` ### `php-sdk` cli (sunsetting) - **command directory:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/` - **naming convention:** `<name>command.php` - **binary:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris` - **run:** `php fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris <command>` or via the symlink at `~/.iris/sdk/bin/iris` ### parity matrix (this skill's source of truth) - **file:** `.claude/skills/iris-cli-roadmap/parity.yaml` - hand-curated. the `audit` action re-extracts both clis' command lists and reports what's drifted from the yaml, but does not auto-edit it. --- ## how each action works ### `status` — current state of the migration read `parity.yaml`. print: - total commands in php-sdk cli - total commands in iris-cli (platform-*) - how many are at parity (in both, or in iris-cli only) - how many are gaps (php-sdk-only, not yet ported) - the top 5 gaps marked `priority: high` in the yaml - last `audit` timestamp from `meta.last_audit` ### `naming` print the naming table from the top of this file. use this when anyone in the codebase or in conversation is confused about which thing is which. ### `gap` — what's in php-sdk cli but missing from iris-cli read `parity.yaml`. list all entries where `iris_cli: missing`. show: - command name (php-sdk side) - what it does (one-line `description` from the yaml) - priority (`high` / `medium` / `low`) - notes (any porting blockers, dependencies) if `<command>` argument provided, show the full entry for that command including `php_sdk_path` and any porting notes. ### `port <command>` — walk through porting one command for the given command name: 1. read `parity.yaml` entry for it. confirm it's marked `iris_cli: missing`. 2. read the php source file at `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/src/console/commands/<name>command.php`. summarize: - what it does - which iris api endpoints it calls - required arguments / options - any auth/setup prerequisites 3. identify which iris-cli `platform-*.ts` file it should live in (existing file? new file?) 4. look at a similar existing iris-cli command for the structural template 5. write the new typescript command, register it in the appropriate root command's `.command()` chain 6. build iris-cli (`bun run build -- --single`), install to `~/.iris/bin/iris` 7. test it manually 8. update `parity.yaml`: change `iris_cli: missing` → `iris_cli: <new-file>.ts`, set `ported_at` to today's date 9. commit to `iris-opencode` with message `port <command> from php-sdk cli` ### `add <feature>` — decision tree for new features when someone wants to add a new cli feature, route them: 1. **default: add it to `iris-cli`.** always. 2. **exceptions where you'd add to `php-sdk` cli instead:** - the feature is *only* needed by an existing php sdk consumer who can't be migrated - the feature wraps a php-only library or workflow (extremely rare) - there's a hard deadline and porting it later is acceptable 3. **if both:** add to iris-cli first, then mirror to php-sdk cli as a thin wrapper that just calls the same fl-api endpoint. mark it in `parity.yaml` with `port_strategy: dual`. 4. **never:** add a feature to `php-sdk` cli that doesn't exist in iris-cli without first checking with the team. every such addition makes the sunset further away. when invoked, ask the user the 3 questions above and write a recommendation. ### `audit` — re-extract both clis' command lists run the `audit.sh` script in this skill folder: it outputs: - all `*command.php` files in php-sdk (normalized to lowercase command names) - all `platform-*.ts` files in iris-cli (normalized similarly) - diff vs `parity.yaml`: - **new in php-sdk** (added to php cli but not in yaml — should be either ported immediately or formally added to the gap list) - **new in iris-cli** (added to node but not in yaml — likely already-ported, update the yaml to reflect reality) - **vanished from php-sdk** (was in yaml, no longer in source — was it deleted? rename?) - **vanished from iris-cli** (was marked as ported, file gone — regression?) then prompt the user to update `parity.yaml` accordingly. ### `sunset-check` — are we ready to delete the php cli? run the gate checklist: 1. ✅ **parity reached:** `gap` returns zero entries marked `priority: high` or `medium` 2. ✅ **usage zero:** check fl-api logs for any api calls coming from php-sdk cli's user agent string in the last 30 days (`php-sdk-cli/*`). if any, list which users. 3. ✅ **docs updated:** all `docs/`, `readme.md`, and `claude.md` mentions of `iris-cli` referring to php have been updated to point at the node cli. grep for `bin/iris` and `php.*iris` patterns. 4. ✅ **existing iris-cli skill updated:** `.claude/skills/iris-cli/skill.md` repointed at the node binary. 5. ✅ **announcement sent:** check `parity.yaml.meta.sunset_announced_at` is set. 6. ✅ **composer package marked:** `fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/composer.json` has `"deprecated-cli": true` or similar marker for one full release cycle. if all 6 are green, output the deletion plan. if any are red, list what's blocking. ### `parity-only-php` / `parity-only-node` quick filters on the yaml. the first lists everything that's only in php-sdk (the gap). the second lists everything that's only in iris-cli (features that exist on node but never existed on php — proves the migration isn't a regression). --- ## decision shortcuts (for quick chats with the user) **"should i add this command to iris-cli or the php one?"** → iris-cli. always. run `add <feature>` if you need the formal decision tree, but the default answer is iris-cli unless you can name a specific reason it can't go there. **"why does the iris-cli skill point at the php binary?"** → historical. the existing `.claude/skills/iris-cli/skill.md` was written when "iris-cli" meant the php one. it needs to be repointed once iris-cli is parity-complete. tracked in `parity.yaml.meta.followups`. **"how do i run the canonical iris-cli right now?"** → `iris <command>` (installed at `~/.iris/bin/iris` from the iris-opencode build). the php one is `php fl-docker-dev/sdk/php/bin/iris <command>`. if both binaries exist on the user's path, the node one wins because of installer precedence. **"is the php cli dead?"** → not yet. it's the production tool today. it's being sunsetted gradually as iris-cli reaches parity. use it freely, but don't add new features to it without checking the parity matrix. --- ## files in this skill - `skill.md` — this file (entry point + naming definitions) - `parity.yaml` — the parity matrix (hand-curated, source of truth) - `audit.sh` — re-extracts both clis' command lists for diffing against the yaml ## verification after any action that updates `parity.yaml`, run `audit` to confirm the yaml still matches reality. if the audit reports drift, fix the yaml before proceeding.

entries.name: iris-discord-agents
entries.describe: IRIS Discord Agents — Setup, Debugging & Maintenance
entries.haystack: iris-discord-agents iris discord agents — setup, debugging & maintenance <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-discord-agents description: manage, debug, and maintain discord bot agents connected to the iris v6 engine. covers bridge config, workflow_channels, agent selection, deployment, and production debugging. pass an action as argument (e.g., "status", "debug", "add-bot", "update-agent"). allowed-tools: - read - edit - write - grep - glob - bash - task --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-discord-agents ` # iris discord agents — setup, debugging & maintenance manage discord bots that connect to the iris v6 engine via the coding-agent-bridge. ## arguments `$arguments` — action to perform. examples: - `/iris-discord-agents status` — check bridge health, bot connections, and recent logs - `/iris-discord-agents debug` — investigate why the bot isn't responding - `/iris-discord-agents add-bot <bloq_id>` — wire up a new discord bot for a bloq - `/iris-discord-agents update-agent <agent_id> <model>` — change which model an agent uses - `/iris-discord-agents deploy` — sync bridge code to droplet and restart - `/iris-discord-agents logs` — tail production logs (bridge + iris-api worker) --- ## architecture overview ### two routing modes | mode | trigger | agent used | scope | |------|---------|------------|-------| | **god mode** | dm to bot (no guild_id) | user's general agent (`user->generalagent()`) | full cross-bloq access | | **project mode** | @mention in server | agent from `workflow_channels.agent_id` | bloq-scoped only | --- ## key infrastructure ### bridge (droplet) - **location**: `fl-web-prod` droplet at `134.199.214.232` - **code**: `/opt/coding-agent-bridge/production.js` - **config**: `/opt/coding-agent-bridge/.env` - **process manager**: pm2 (`pm2 list`, `pm2 logs coding-agent-bridge`) - **source**: `fl-docker-dev/coding-agent-bridge/production.js` **key env vars:** ### resilience (3 layers) 1. **pm2 auto-restart** — restarts on crash (built-in) 2. **systemd pm2-root.service** — restarts pm2 on server reboot 3. **cron health check** — `*/5 * * * * curl -sf > /dev/null || pm2 restart coding-agent-bridge` ### iris-api (v6 engine) - **app id**: `68ad4e37-3502-4681-8f28-9c5725044dce` - **branch**: `beta/heartbeat-groundhog` (deploy_on_push: true) - **worker**: `fl-iris-worker` (processes async queue jobs) ### database tables - **`iris_db.workflow_channels`** — maps discord servers/dms to bloqs/agents with bot credentials - **`freelabelnet.bloq_agents`** — agent configs including model (stored in `config` json as `$.model`) --- ## common operations ### check status ### deploy bridge code changes ### deploy iris-api changes ### change agent model **supported models for discord agents:** - `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning` — xai grok (recommended, fast with reasoning) - `grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning` — xai grok (faster, no reasoning) - `gpt-4o` — openai (caution: production key may be exhausted) - `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` — google gemini (automatic fallback if openai fails) ### add a new discord bot for a bloq ### remove a discord bot --- ## debugging guide ### bot not responding at all 1. **check bridge health:** - is `messaging.discord.status` = "running"? - is the bot `ready: true`? 2. **check bridge logs for forward errors:** - `unexpected token '<'` = bridge pointing at frontend url, not api - `forward error` = iris-api endpoint unreachable or returning errors 3. **check iris-api logs:** - `skip_reason: "not_mentioned"` = bot @mention format mismatch (check bot_id in workflow_channels config) - `channel not found` = no workflow_channels record for this guild_id - `500` responses = check for php exceptions in the log ### bot accepts message but no reply 1. **check worker logs for job failures:** 2. **common failures:** - `serializesmodels` crash = virtual channel without db id (must use firstorcreate) - `unknown named parameter` = reactloopservice signature mismatch - `class not found` = missing model class (wrap in try/catch) - `failed to read fastcgi header` = http timeout (sync processing took too long — must use async queue) 3. **check the ai is responding:** - `openai quota exhausted` = key dead, falling back to gemini - `making chat request` with correct model = ai is being called - `execution complete` with `response_length > 0` = ai responded 4. **check discord api response sending:** - if missing: bot_token may be wrong or discord api rejecting the message ### bot responds but wrong agent - **dms** always route to `user->generalagent()` (god mode). to change which agent handles dms, update the general agent's config/model. - **server @mentions** use the agent from `workflow_channels.agent_id`. check: ### bot responds but wrong model check the agent's model in the config json: the v6aiservice model resolution chain: 1. agent's `config.model` → used directly 2. if openai model + quota exhausted → falls back to `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` 3. grok models (`grok-*`) → routed to ` via `xai_api_key` --- ## key files ### bridge (node.js) | file | purpose | |------|---------| | `fl-docker-dev/coding-agent-bridge/production.js` | main bridge — discord gateway connection, message forwarding, history fetching | | `/opt/coding-agent-bridge/.env` (droplet) | runtime config — api urls, bot tokens, bloq ids | ### iris-api (php/laravel) | file | purpose | |------|---------| | `app/http/controllers/v6/unifiedchannelcontroller.php` | entry point — detects channel type, finds workflow_channels record, dispatches job | | `app/services/v6/channels/adapters/discordadapter.php` | parses discord payloads, sends responses via discord rest api | | `app/services/v6/channels/channelmessagerouter.php` | god mode vs project mode routing, onevent progress callbacks | | `app/services/v6/channels/parsedmessage.php` | value object for parsed messages | | `app/jobs/processchannelmessage.php` | async queue job — calls router + sends response | | `app/services/v6/reactloopservice.php` | core ai execution — tool calling, rag, conversation history | | `app/services/v6/v6aiservice.php` | ai provider routing — openai, grok (xai), gemini fallback | ### database | table | db | purpose | |-------|----|---------| | `workflow_channels` | `iris_db` | discord server/dm → bloq/agent mapping with bot_token | | `bloq_agents` | `freelabelnet` | agent configs including model (`config->$.model`) | --- ## progress updates (tool call visibility) the bot posts progress messages to discord as it works: this is powered by the `onevent` callback in `channelmessagerouter::makediscordprogresscallback()`. tool emoji mappings: | tool | emoji | |------|-------| | managebloqitemstool | 📋 | | searchknowledgebasetool | 🔍 | | activitylog | 📅 | | workflow-composer | ⚙️ | | composepage | 🎨 | | agent_memory | 🧠 | | httprequest | 🌐 | | marketplacepurchasetool | 🛒 | --- ## production database access --- ## current bot inventory | bot | discord user | bloq | agent | model | server | |-----|-------------|------|-------|-------|--------| | iris ai#8500 | `1466253034584670464` | 38 | 473 (dj ghost, server) / 69 (general, dms) | `grok-4-1-fast-reasoning` | freelabel (`872124790876549170`) | --- ## known issues & workarounds 1. **externalaccount model not found** — warning on every dm (non-fatal). the `externalaccounts` relationship on user references a model that doesn't exist. caught by try/catch, falls back to channel owner. 2. **openai quota exhausted** — production openai key is dead. agents using `gpt-4o` fall back to `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`. use grok models to avoid this entirely. 3. **billing tracking 401** — `fl_raichu_api_token` in iris-api is expired. ai usage isn't tracked for billing. needs a fresh passport token from fl-api. 4. **bloqrag/searchknowledgebasetool 429** — uses openai embeddings which also fail with the dead key. rag search returns errors but the agent continues with other tools. 5. **no ui for discord agent management** — `workflow_channels` mapping is db-only. no frontend settings page exists yet for linking discord servers to bloqs/agents.

entries.name: iris-genesis
entries.describe: IRIS Genesis — from nothing to a page a stranger can open
entries.haystack: iris-genesis iris genesis — from nothing to a page a stranger can open <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-genesis description: ship a page on iris genesis from nothing — pick the lane, create it, edit it, prove it renders, and control who can reach it. the path that ends in a url a stranger can open, and the four states along it that look alike and are not. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-genesis <slug>` > steps: surface → create → state → push → verify → reach → done # iris genesis — from nothing to a page a stranger can open **what it is:** the page system — composable pages, sites, and a stored **component library**. `iris genesis` and `iris pages` are the same command group. it owns `pages`, `page_versions`, `page_sites`, `page_partials`, `page_views`, `page_analytics` and `page_share_links`, plus `code_components` / `code_component_versions` behind the library. **what it is not: a static site generator.** a page is a **json document in a database**, rendered on request and **cached**. no build, and no file that is the truth — `./pages/<slug>.json` is a working copy. nor is it git: `versions` and `rollback` exist, but there is no branch, no merge, and `pull` overwrites local edits without asking. ## the two lanes — choose before writing a line composable standalone (render_mode: "html") json_content.components: [...] json_content: raw css + html platform components, props, slots your own document, your own css inherits the genesis shell + theme inherits nothing genesis create / push genesis publish-html --file x.html verify --lane composable verify --lane bespoke not two styles of one thing — moving between them is a rewrite. assert which renderer served the request with `verify --lane`; a page that fell back to the wrong lane still renders *something*. ## four states that look alike exists ──> published ──> reachable ──> rendering what you wrote │ │ │ └─ the cache was purged │ │ └─ visibility public/unlisted, no otp gate │ └─ status == published (`create` already did this) └─ a row with a slug - **`create` publishes.** no draft on the way in: it returns `status: published`, `visibility: public`, and a stranger gets http 200 immediately. verified 2026-09-02. - **`push` un-publishes.** pushing local json to a **live** page drops it to `draft` and the url starts returning **404**. `--publish` is what you wanted, every time. - **published is not rendering your change.** `set` edits the record; the cache keeps serving the old render, and nothing in the output distinguishes the two. - **404 does not mean broken.** draft, `private`, and a nonexistent slug 404 identically — `check-public` is the only command that says what a stranger actually gets. ## steps

entries.name: iris-heartbeat
entries.describe: IRIS Heartbeat
entries.haystack: iris-heartbeat iris heartbeat <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-heartbeat description: hand an agent a project instead of a task. give it a schedule, a diary it reads before it acts, and a mode that decides how much it may do on its own — then read the fleet honestly enough to tell a working agent from one that has been dark for four months. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-heartbeat ` > steps: fleet → read → agent → mode → kill → cadence # iris heartbeat **what it is:** autonomous agent scheduling with continuity. an agent wakes on a cadence, reads the diary of what the last wake did, looks at the project as it stands now, acts with full tool access, and writes the entry its successor will read. sold standalone as `iris-heartbeat-monthly`, $149/mo, compute class *heavy* — the price of a thing that thinks unattended. **what it is not: a cron.** a cron re-runs a command. heartbeat's product is the *diary* — what makes wake #40 aware of wake #39. strip that out and you have the scheduler iris already had. **nor is it pulse** ($99/mo, `iris-pulse-monthly`), which scores relationships and accounts. two skus, two subjects, one unfortunate word. ## the name collision — the single biggest trap here **`iris heartbeat` is not this product.** it hits `/api/v1/users/{id}/heartbeat` → `clientreadinessservice::foruserheartbeat()`, a **filtered subset of pulse's signal registry**; `iris heartbeat signals` prints two columns headed `pulse (agency)` and `heartbeat (you)`. one registry, two audience flags, nothing to do with agents. **this product's command is `iris monitor`** (`/api/v6/agents/heartbeat-status`), plus `iris schedules`, `iris agents update`, `iris diary`. `iris health` reaches only one of `doctor`/`monitor`/`heartbeat` — a ratcheted collision in `command-collisions.test.ts`. the word means a *third* thing in `fl-iris-api` (compute-node check-ins), which is why `routes/console.php` named its scheduler check `liveness` instead. ## the six modes off excluded from every fleet view. the only mode that means "not running". passive observes and records. no action. reactive acts when something happens to the project, not on a clock. briefing read-only morning digest — inbox, calendar, project — synthesised and sent. co-pilot decides, then files a task for a human to approve before anything executes. autonomous acts. full tool access, no approval gate. **`co-pilot` exists in the database and cannot be set from the cli.** the enum was widened by `2026_05_26_000001_add_copilot_mode_and_workflow_to_heartbeat.php`; `platform-agents.ts` still lists five choices and rejects the sixth, though four production agents run it. until that catches up, set it via `put /api/v1/bloqs/agents/{id}/heartbeat`. ## the states everyone misreads - **`last_heartbeat_at: null` is not broken.** `briefing` and `reactive` never stamp it — null is their normal steady state. reading null as dead condemns seven healthy agents. - **a mode is a setting, not a pulse.** `autonomous` with a four-month-old `last_heartbeat_at` is the #179799 failure: jobs due on time, skipped on time, output zero. reads *configured*, is *dark*. - **heartbeat has no cron of its own, on purpose.** it rides `agents:process-jobs --sync --limit=50` every minute, same pipeline as every other agent job. `kernel.php` calls it "the canary": if heartbeats stop, agent scheduling is broken, and a private cron would have hidden that. - **`due_within_30min` includes long-overdue jobs** — "due soon *or* past due". read the timestamp. - **the 2-hour staleness threshold is `health:check`'s, not the agent's.** anything legitimately on `every_8_hours` trips it six times a day. the breaker window is 7 days. ## steps

entries.name: iris-hive
entries.describe: IRIS Hive — Compute Mesh Management
entries.haystack: iris-hive iris hive — compute mesh management <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-hive description: run ai work across the machines you already own instead of paying for compute you don't need, and actually know when a node goes quiet instead of finding out days later. checks reachability, dispatches tasks, and tells you which transport rail will get through. pass an action as argument. allowed-tools: - read - bash - grep - glob - edit - agent - webfetch --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-hive ` > steps: rails → status → ping → dispatch → test → doctor → debug-node # iris hive — compute mesh management manage multi-node hive compute mesh. dispatch tasks across machines, send notifications, debug daemon issues, and run health checks. ## use cases concrete scenarios, mapped to the actions below. | i want to… | run | note | |---|---|---| | kick off a build/job on my other machine, keep working here | `iris playbook run iris-hive dispatch --node <id> --prompt "npm run build"` | serial only — don't fan out to two nodes at once | | know the instant a remote job finishes | `iris playbook run iris-hive ping --node <id>` | `message` type — the one reliable, no-subprocess path | | sanity-check the whole mesh before relying on it | `iris playbook run iris-hive status` | every node + this machine's daemon, one call | | a node won't take tasks / looks stuck | `iris playbook run iris-hive debug --node <id>`, then `doctor` | `debug` = one node's detail; `doctor` = whole-daemon diagnostic | | move a file, a db dump, or a directory between machines | **don't** dispatch it — see rail picker below | rail 1 can't carry bytes faithfully; use tailscale (`scp`/`rsync`) instead | | prove the mesh survived a deploy, not just "looks fine" | `iris playbook run iris-hive test` | the real cross-network playwright e2e suite | | figure out which network path will actually work right now | `iris playbook run iris-hive rails --node <hostname-or-ip>` | probes cloud / lan / tailnet live instead of assuming | ## quick reference ## rail picker — which transport to use full measured writeup: (2026-08-23). hive can reach another machine three different ways. they are not interchangeable — pick the rail from what you're moving, not from what the command is called. | rail | reach | carries | status | |---|---|---|---| | **1 · cloud** (`iris hive dispatch`, `iris hive ping`) | any network, crosses nat, no open ports | task control only — pty pane scrape, not real stdout | native, but serial only (parallelism is 1 regardless of what the node advertises) | | **2 · lan mesh** (mdns `_iris-hive._tcp`, daemon `:3200`) | same lan, in theory | nothing today | native but unreachable — daemon binds `127.0.0.1` while the advert names a routable host (`daemon/index.js:1624`, `#182079`) | | **3 · tailscale** (`ssh`/`scp`/`rsync`/`rdp` over the 100.x tailnet ip) | any network | any protocol, byte-exact | works, but it's borrowed — not hive's own transport | **rules that follow from the measurements:** - never parallelise hive dispatch — fan-out loses every task but one. - never trust hive dispatch output byte-for-byte — it's a tmux pane scrape (merged stdout/stderr, ansi escapes, the wrapper's own command line included), not real stdout. use it for exit-shaped questions and short status; for anything structured, write to a file on the node and carry the file over tailscale (rail 3). - verify any file moved over tailscale with a digest on both ends — sizes can match when contents don't. - treat an empty `ssh` read as unknown, not empty, if the path is inside a tcc-protected app container — `sshd` is denied those paths and returns empty rather than denied. re-read through the daemon (rail 1, gui-session ambient authority) before concluding a directory is empty.

entries.name: iris-hive-start
entries.describe: IRIS Hive — from nothing to a working node
entries.haystack: iris-hive-start iris hive — from nothing to a working node <!-- auto-generated by iris playbook sync — do not edit --> --- name: iris-hive-start description: turn a second machine you already own into compute you can actually use — from nothing, in one sitting. find it, authorise it, prove the transport really carries bytes, and get one real command to run on it. the nothing→working path; `iris-hive` is the playbook for after this one. --- > run this playbook: `iris playbook run iris-hive-start <node>` > steps: account → find → add → online → prove → first → bytes # iris hive — from nothing to a working node **what it is:** a way to run work on machines **you already own** — the laptop in the other room, the box at the office — from wherever you are, without opening a port or paying for a vm. **what it is not:** - **not a cluster scheduler.** no fan-out. dispatch is **serial per node** — one task in flight, regardless of the `2/3` concurrency the node advertises. parallelising loses tasks. - **not remote access to machines you do not control.** every path needs a credential you already have: your iris login on the box, or ssh key auth you already installed. - **not a file transfer.** `iris hive run` returns a **tmux pane scrape**, not real stdout. bytes move on a different rail — see the last step. ## the state everyone misreads: registered ≠ online ≠ usable registered ──daemon starts──> online ──selftest passes──> usable (a row in (heartbeat (the transport actually your account) seconds ago) carries output) `iris hive nodes list` shows **online**. online means a heartbeat arrived. it says nothing about whether a dispatched task runs, runs *there*, or returns anything readable. that gap is why `iris hive selftest` exists, and its own source says why: *"#182004 sat broken while the node reported online, 147 tasks completed, heartbeat 5s."* **`online` is where most people stop, and it is one step short of the thing they wanted.** ## two directions, and one prerequisite hive connect run it on the machine. needs egress only. no ssh, no vpn, no ports. hive enroll <t> run it from here. needs a routable address + ssh key auth. `connect` works behind nat, cgnat, corporate wifi and on a laptop that changes networks; `enroll` cannot onboard a machine you cannot already reach. **prefer `connect`.** the prerequisite either way: **you are logged in** (`iris auth whoami`) and the target logs in **as the same account**. nodes belong to an account, not a person or a network — one registered under a second login is invisible here, and looks identical to one that failed to register. ## steps
